records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
test: fix wallet_pruning.py dropping its peer on a busy machine

mine_large_blocks() moved every node's mock time forward 10 minutes per
1 MB block. A node times out a block download by its own clock (15
minutes with one peer), so when the pruning node was still downloading a
block across two of those jumps, it disconnected its only peer and the
test failed in sync_blocks ("Timeout downloading block ... disconnecting"
in node1's debug.log). Seen once in a parallel run with other heavy tests.

Blocks still advance 10 minutes each, but the nodes' clocks now move once
per 6 blocks (nodes accept blocks up to 2 hours ahead), after the nodes
have synced, so no download is in flight when a clock moves.

records.message:
rpc: publish immutable chain and mempool snapshots

Read RPCs need a coherent generation without taking chain or mempool locks.
Publish chain metadata and an immutable entry tree using ABC's existing
copy-on-write RadixTree. Mutation hooks capture changed entry values; lazy
vectors enumerate only their pinned tree, even after the live pool changes.
Coalesce nested removal/trim/expiry scopes, publish fee/freeze changes, and
avoid publication for no-op prioritisation or unbroadcast updates.

Retain only the current atomic snapshot pointer; readers own older generations.
Atomic shared_ptr and RCU synchronization are not claimed to be wait-free.
Chain index updates and lazy vector construction remain linear where stated.
Mining assembly, RPC consumers, batch submission and their native fixtures
belong to their own feature patches. V2 monetary/state-template fields and
future fee-hysteresis policy are not prerequisites of this eCash foundation.

Native regressions retain historical snapshots across insertion, fee changes,
unbroadcast updates and clearing; verify readers avoid chain/pool locks and
batch removal publishes once. Compact-block reference counts still use exact
equality and now identify the additional immutable transaction owner.

records.subject: primitives: add GlobalConcurrentSlabAllocator and wire MakeTransactionRef to slab arena
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
primitives: add GlobalConcurrentSlabAllocator and wire MakeTransactionRef to slab arena

MakeTransactionRef used std::make_shared, so every transaction received
over P2P/RPC or read from disk went through the global heap. Unlike
mapTx or BlockMap, CTransactionRefs are created and released on
different threads, so the single-threaded ChunkedSlabAllocator cannot
be used.

Add GlobalConcurrentSlabAllocator to chunked_slab.h (existing
definitions unchanged). It is stateless and backed by a per-slot-class
ConcurrentSlabPool: a mutex-guarded SlabArena constructed in static
storage and never destroyed, so references released during static
destruction remain safe. Each thread caches up to 64 free slots in a
trivially destructible thread_local magazine; allocate(1) and
deallocate(p, 1) touch only that magazine on the fast path (no locks,
no atomics) and refill/flush 32 slots at a time under the pool mutex.
Slots may be freed on any thread. A thread_local retirer flushes the
magazine at thread exit and marks it retired, after which frees on that
thread go directly to the pool.

The shared_ptr reference count itself remains atomic.

MakeTransactionRef now uses std::allocate_shared with this allocator,
placing the control block and CTransaction in one slab slot.

Transactions deserialized into a CTransactionRef (P2P tx messages, block
vtx, txindex/disk reads) bypassed MakeTransactionRef: the generic
shared_ptr<const T> Unserialize in serialize.h called std::make_shared.
It now takes its allocator from a SharedPtrDeserializeAllocator<T> trait
(std::allocator by default, so other types are unchanged), which
transaction.h specializes for CTransaction. A trait is used rather than
an Unserialize overload because streams call the qualified
::Unserialize, so an overload would only be found in translation units
that happen to include transaction.h before streams.h.

Tests: direct allocator test (cross-thread free, slot accounting back
to zero after thread exit, chunk reuse, free after magazine retirement)
an 8-producer/4-consumer MakeTransactionRef churn test, and
CTransactionRef deserialization singly and as a block-style vector.

records.subject: primitives: store each CTransaction in one allocation
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
primitives: store each CTransaction in one allocation

A CTransaction held std::vectors of inputs and outputs, each a heap
allocation, and every script longer than CScript's inline capacity was
another. Now the inputs, the outputs and those scripts' bytes share a
single allocation, and a CTransactionRef places it directly after the
shared_ptr control block, so a transaction and its reference count are one
contiguous slab slot:

  [ control block + CTransaction | CTxIn[] | CTxOut[] | long scripts ]

Existing code keeps reading tx.vin[i].prevout, .scriptSig and so on: the
inputs and outputs are real CTxIn/CTxOut objects, and vin/vout are spans
over them.

- prevector gains a borrowed mode (indirect with capacity 0) that never
  frees or reallocates the viewed elements; copies own their elements and
  growing takes a private copy. Long scripts borrow their bytes from the
  transaction's storage. Borrowed scripts only exist as const objects
  inside a CTransaction, so they are never modified in place.
- Deserialization reads the transaction's bytes into a per-thread scratch
  buffer, checking the structure with the same ReadCompactSize calls as
  CMutableTransaction, then allocates exactly once. Both reject the same
  truncated, trailing and non-canonical inputs. The hash is computed from
  those bytes, which are not kept; the serialized size is cached for
  GetTotalSize() and SizeComputer. Serialize() writes the fields as
  SerializeTransaction does, into a per-thread buffer of exactly that
  size, and hands the stream a single write: relaying block 413567's
  transactions takes about 53 ns each instead of 127 ns with field-by-field
  stream writes.
- Storage comes from thread-safe slabs in 128-byte size classes up to
  2 KiB, then up to 4 KiB; larger transactions use the heap.
- MakeTransactionRef builds through a TransactionRefAllocator that reserves
  the storage after the control block, and shared_ptr deserialization goes
  through a SharedPtrDeserializer hook so that block and P2P transactions
  take the same path.
- CTxIn places nSequence directly after prevout, filling its tail padding
  (80 to 72 bytes on LP64). Serialization still writes prevout, scriptSig,
  nSequence, so no serialized bytes change.

Block 413567 now needs 23 heap allocations instead of 8005, and a typical
transaction none. Its mempool memory accounting drops from 1.75 MB to
1.56 MB.

Integration adaptations: retain shared ABC consensus; adapt Chronik bridge input/output views to immutable spans.

records.subject: primitives: build transactions from contiguous streams in place
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
primitives: build transactions from contiguous streams in place

Every deserialized CTransaction first copied its bytes into a per-thread
scratch buffer, then copied them again into its own storage. When the
stream already holds its unread bytes in one buffer, as DataStream does for
P2P messages and SpanReader does for in-memory blocks, the first copy is
unnecessary.

For such streams, ScanTransactionWire checks the transaction's structure
where it lies, with the same ReadCompactSize calls and limits as
ReadTransactionWire, and the transaction is built from those bytes. The
stream is advanced only after the transaction has been built, because
DataStream::ignore releases its buffer when it reaches the end. Other
streams (files, hashing readers) keep the scratch-buffer path.

SpanReader gains data() and ignore(), matching DataStream, so it takes
this path as well.

Block 413567 deserializes about 6% faster with software SHA-256 (about
150 us of 2.5 ms per block); the saving does not depend on hashing.

Tests: SpanReader, DataStream and a read-only stream accept and reject
the same truncated, trailing, non-canonical and oversized inputs as
CMutableTransaction; contiguous streams leave the scratch buffer
untouched, consume exactly the transaction, and the result does not
refer to the stream's bytes.

crypto: add ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions to the SHA-256 implementations

On arm64 SHA256AutoDetect only had the portable implementation, so every
hash on Apple silicon and ARM servers (transaction ids, merkle roots,
sighash midstates) ran in software.

src/crypto/sha256_arm_shani.cpp from bitcoin/bitcoin
924f4c4ac78b0cd3b917c694f42c0651a6f3003a (originally added by Pavol

the compiler supports the instructions (-march=armv8-a+crypto), and
selected at runtime when the CPU reports them: AT_HWCAP/AT_HWCAP2 on Linux,
hw.optional.arm.FEAT_SHA256 on macOS. The existing self-test checks it
before use.

records.subject: depends: build OpenSSL 3.5.9 LTS instead of end-of-life 1.1.1t
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
depends: build OpenSSL 3.5.9 LTS instead of end-of-life 1.1.1t

The node terminates TLS itself (wss:// P2P, TLS on the RPC and
-publicbind listeners, its own OpenSSL session layer, the browser-like
client profile and generated, live-reloaded certificates), and release
builds link depends' OpenSSL. That was 1.1.1t, out of support since
September 2023. It also cannot do what the TLS code asks for: no
X25519MLKEM768 key exchange (OpenSSL >= 3.5), which the client profile
offers first, and no QUIC TLS API, which the planned ngtcp2 QUIC
transport needs.

OpenSSL 3.5.9 (2026-09-29) is the newest 3.5 LTS release, supported
until April 2030. The SHA-256 above was computed here and matches the
.sha256 files on openssl.org and on the GitHub release. The tarball's
PGP signature verifies with the OpenSSL release key
C46ED3F2CBEFDA1FDAADA44264ED7B1DCCE71CB2. The download comes from the
GitHub release, which stays at a fixed URL; openssl.org/source moves
older releases away.

Configure options, still static libcrypto and libssl only:
- Dropped no-ssl2 and no-heartbeats, which 3.x accepts but ignores.
  no-dtls1 becomes no-dtls.
- Dropped no-sock for x86_64-darwin and mingw. It hides SSL_set_fd,
  which the TLS byte layer and the HTTP server bind sessions with, so the
  node could not compile for those hosts against the old recipe.
- Added 3.x options: no-apps, no-docs, no-module (providers built in),
  no-legacy, no-winstore, and no-autoload-config. The last one stops
  libssl from reading an openssl.cnf under the depends prefix path baked
  in at build time on users' machines.
- Disabled more protocols and algorithms the node does not use: CMP,
  CMS, CT, OCSP, SRP, SRTP, TS, ARIA, SM2/3/4 and RC2. no-quic drops only
  OpenSSL's own QUIC stack; the QUIC TLS API ngtcp2 uses is built anyway.
  ML-KEM stays on.
- --libdir=lib, since 3.x installs into lib64 on x86_64 Linux. Staging
  uses DESTDIR rather than editing INSTALLTOP. Empty engine/module
  directories and the CMake package files are removed: the build finds
  OpenSSL through FindOpenSSL.

The build-date blanking in mkbuildinf.pl still applies. As before, the
depends prefix is embedded as OPENSSLDIR/ENGINESDIR (and now
MODULESDIR); Guix builds use fixed paths.

Evidence:
- aarch64-apple-darwin: depends build (1m44s) gives libcrypto.a,
  libssl.a, headers and pkg-config files only. A TLS smoke program
  linked against it negotiates TLS 1.3 with X25519MLKEM768 and ALPN
  http/1.1 over a non-blocking socket pair. Against 1.1.1t from the old

records.message:
http: replace libevent evhttp with Boost.Beast HTTP/1.1 + async_detect_ssl + zstd server

The RPC/REST HTTP server now runs on Boost.Beast over a Boost.Asio
io_context (-rpciothreads, default 2) instead of libevent's evhttp.
Handlers still run on the existing -rpcthreads work queue with the same
-rpcworkqueue admission limit, and the public httpserver.h API
(HTTPRequest, RegisterHTTPHandler, HTTPEvent, EventBase) is unchanged for
callers: httprpc.cpp and rest.cpp need no changes.

Each accepted connection is classified with beast::async_detect_ssl, so
one port serves both plain http:// and TLS https://. TLS uses
-tlscert/-tlskey, or (default -tlsephemeral=1) a self-signed EC P-256
certificate generated once in <datadir>/node_tls_{cert,key}.pem.
-tlsmutual=1 requests, without requiring, client certificates and exposes
their SHA-256 fingerprint via HTTPRequest::GetClientCertFingerprint().

Replies of at least 512 bytes are sent with Content-Encoding: zstd (level
1) when the request's Accept-Encoding lists zstd, and request bodies with
Content-Encoding: zstd are decompressed (bounded by the body limit).

Behaviour kept from evhttp: keep-alive/Connection handling, 400 on
oversized headers, the ACL check, the -rpcservertimeout idle timeout,
default Content-Type, HEAD without body, and libevent's query-string
semantics (now parsed without libevent, including RFC 3986 validation).
libevent remains linked for torcontrol and bitcoin-cli.

Build: OpenSSL and zstd are now required for the server library; a
FindZstd module and a depends zstd package (static libzstd) are added.

Integration adaptation relative to HTTP/WS series-20261019/0001: retain the independently reviewable preceding asynchronous RPC coroutine dispatcher; replace evhttp connection keys with monotonic Beast connection IDs, preserve bounded suspended-request accounting, and remove the obsolete HTTPClosure adapter. records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
build: require OpenSSL 3.0 and compile against the OpenSSL that was found

find_package(OpenSSL 1.1.1) let the node build against an end-of-life
OpenSSL it no longer compiles with. OpenSSL 1.1.1's public sha.h
defines a U64(C) macro, which breaks LogField::U64() in logging/event.h
in every translation unit that includes OpenSSL before logging.h
(httpserver.cpp, net_websocket_tls.cpp).

Require 3.0, the oldest API the TLS code uses (upstream no longer
supports 3.0 either, but Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 and RHEL 9 ship
patched 3.0.x as their system OpenSSL). Release builds use depends'
3.5 LTS. The one feature that needs 3.5, the X25519MLKEM768 hybrid key
exchange, is already detected at run time with a fallback to X25519. A
configure warning now says so when OpenSSL is older than 3.5. Raising
the minimum to 3.5 would break building with those distributions'
OpenSSL for no code reason. The planned QUIC transport can require 3.5
for itself when it lands.

Search the found OpenSSL's headers ahead of other dependencies' include
directories. Homebrew links one OpenSSL's headers (now 4.0.3) into
/opt/homebrew/include, which Boost and others add as -isystem before
OpenSSL's own directory. A macOS build pointed at another OpenSSL with
OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR therefore compiled against Homebrew's headers and
linked the other OpenSSL's libraries. Against depends' 1.1.1t that
failed to link (EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_ec_param_enc is a macro in 1.1.1 and a
function in 3.x). Against a same-ABI pair it would have linked silently.
An extra -I cannot fix this: clang drops an -I for a directory that is
also an -isystem.

Evidence (macOS arm64, OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR at depends' 3.5.9 prefix):
- Configure finds 3.5.9.
- Before this change, tls_util.cpp's OpenSSL headers resolved to
  /opt/homebrew/include. After it, all 83 resolve to the depends prefix,
  and no object in the build depends on a Homebrew OpenSSL header.
- bitcoind and test_bitcoin link no OpenSSL dylib and embed "OpenSSL
  3.5.9".
- The base tree against depends' 1.1.1t fails to compile on U64, as
  above.

Not tested: building against a 3.0.x-3.4.x OpenSSL, and Linux or Windows
builds of the node.

http: delegate /chronik/* and /chronik/ws on main RPC port to Chronik server

With -chronik, the RPC port now also serves Chronik under /chronik
(-chronikpubliconrpcport, default 1), so a single port can carry JSON-RPC,
REST and Chronik over plain HTTP or TLS:

- HTTP requests to /chronik/<path> are forwarded asynchronously, on the
  I/O threads, to Chronik's own listener (the first -chronikbind address,
  via loopback for wildcard binds, default port BaseParams().ChronikPort()).
  Hop-by-hop headers are dropped, X-Forwarded-For/-Proto are added, a
  keep-alive upstream connection is reused per client connection, and the
  reply gets the usual zstd Content-Encoding when the client accepts it.
- WebSocket upgrades to /chronik/ws are accepted locally and bridged
  message-for-message (text/binary preserved) to Chronik's /ws.

RegisterPublicHTTPPrefix() exempts such paths from the -rpcallowip
address check; they perform no RPC authentication. JSON-RPC and
/wallet/ keep the ACL and Basic auth. Builds without Chronik, -chronik=0
or -chronikpubliconrpcport=0 return 404 for /chronik.

The new chronik_rpc_port_proxy.py test checks byte-identical replies
against the Chronik port, error passthrough, https, zstd, ws:// and wss://
subscriptions, and the opt-out.

records.subject: net: add WebSocket P2P transport (/p2p/ws) with streaming zstd and prebaked P2P dictionary
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: add WebSocket P2P transport (/p2p/ws) with streaming zstd and prebaked P2P dictionary

P2P peers can now connect to the RPC/HTTP port at /p2p/ws, over ws:// or
wss:// (TLS is detected per connection as for HTTP), alongside the
unchanged raw TCP P2P listener. -p2pwebsocket (default 1, requires
-listen) enables it; /p2p/ws is exempt from -rpcallowip.

The P2P wire format is unchanged: the normal 24-byte-header messages are
carried in binary WebSocket messages. After the upgrade a socketpair is
created; CConnman::AcceptWebSocketPeer() receives one end and treats it
like an accepted TCP socket (same limits, bans and eviction, peer address
from the TCP connection, or from X-Forwarded-For behind a local proxy with
-p2pwebsockettrustforwardedfor), while the HTTP I/O threads pump the other
end to/from the WebSocket. V1Transport, CNode and net_processing are
untouched.

Compression is negotiated with Sec-WebSocket-Protocol:
- p2p-zstd-v1: one zstd stream per direction, flushed (ZSTD_e_flush) per
  WebSocket message so each decodes immediately while the 128 KiB window
  stays warm across messages, primed with the 9586-byte P2P_ZSTD_DICT_V1
  raw-content dictionary (message headers for all networks, inv/getdata
  entries, tx/script templates incl. CashTokens and Lotus V2 Taproot
  patterns). The dictionary is generated deterministically by
  contrib/devtools/gen-p2p-zstd-dict.py and pinned by a unit test.
- p2p-zstd: the same without the dictionary.
- otherwise RFC 7692 permessage-deflate if offered, else plain.
Decoder windows are capped at 1 MiB.

getpeerinfo reports "transport" (tcp/ws/wss) and, for WebSocket peers,
the compression and payload vs. wire byte counts; getnettotals reports
node-wide WebSocket totals.

Tests: zstd session unit tests (round trips, warm window, dictionary
benefit, corrupt input, negotiation) and p2p_websocket_inbound.py, which
handshakes with an independent python-zstandard peer for every
sub-protocol over ws:// and wss://.

Integration adaptation relative to HTTP/WS series-20261019/0003: retain coroutine shutdown/handler APIs. Keep the existing inbound-WebSocket local-address safety fix and its 21-line regression test here, ahead of source0009, so this intermediate state does not advertise an HTTP listener as a TCP listener.

records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: support outbound wss:// and ws:// domain:port P2P connections and BIP155 ADDRv2 advertisement

Outbound: -addnode, -connect and the addnode RPC accept ws:// and wss://
URLs (e.g. wss://node.example.com:443/p2p/ws; default ports 80/443,
default path /p2p/ws). CConnman::ConnectNode() dispatches them, and
NET_WSS addresses from addrman, to the new ConnectWebSocketNode();
ordinary "ip:port"/"host:port" peers keep using the unchanged TCP path.

The dialer (net_websocket.cpp, its own I/O thread) resolves and connects,
does TLS with SNI (SSL_set_tlsext_host_name) for wss://, sends
Host: <host>:<port> and Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: p2p-zstd-v1, p2p-zstd
(permessage-deflate offered as fallback), and bridges the result to
CConnman over a socketpair with the same pump as inbound /p2p/ws. Peers
are not authenticated by TLS (self-signed certificates are expected);
our certificate is presented to servers using -tlsmutual. It is
registered through SetWebSocketDialer() so net.cpp stays free of
Boost.Beast/OpenSSL for bitcoinkernel.
The debug-only -p2pwebsocketoffer restricts what is offered (for
benchmarking dictionary vs. plain zstd vs. uncompressed).

Addresses: new Network NET_WSS holds a lowercase DNS name (max 253
chars), serialized in ADDRv2 with network id 0x10 ("wss"). It is not
ADDRv1-compatible, so the existing IsAddrCompatible() check relays it
only to peers that sent sendaddrv2; ADDRv2 nodes without this change
ignore the unknown id as BIP155 requires, and malformed names are
ignored rather than treated as errors. Each name is its own netgroup.
-externaldomain=<domain>[:port] (default port 443) adds such a local
address so it is advertised. getnetworkinfo's network list is unchanged.

Tests: NET_WSS/URL unit tests, and p2p_websocket_tls.py: node1 joins
node0 over wss:// with p2p-zstd-v1, node2 over TCP; http/https/zstd RPC
on node0's port; blocks and transactions relay across TCP <-> wss; the
domain is advertised to an ADDRv2 test peer but not to an ADDRv1 one, and
node2 learns it over TCP ADDRv2. The test framework's CAddress learns
network id 0x10.

Re-derived from authoritative HTTP/WS series-20261019/0004, including versioned Lotus-private NET_WSS 0x10 and opaque unknown-version relay. records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
http: move reply bodies into the response instead of copying them

HTTPRequest::WriteReply() took the body by const reference and copied it
into the Beast response; it now takes it by value and moves it, and the
response is moved on to the socket write. Existing callers still compile
unchanged (lvalues are copied as before); the JSON-RPC reply and the REST
block/tx/header/UTXO replies now pass rvalues, so their bodies are never
copied after being generated.

This saves one reply-sized allocation and copy per request (3.35 MB for
getblock verbosity 2 of a 1000-transaction block). Throughput on that
workload is unchanged within run-to-run noise, as JSON generation
dominates; the benefit is lower peak memory under concurrent large
replies.

records.subject: http: cut per-request I/O overhead (write fast path, one idle timer)
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
http: cut per-request I/O overhead (write fast path, one idle timer)

Single-connection RPC latency was 15-40 us higher than with evhttp
(e.g. a 50-call batch: 150 vs 111 us p50). Per-stage timing showed the
Beast path spending ~13 us writing a 0.7 KB reply and re-arming stream
timers on every read and write.

- WriteResponse(): on plain TCP, write directly while the non-blocking
  socket accepts data, and fall back to async_write (continuing the same
  serializer) only if it would block. Most replies now cost one writev
  and no trip through the I/O scheduler; large replies and slow clients
  still take the async path, so I/O threads never block.
- -rpcservertimeout: replace per-operation tcp_stream expiries with one
  watchdog timer per connection that wakes about once per timeout and
  shuts the socket down if the connection made no progress for that long
  while no handler (or WebSocket session) was running. Semantics are
  unchanged: idle and keep-alive connections close after the timeout,
  long-polling handlers and /p2p/ws sessions are not cut off.

c=1 p50 after (macOS arm64, loaded host): batch 130 us vs evhttp
113-119 us (was ~40 us behind), getblockcount 48-51 us vs 36-40 us (was
~20 us behind). The remaining gap is the two cross-thread handoffs.
Concurrent throughput is unchanged or better.

records.subject: net: never self-advertise a WebSocket port as a TCP P2P address
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: never self-advertise a WebSocket port as a TCP P2P address

GetLocalAddrForPeer() may adopt the address a peer reports seeing us at.
For inbound peers ABC takes that report's port too, since such a peer
reached our listening port. An inbound /p2p/ws peer, however, reached the
HTTP/WebSocket endpoint (-publicbind or the RPC port), so with a routable
address we could advertise IP:<websocket port> as a plain TCP P2P address
and third parties would try P2P against the HTTP server.

For WebSocket peers, take only the reported IP and keep our P2P port, as
for outbound peers. Likewise, if the best local address is the
-externaldomain NET_WSS entry, never pair its wss:// port with an IP.
WebSocket reachability is advertised only through -externaldomain
(NET_WSS over ADDRv2).

The extended get_local_addr_for_peer_port test fails without this change.

records.message:
net: fail closed when a WebSocket dial would bypass -proxy

The WebSocket dialer resolves names and connects directly. With -proxy

also refuse them when -onlynet excludes the wss network.

are refused without touching the proxy or the target, that -onlynet
without wss refuses them, and that they work otherwise.

records.subject: net: let Sock implementations buffer data in user space
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: let Sock implementations buffer data in user space

A socket implementation that decodes or decrypts in user space (TLS,
WebSocket framing) can hold received bytes that poll() cannot see, and can
accept data from Send() that it has not written yet. Add three Sock hooks,
with defaults describing a plain socket:

- HasBufferedRecv(): Recv() can return data now. CConnman then polls with
  a zero timeout and treats the socket as readable.
- PendingEvents(): OS socket events needed to flush data accepted by
  Send() (a TLS write can need RECV). CConnman polls for them even when it
  has nothing queued itself.
- FlushPending(): called when one of those events occurs; failure
  disconnects the peer.

Receiving still honours fPauseRecv when RECV was only polled on behalf of
a pending flush. Plain sockets behave exactly as before.

records.subject: net: add WebSocketSock, a WebSocket-framed P2P socket for CConnman
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: add WebSocketSock, a WebSocket-framed P2P socket for CConnman

Groundwork for carrying /p2p/ws peers on the real TCP socket instead of
the socketpair bridge (an extra thread hop per side and direction, about
77 us per round trip on loopback). Not used yet.

- WebSocketCodec: RFC 6455 framing without I/O. Each P2P chunk becomes one
  binary message, zstd-compressed per the negotiated mode (p2p-zstd-v1,
  p2p-zstd, none) using P2PZstdSession. Decoding handles fragmentation,
  answers pings and closes, and rejects text frames, reserved bits and
  opcodes, wrong masking for the role, fragmented or long control frames,
  frames or messages over 64 MiB (checked from the header, before
  buffering), corrupt zstd and decompression beyond the same limit.
- WebSocketSock: a Sock CConnman polls directly. Send() frames and
  compresses on the calling thread, coalescing MSG_MORE chunks into one
  message, accepts what it is given unless more than 4 MiB is already
  waiting (then EAGAIN), and leaves the unwritten tail to the Sock
  PendingEvents()/FlushPending() hooks. Recv() deframes and decompresses;
  decoded bytes not yet returned, EOF and errors are reported through
  HasBufferedRecv(). The socket is made non-blocking (MSG_DONTWAIT may be
  defined as 0) and SIGPIPE-safe. A pluggable byte layer (plain here)
  lets TLS reuse the framing.

Unit tests cover every frame-length class in all compression modes in
both directions (incl. 3 MB payloads), MSG_MORE coalescing, buffered-data
signalling, fragmented messages with an interleaved ping, close handling,
each protocol violation, EOF mid-frame, corrupt zstd and back-pressure.
A websocket_codec fuzz target checks arbitrary input and encode/decode
round trips across arbitrary splits.

records.message:
net: add a TLS byte layer for WebSocketSock (OpenSSL on the socket, kTLS)

asio's ssl_stream keeps the TLS session in its own memory BIOs, so it
cannot be handed to CConnman. TlsByteLayer instead drives an OpenSSL
session bound to the socket itself (SSL_set_fd), non-blocking, under
WebSocketSock's framing:

- SSL_ERROR_WANT_READ/WANT_WRITE map to EAGAIN; the event a blocked write
  waits for (RECV for e.g. a TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate) is reported through
  PendingEvents(), and SSL_pending() through HasBufferedRecv().
- close_notify reads as EOF; destruction sends one non-blocking
  close_notify after the WebSocket Close.

New tls_util module shared with the HTTP server: TLS 1.2+ contexts for
caller-owned non-blocking sockets (partial writes, moving write buffers,
no compression or renegotiation, SSL_OP_ENABLE_KTLS where available, so
on Linux OpenSSL can offload records to the kernel), PEM loading,
self-signed certificate generation (moved from httpserver.cpp, unchanged
output), SPKI and certificate fingerprints.

Tests: a real handshake over a socketpair, then round trips of up to 3 MB
both ways with and without compression, a TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate mid-stream,
orderly close (Close + close_notify reads as EOF) and SPKI fingerprints.
Not used by the node yet.

records.subject: net: dial ws:// and wss:// peers directly into CConnman, through -proxy
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: dial ws:// and wss:// peers directly into CConnman, through -proxy

Outbound WebSocket peers no longer go through a socketpair bridge or the
dialer's own I/O thread, and they honour the proxy configuration:

- CConnman::ConnectWebSocketNode opens the TCP connection exactly as for
  TCP peers: ConnectThroughProxy() with the host name (the proxy resolves
  it; no local DNS lookup) when -proxy applies, the -onion proxy for
  .onion hosts, otherwise every resolved address in turn via
  ConnectDirectly(). A failed proxy never falls back to a direct
  connection, and -onlynet must include wss (onion for .onion). This
  replaces the previous refusal of WebSocket dials under -proxy.
- The dialer hook (net_websocket.cpp) then performs, synchronously on that
  socket with a 20 s deadline: TLS for wss:// with OpenSSL on the socket
  (SNI for names), and the RFC 6455 upgrade written by hand (random
  Sec-WebSocket-Key, Sec-WebSocket-Accept verified, the selected
  sub-protocol must be one we offered, extensions refused). The result is
  a WebSocketSock that CNode uses directly; leftover bytes after the 101
  response are kept.
- permessage-deflate is no longer offered outbound (node-to-node uses
  zstd); it remains accepted from inbound generic clients. The default
  -p2pwebsocketoffer is now "p2p-zstd-v1,p2p-zstd".

p2p_websocket_proxy.py uses a forwarding SOCKS5 proxy: wss:// and ws://
peers connect through it with the host name in the CONNECT request, a
dead proxy leaves no direct connection, -onlynet without wss refuses the
dial, and without a proxy the dial is direct.

records.subject: http: terminate TLS with our own OpenSSL session instead of asio's ssl_stream
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
http: terminate TLS with our own OpenSSL session instead of asio's ssl_stream

asio's ssl::stream keeps the TLS session in its own memory BIOs, so an
upgraded connection cannot be handed elsewhere with its session. The HTTP
server now owns the TLS session itself; Beast still does all HTTP and
WebSocket parsing and serialization on top:

- TLS is detected from the first byte (0x16) peeked with MSG_PEEK, so no
  bytes are consumed; an SSL is created from the tls_util context and bound
  to the socket with SSL_set_fd.
- OsslStream is an asio AsyncStream (and non-blocking SyncWriteStream) over
  that SSL: WANT_READ/WANT_WRITE wait with async_wait, immediate results
  are re-posted (never completed inline from initiation), multi-buffer
  writes (HTTP header + body) are gathered into one SSL_write so a reply is
  one TLS record and syscall, and a write OpenSSL asked to retry is retried
  with the same length. Beast WebSocket teardown is provided for it.
- WriteResponse's non-blocking write fast path now covers TLS too.
- Until the TLS handshake completes, a deadline (-rpcservertimeout) shuts
  the socket down, so silent or stalled clients are dropped.
- -tlscert/-tlskey/-tlsephemeral and -tlsmutual behave as before;
  boost/asio/ssl is no longer used by the server.

Measured on loopback (16 RPC threads): small RPCs over TLS 45-67k req/s
at c=16/64 (plain 60-72k) and equal c=1 latency; 3.35 MB getblock replies
over TLS within noise of plain. A unit test covers handshake, reads,
gathered writes through would_block and async retry, and close_notify.

records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
http: hand /p2p/ws connections to CConnman without a bridge

After Beast accepts a /p2p/ws upgrade negotiating p2p-zstd-v1, p2p-zstd
or no compression, the HTTP server now hands the connection itself to the
P2P layer: the TCP socket, our TLS session (wss://), and any bytes the
client sent after the upgrade request become a WebSocketSock that CConnman
polls directly. The connection leaves the HTTP server's tracking, so
stopping the HTTP server never closes P2P sockets, and P2P data no longer
crosses the HTTP I/O threads or a socketpair.

The socketpair bridge remains only for clients that negotiate RFC 7692
permessage-deflate (generic WebSocket clients) and behind the new debug
option -p2pwebsocketbridge; on platforms without local sockets
(Windows) permessage-deflate is declined and the direct path is used.

Loopback median P2P ping round trip, 3 runs (TCP 110-118 us):
  ws://, no compression   112-123 us   (was +77 us over TCP via bridge)
  ws://, p2p-zstd-v1      130-138 us
  wss://, p2p-zstd-v1     156-169 us   (bridge: 220-226 us)
The remaining difference to TCP is zstd per message and TLS.

p2p_websocket_inbound.py also covers the debug bridge; its WebSocket
client helper treats the node's Close frame as end of stream.

Integration adaptation relative to HTTP/WS series-20261019/0016: use the existing HTTPConnectionInfo::connection_id for handoff deregistration and coroutine dispatch rather than adding a second conn_id field. Reuse the existing public_only field; socket ownership and all source handoff behavior remain unchanged.

does for globals, which silences the thread-safety negative-capability

records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
http: real client addresses behind load balancers, and health endpoints

Nodes run behind one or more balancer layers (e.g. AWS NLB and ALB in a
VPC, or OVH vRack) see the balancers' addresses, so -rpcallowip, bans,
eviction and addrman saw the wrong peers. -trustedproxy=<ip|subnet>
(repeatable) names balancers whose client information is believed:

- a PROXY protocol v1 or v2 header at the start of the connection, read
  exactly so TLS or HTTP behind it is still detected (LOCAL/UNKNOWN keep
  the balancer's own address, e.g. for its health checks);
- X-Forwarded-For on each request, walked from the right while hops are
  trusted. The first untrusted address is the client, so what a client
  writes into the header itself is never believed.

The resolved address is used for -rpcallowip, P2P WebSocket peers, logs
and the X-Forwarded-For sent to Chronik (which no longer passes on a
client's own header). -p2pwebsockettrustforwardedfor becomes shorthand
for trusting loopback.

/livez (the server runs), /readyz and /healthz (out of initial block
download, with peers; else 503 and the reason as JSON) serve health
checks on every listener. -httphealth turns them off; they are off by
default with -p2pwebsockettoken or -publicfallback, where they would
reveal a bridge to probes.

records.subject: net: dial outbound connections without stalling the others
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: dial outbound connections without stalling the others

Outbound connections were opened synchronously by the thread wanting
them (automatic outbound, -addnode, -connect, addconnection). A wss://
peer takes a TCP connect, a TLS handshake and an HTTP upgrade (up to 5 s
plus 20 s), so one slow or unresponsive peer held up every connection
after it.

Each outbound attempt now runs on a thread of its own, and the finished
node is registered as before. While it is in progress it counts as a
connection: it keeps its outbound slot (the semaphore grant moves with
it), its connection type, address and address group are counted when
choosing what to open next, and the same address or name is not dialed
twice. It stops counting only once the node is registered (or failed),
so there is no window in which a peer is neither. Shutdown interrupts
attempts in flight and joins them before nodes are cleaned up.

addconnection now returns once the attempt has started.

records.subject: net: resume a TLS read that is waiting to write
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: resume a TLS read that is waiting to write

A TLS read can need to write before it can return data, for example
when the TLS library sends a reply from inside SSL_read and the send
buffer is full. TlsByteLayer reported that as a plain EAGAIN, and the
socket loop then waited only for readability. The data the read needs
may already have been read from the OS socket, so readability might
never come: the peer then stalled until something else happened on the
connection.

TlsByteLayer now records which OS event a blocked read is waiting for
(ReadWaitsFor()). WebSocketSock reports SEND among its PendingEvents()
while a read waits for writability. FlushPending() retries that read
once the socket is writable, and CConnman receives in the same pass when
FlushPending() leaves decoded data behind (HasBufferedRecv()).

OpenSSL 4.0 defers its reply to a TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate to the next write,
so a KeyUpdate under back-pressure does not reach this path there. A
unit test drives it with a byte layer whose reads wait for writability;
without this change, the test's read never resumes. A second test checks
that a KeyUpdate asking for one back still delivers everything, in both
directions, while the server's writes are blocked.

records.subject: net: wake the socket handler instead of waiting out its poll timeout
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: wake the socket handler instead of waiting out its poll timeout

SocketHandler() waits up to 50 ms (SELECT_TIMEOUT_MILLISECONDS) on the
sockets it knew about when the wait began. A peer added meanwhile, a
peer whose receiving resumed, or a send that left data queued all waited
for that timeout before their socket was watched. Each new connection
paid it at least once before its handshake completed.

A new SockWakeup (util/sockwakeup.{h,cpp}) is a non-blocking connected
socket pair: socketpair(2), or loopback TCP where that is unavailable
(Windows). SocketHandler() waits on one end along with the peers, and
drains it before working out what to wait on next. Wake() writes at most
one byte per drain. CConnman wakes the handler when it adds a node
(AddNodeLocked), when a node stops pausing receives (CNode::pauseRecv),
and when an optimistic send leaves data queued or buffered in the socket.
If the pair cannot be created, the node logs a warning and keeps the old
behaviour.

Measured on macOS arm64 (two interleaved rounds of 20 connections per
transport, load average about 34), the median time from connect to
handshake:
- ws: 19.7–36.4 ms -> 0.10–0.35 ms;
- wss: 23.5–36.8 ms -> 0.11–0.42 ms;
on both the server side (accept -> version) and the client side
(added -> verack). These are medians, not worst cases: one loaded run
still had a 38 ms outlier.

Unit tests cover coalesced wakeups, a wakeup from another thread, a
2000-change stress loop that would catch a lost wakeup, and the loopback
pair on every platform. The loopback pair is not yet built or run on
Windows.

logging: keep the log file unbuffered after reopening it

records.subject: logging: optional JSON log lines (-logformat=json)
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
logging: optional JSON log lines (-logformat=json)

Log shippers such as Fluentd and Vector had to parse debug.log with
regexes, and the prefixes it carries depend on several options.
-logformat=json (default text, unchanged) writes each log record as one
JSON object per line:

  {"ts":"2026-10-19T07:41:17.348212Z","level":"debug","category":"net",
   "thread":"msghand","file":"net_processing.cpp","line":3530,
   "msg":"received: feefilter of 10.00 XEC/kB from peer=0"}

ts (RFC 3339, always with microseconds, omitted with -logtimestamps=0),
level, category ("none" for uncategorized messages), thread and source
file/line are always present; func is added with -logsourcelocations;
mocktime appears when mock time is set; continued:true marks a record
that continues one which did not end in a newline; ratelimited:true is
the equivalent of the "[*]" text prefix while rate limiting suppresses
some source location. -logthreadnames, -logtimemicros and
-loglevelalways only shape the text format. Messages are escaped for
JSON (quotes, backslash, control characters and DEL); valid UTF-8 is kept
and each byte that is not part of a valid sequence becomes U+FFFD, so
every line is valid JSON and the output is deterministic.

Only the sink changes: no call site does. The line is built in a buffer
owned by the logger, under the lock it already holds, and reused for the
next line (one over 64 KiB is not kept). Field names, levels and
categories are appended from static strings, the timestamp and line
number are formatted by hand, so a JSON line costs no allocation once
the buffer has grown; the only allocations left are the call site's own
formatting of the message, as in text mode. Rate limiting counts the
JSON line, as it counts the text line. Messages logged before the log
file opens are now buffered raw and escaped for the selected format when
they are written, which leaves the text output unchanged.

Messages shown to the user through the non-GUI message box (init errors
and warnings) are now logged at their severity (error, warning) instead
of info, so that structured logs report them as errors; the text line
gains the usual "[error] " or "[warning] " prefix.

With a no-op sink, formatting a short debug line takes about 240 ns and
no allocation against 600 ns and 3 allocations as text; a 300 byte line
510 ns against 1370 ns (bench: LogText*/LogJson*).

(cherry picked from commit b4d50f7bb6d6b2372789ec750e1a7b13a6a2a16c)

records.subject: metrics: lock-free metrics registry in the Prometheus text format
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
metrics: lock-free metrics registry in the Prometheus text format

A small registry for operator metrics, to be served at /metrics: no new
dependency, and recording that never takes a lock, allocates or makes a
system call, so that it can sit on validation and P2P paths.

- Counter: split into 16 cache-line aligned shards. A thread adds to its
  own shard with a relaxed fetch_add; shards are summed when scraped.
  Eight threads on one counter cost 2.3 ns per add, against 45 ns for a
  single shared atomic (cache-line ping-pong).
- Gauge: one relaxed atomic, set where a value changes.
- EventHistogram: samples (durations) go through a bounded
  single-producer ring per recording thread (6 ns per push). A full ring
  drops the sample and counts it. A drain thread folds the rings into
  fixed buckets every 50 ms. A thread can get its ring when it starts
  (PrepareThisThread); rings of exited threads are drained once more and
  reused, so short-lived threads do not allocate.
- Labels are fixed sets of values, combined row-major; histograms can
  hide series that never had a sample. Collectors run before rendering,
  for values computed at scrape time.
- Render produces the text exposition format 0.0.4 (HELP/TYPE lines,
  escaping, cumulative le buckets, _sum and _count, and
  lotus_metrics_dropped_samples_total), and can reuse a rendering made
  less than a given interval ago.

Benchmarks (bench_bitcoin -filter='Metrics.*') measure the cost of each
kind of record, contended and not, and of the clock.

(cherry picked from commit 423c581e3c357ee7f23883e8372f54480e69861d)

records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
metrics: serve /metrics (-metrics), with HTTP request metrics

-metrics (default off) serves the node's metrics in the Prometheus text
format at /metrics on the RPC listeners. It is an ordinary HTTP handler,
so it gets RPC's access rules: only -rpcallowip clients (the address
resolved through -trustedproxy), never -publicbind listeners. It has no
authentication, as scrapers expect, which is why it is opt-in: an
-rpcallowip opened for authenticated RPC does not start publishing node
state. GET and HEAD only; a rendering is reused for up to a second.

node::NodeMetrics holds the node's registry. It exists only with
-metrics; recording sites check node::GetNodeMetrics(), so disabled
metrics cost a load and a branch. It is never freed, like the logger, so
a pointer taken by a recording thread cannot dangle. The drain thread
starts with the HTTP server and stops after it.

First metrics: HTTP requests answered by endpoint class and status
class, their duration from header to response, and TLS handshakes by
result. interface_http_metrics.py checks the exposition format, these
values, and that clients outside -rpcallowip, public listeners and nodes
without -metrics get no metrics.

metrics: P2P traffic and peers

records.message:
logging: rate limit per call site without a lock or lookup

The quota of unconditional logging per source location was kept in an
unordered_map keyed by std::source_location, behind a mutex: every
rate-limited log line hashed its file name and took that lock, on
whatever thread logged (validation, message handling, network).

Each log macro expansion now owns its quota: a constant-initialized
static (LogSiteLimit) created by the macro itself. Its window, its
suppressed flag and the bytes left are packed in one atomic word, so a
check is a load and a compare-and-swap on that site's own cache line;
concurrent threads on one site let exactly the quota through. A site
over quota pushes itself on its limiter's lock-free list of suppressed
sites, which the periodic reset walks to log the "Restarting logging"
notices, as before. Windows are numbered across limiters, so a site last
used by another limiter (tests) starts afresh.

Semantics are unchanged: a per-location byte quota per window, counted
by message length, the "Excessive logging" notice when a site starts
being suppressed, the "[*]" marker while any is, and a notice of the
dropped bytes when the window resets. The quota is capped at 16 MiB
(the default is 1 MiB).

  and without credentials, 503, 403, 404/500 JSON errors, empty and
  unparsable bodies, a 50 MB body, a silent server (timeout, error
  code 0), a server that trickles bytes slower than the timeout but
  never pauses for longer (inactivity semantics, succeeds), a refused
  port (libevent reports no error code), a server that closes after

records.subject: cli: send RPC requests with Boost.Beast instead of libevent
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
cli: send RPC requests with Boost.Beast instead of libevent

The command line client was the last libevent HTTP client. Replace its
transport with a small Boost.Asio/Beast POST: resolve, connect, write
the request and read the reply with a response parser, all on one
io_context.

The behaviour recorded by interface_bitcoin_cli_http.py is kept:

- the same request line, header set and header order (Host,
  Connection: close, Content-Type, Authorization, Content-Length) and
  body, with the wallet path percent-encoded by urlEncode;
- chunked and connection-delimited bodies, an unlimited body size;
- -rpcclienttimeout limits inactivity, not the whole request: the
  timer is re-armed before connecting, before the write and before
  every socket read, which is why the client reads the socket itself
  and feeds the parser rather than using http::async_read_some (that
  keeps reading until a complete header has arrived). A timeout of 0
  now really means no timeout instead of five years;
- the same error codes and strings: a failed resolve or connect
  reports no code, a timeout code 0, a connection closed before a
  complete reply code 1, a malformed reply code 2;
- the status handling, credential logic and -rpcwait loop are
  unchanged.

One deliberate difference: a host name in -rpcconnect is now tried on
each of its resolved addresses, where libevent gave up after the first
(so "localhost" failed against an IPv4-only server when ::1 resolved
first). The test now expects success.

The client no longer installs a libevent log callback or includes any
libevent header. Its build still links libevent; that goes with the
rest of the libevent removal.

Tier: eCash

records.subject: torcontrol: run the Tor controller on Boost.Asio
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
torcontrol: run the Tor controller on Boost.Asio

The Tor control client was built on libevent bufferevents, an event
base of its own and libevent's thread support. Run it on a Boost.Asio
io_context on the same torcontrol thread instead.

- TorControlConnection reads with async_read_some and splits lines on
  LF, removing one CR before it, as EVBUFFER_EOL_CRLF did. The reply
  parsing, async/sync dispatch and MAX_LINE_LENGTH check are the same
  code; an overlong line still disconnects without the disconnected
  callback, so the controller does not reconnect. Commands queued
  before the connection completes are sent once it does, as with a
  bufferevent.
- A generation counter, incremented by Disconnect(), makes the
  completion of any operation on an older socket a no-op, and stops
  processing buffered lines once a reply handler has disconnected
  (libevent kept reading from the freed buffer).
- The control address is parsed by ParseTorControlAddress, which
  accepts the same numeric forms as evutil_parse_sockaddr_port.
- The reconnect timer is a steady_timer with the same exponential
  backoff; the "out of memory" message for a failed event_new goes.
- InterruptTorControl() stops the io_context, which, like the
  event_base_once loopbreak it replaces, also works before the loop
  has started. evthread_use_* is no longer needed.

TorControlReply, TorControlConnection and the reply parsers are now
declared in torcontrol.h, so torcontrol_tests can drive a connection
against an in-test acceptor: replies split across reads, CRLF and LF
endings, async events, commands queued before connect, a handler that
disconnects, the line-length limit, a refused connection and a host
name. All log messages are unchanged, and feature_torcontrol.py passes
unmodified.

Tier: eCash

records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
test: don't share argument lists between test nodes

setup_nodes() and add_nodes() built per-node lists with `[[]] * n`, so
every node shared one list object, and TestNode.start() appended its
-bind arguments to whatever list it was given:

- Without a bind=... config line (bind_to_localhost_only = False) and
  with default arguments, node 0's -bind arguments ended up in the list
  of every later node.
- Each restart without an explicit bind appended the -bind arguments
  again, to the test's own self.extra_args[i].

Today the bind=127.0.0.1 config line hides the first problem.

Nodes now get their own lists (node_extra_args()), TestNode keeps a copy
of its arguments, and start() computes the arguments it passes on a new
list (start_args()), never modifying the stored or the caller's list.

One existing behaviour is kept on purpose: with noban_tx_relay, the
whitelist argument is still written into the test's own lists, because
tests restart nodes with self.extra_args[i] + [...] and rely on it (e.g.
abc_feature_proof_cleanup.py, abc_p2p_avalanche_cooldown.py,
abc_p2p_getavaaddr.py). It is now stored as new lists per node.

mempool_limit.py and mempool_expiry.py extended self.extra_args[0] and
relied on that list being the node's own; they now pass the arguments
to restart_node() explicitly.

Unit tests for the argument handling run with the test framework's
other unit tests (test_runner.py). The full functional suite gives the
same passed/skipped/failed result for every test as before.

define both run_test and set_test_params in its own class body. That
prevents a test that only changes parameters of another test by
subclassing it, and an intermediate base class shared by several tests.

The metaclass now requires both methods to be provided somewhere below
BitcoinTestFramework (the class itself or one of its bases). A class
meant only to be subclassed sets `abstract = True` in its own body and
is exempt; subclasses don't inherit the exemption.

As before, subclasses may not override __init__ or main. They now also
may not override setup, which no test does.

Every existing test module still imports. Unit tests cover:
- an inheriting subclass;
- an abstract base and its concrete subclass;
- a missing run_test;
- the exemption not being inherited;
- each forbidden override.

The full functional suite gives the same per-test results as before.

records.message:
test: allow running a test from code, and keep its outcome details

A test could only run as a script: BitcoinTestFramework.__init__()
parsed sys.argv and main() always ended with sys.exit(). A test runner
that runs tests in its own worker processes, and reports structured
results, needs both under its control.

  arguments; the default is sys.argv[1:], as before.
- main(exit_process=True): exits as before, or returns the exit code
  when exit_process is False.
- main() keeps the outcome details on the instance:
  - skip_reason: the SkipTest message;
  - failure: type, message and traceback of the exception that failed
    the test.

  Logging is unchanged.

Unit tests run node-less tests in-process that pass, skip and fail, and
check the exit codes and details. The full functional suite gives the
same per-test results as before.

records.subject: test: run a functional test in a worker process with a structured result
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
test: run a functional test in a worker process with a structured result

New test_framework/worker.py:
- run_job() runs one test class in its own process. It leads its own
  process group, sends the test's stdout and stderr (and that of
  anything it starts) to files, runs the class with the job's arguments
  (main(exit_process=False)), and sends a JobResult back over a pipe.
- run_in_process(job, timeout) starts run_job() with multiprocessing's
  "spawn" context and waits for the result.
  - A worker that exits without reporting is "crashed".
  - One still running after the timeout gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL, for
    its whole process group, and is "timeout".
  - After every job, whatever is left in the group (e.g. the nodes of a
    failed test) is killed.

As before, a test that passes but writes to stderr fails.

interface_rpc.py set multiprocessing's start method to "fork" in its
__main__ block, which a worker does not run. It now asks for a "fork"
context itself.

Unit tests run small node-less tests in workers that pass, fail, skip,
write to stderr, crash and hang (stopped by the timeout).
test_runner.py does not use workers yet.

records.message:
test: run discovered functional tests in worker processes

test_runner.py now runs every discovered test in a worker process
(test_framework/worker.py) instead of a plain `python3 <test>`
subprocess, and gets a JobResult back instead of only an exit code and

  and takes the next as soon as it finishes; tests are still ordered
  longest first.

  --test-timeout seconds. The default is 1200, multiplied by the tests'
  --timeout-factor; 0 disables it. Before, a hung test hung the run.

  test) are killed with its process group.
- The test's full stdout and stderr are still printed for a failure. The
  JobResult is kept on each TestResult, for structured output.
- The runner sets SRCDIR, which test modules need to import, for itself
  and the workers.

and leaves no bitcoind running. Accumulated time is unchanged within
noise: -j 12, load average about 30, 353 s wall time.

records.subject: test: give concurrently running tests disjoint port ranges
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
test: give concurrently running tests disjoint port ranges

Each test's port range comes from its --portseed:
PORT_MIN + (64 * seed) % 2935. The runner used the test's position in
the queue as its seed, which wraps after 46 values. So tests 46
positions apart, e.g. a long test started early and one started later,
could be given overlapping ranges while running at the same time. Only
the port-availability check and retry in UniquePort guarded against
that, and that check is racy.

Each runner thread is now a pool slot (0 to jobs-1), and a test uses
its slot as port seed. Tests running at the same time therefore never
share a range. The test directory is still named after the test's
position, so it stays unique.

--jobs is limited to the 45 slots with disjoint ranges, and a higher
value is rejected when the arguments are parsed.

The full functional suite gives the same per-test results as before.

records.subject: test: named test variants, selected with --variant
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
test: named test variants, selected with --variant

Variants replace per-test parameter flags as the way to run the same
test with different settings. A test class declares
`variants = {name: {option: value}}`, where each option is the
destination of a command-line option (the framework's or the test's own
add_options). The first variant is the default.

- --variant=NAME sets that variant's options. An option also given
  explicitly on the command line keeps the explicit value.
- --variant=all runs every variant in turn, each in a new instance (and
  its own directory under --tmpdir), and exits with the worst result.
- --list-variants prints the names.
- An unknown variant is an argument error. A variant setting something
  that isn't an option raises ValueError.

Discovery reports each test's variants. test_runner.py runs the first
variant as "<file>" and the others as "<file>[<variant>]" (passing
--variant), alongside TEST_PARAMS until its entries move to the test
classes. Result names, rerun commands and phase records include the
variant.

Also: parse_args() now closes config.ini after reading it.

No test declares variants yet. Unit tests cover selection, explicit
options winning, unknown variants and options, --variant=all with a
skipping variant, discovery of variants and job-name parsing. The full
functional suite gives the same per-test results as before.

records.subject: test: report a test that fails early in setup instead of crashing
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
test: report a test that fails early in setup instead of crashing

When setup() failed before it had started logging and the network thread
(e.g. a config.ini without [environment]), main()'s own error handling
crashed: self.log, self.success and the network thread did not exist
yet, and shutdown() looked up PACKAGE_BUGREPORT, which was missing too.
The resulting AttributeError hid the original error.

__init__ now sets self.log and self.success (FAILED until setup()
completes). shutdown() skips a network thread that was never started
and tolerates a missing PACKAGE_BUGREPORT. The original exception is
reported (and kept as self.failure).

A unit test runs a test whose setup fails this way. The full functional
suite gives the same per-test results as before.

records.message:
test: test parameters can be class attributes

The framework's parameter defaults (chain, setup_clean_chain,
noban_tx_relay, rpc_timeout, supports_cli, bind_to_localhost_only,
default_wallet_name, wallet_data_filename, wallet_names,
disable_autoconnect) were set as instance attributes in __init__. A test

shadows a class attribute.

They are now class attributes of BitcoinTestFramework. A test can set
its parameters, num_nodes and extra_args included, as class attributes,
which the test runner can also read without instantiating the test.
set_test_params() remains for parameters known only at runtime, is
optional, and no longer required by the metaclass (run_test is).

A class-level extra_args is shared by every instance, and the framework
and some tests modify it, so each instance gets its own copy of the
lists.

Unit tests cover a test declared only with class attributes, and that
modifying one instance's extra_args leaves the class and other
instances alone. The full functional suite gives the same per-test
results as before (one run had two load-related RPC timeouts; both tests
pass on their own and in a rerun of the suite).

records.subject: util: let BoundedTaskQueue block producers instead of failing on overflow
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
util: let BoundedTaskQueue block producers instead of failing on overflow

BoundedTaskQueue only had a fail-closed overflow mode: a task that does
not fit invokes the fatal callback and stops the queue. That is right for
Chronik, which must never block the shared scheduler, but not for a
subscriber that can legitimately fall behind for minutes (a wallet that
holds cs_wallet for a load rescan).

Add Overflow::BLOCK. In this mode Enqueue waits on m_drained until the
task fits, the queue is empty, or the queue stops. A single task larger
than the byte limit is admitted only to an empty queue, so it can never
wait forever; the wait condition is written so it cannot underflow after
such a task. Stop() now also wakes blocked producers, which return
false. Enqueue in BLOCK mode asserts it is not called from the worker,
which would wait for itself.

The constructor also takes an optional thread name for the worker.
Chronik's call and the FAIL path are unchanged.

Tier: eCash

records.message:
validation: fence secondary queues for broadcast callers that wait

BroadcastTransaction(wait_callback=true) waited only for the main
validation queue. Subscribers that move work to their own worker
(Chronik today, the wallet next) could still be behind when it returned.
sendrawtransaction covered this with an extra

records.subject: wallet: deliver chain notifications to each wallet on its own FIFO worker
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
wallet: deliver chain notifications to each wallet on its own FIFO worker

Wallet Chain::Notifications callbacks ran inline on the shared
ValidationSignals scheduler thread. A wallet that holds cs_wallet (a
load rescan can take minutes) therefore stalled every other subscriber.

interfaces::Chain::handleNotifications takes a NotificationDelivery,
defaulting to SCHEDULER_THREAD, so Avalanche and the wallet benchmark
keep today's synchronous delivery. CWallet::AttachChain asks for
DEDICATED_WORKER: the proxy then forwards each event to a per-wallet
BoundedTaskQueue in BLOCK mode (64 MiB, 65536 tasks, 256 bytes of
overhead per task), run by one "walletnotify" thread. One producer, one
FIFO and one consumer keep the per-subscriber CValidationInterface
ordering. Payloads are copied: the transaction or block shared_ptr, the
height rather than the CBlockIndex, the locator by value.

- Fences: SyncTransactionQueue() waits for the worker, so
  SyncWithValidationInterfaceQueue(), FlushBackgroundCallbacks() and
  BroadcastTransaction(wait_callback) cover the wallet.
- Backpressure: a full queue makes the scheduler wait, which at worst
  reproduces today's wait on cs_wallet.
- Unload: disconnect() unregisters, then runs every accepted callback
  and joins. Later events are dropped; the wallet's persisted locator
  makes the next load rescan. RemoveWallet asserts it does not hold
  cs_wallet.
- Failure: the first callback exception logs a FATAL line and requests
  shutdown, and the wallet's later queued callbacks are discarded, so a
  later chainStateFlushed cannot persist a block the wallet failed to
  apply. Previously the exception terminated the process.

Tier: eCash

records.subject: http: serve the wallet PWA under /wallet/ with browser sessions and -gui
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
http: serve the wallet PWA under /wallet/ with browser sessions and -gui

The node now serves a browser wallet app (the node PWA, built in the
monorepo's wallets/node-pwa) at /wallet/ on its RPC listeners, and lets
a browser use JSON-RPC through a session cookie instead of Basic auth.

Files:
- GET /wallet/<path> serves the app; other methods under /wallet/ stay
  multi-wallet JSON-RPC. GET /wallet redirects to /wallet/. Paths are
  decoded once; traversal, encoded separators, dot-files and unknown
  types are 404. Every reply carries a strict CSP and related headers.
- Release builds embed a prebuilt node-pwa-bundle/1 tarball given by
  -DWALLET_PWA_BUNDLE and its required -DWALLET_PWA_BUNDLE_SHA256.
  contrib/devtools/embed_wallet_pwa.py checks every member against
  BUNDLE.json and its .gz siblings and emits sorted C++ arrays, so the
  output depends only on the bundle bytes. Embedded files get an ETag,
  If-None-Match/304, Cache-Control: no-cache and their gzip variant.
  Without a bundle (the default: none is published yet), /wallet/ is a
  short 404 page.
- -walletpwadir=<dir> serves a development directory instead, read on
  every request with Cache-Control: no-store.

Sessions:
- POST /auth/session logs in with a one-time token (from -gui or the new
  getwalletpwaurl RPC: 120 s, single use, stored hashed, at most 16) or
  with RPC credentials (checked by the existing RPC code, made reusable
  as CheckRPCCredentials, with the same 250 ms failure delay). It sets an
  HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie nodewallet_<rpcport> (Secure over
  https) and returns a CSRF token. GET /auth/session returns the session
  and its CSRF token; POST /auth/logout ends it.
- Sessions are in memory only (a restart logs everyone out), at most 64,
  expiring after 7 idle days or 30 days.
- A request without Authorization is authorized by its session only with
  the CSRF token, an Origin exactly equal to the node's own, an allowed
  Host (loopback, localhost or a -walletpwaorigin: the DNS-rebinding
  defence) and Content-Type: application/json. -rpcwhitelist applies to
  the session's RPC user as usual. Such failures omit WWW-Authenticate,
  so browsers do not prompt for a password.
- Sessions are only created over https or from loopback clients.
  HTTPRequest::GetScheme() believes X-Forwarded-Proto only from a
  -trustedproxy TCP peer.
- Basic auth (bitcoin-cli, scripts) is unchanged and needs no CSRF;
  -rpccorsdomain remains a Basic-auth-only path.

-gui opens the app in the default browser with a one-time link once the
HTTP server is up (open/xdg-open via posix_spawnp, ShellExecuteW on
Windows), printing the link only to a terminal and never to debug.log.
It implies -server and is an error with -walletpwa=0 or with no app to
serve. -walletpwa=0 turns all of it off.

Tests: walletpwa_tests (paths, MIME, ETags, encodings, the directory
source, the Origin/Host matrix, cookies, tokens and sessions under mock
time), test_embed_wallet_pwa.py, and interface_wallet_pwa.py (raw HTTP:
files and headers, logins, session RPC and its rejections, rebinding,
tokens and expiry, logout, whitelists, CORS, trusted proxies,
-publicbind, -walletpwa=0, -gui and, when built in, the embedded
bundle). Documentation: doc/wallet-pwa.md.

Tier: eCash

records.message:
node: report which block files may grow and announce pruned-file deletion

Readers outside BlockManager that keep block files open need two facts
the node did not expose:

- MayAppendToBlockFile(n): whether a block may still be written to
  blk n (it is a blockfile cursor's current file, or does not exist
  yet). Every other blk file is complete. The comment notes that undo
  data can still be appended to an older rev file when a block stored
  there is connected later (e.g. in a reorg).
- RegisterUnlinkFilesCallback(): UnlinkPrunedFiles runs the registered
  callbacks with the file numbers before it deletes them, so a reader
  can close its descriptors. Callbacks run under their own mutex, so
  none runs after UnregisterUnlinkFilesCallback() returns.

GetUndoPosFilename() completes GetBlockPosFilename() for rev files.

Test: blockmanager_unlink_files_callback (callbacks see the files
before deletion; unregistered callbacks never run).

records.message:
metrics: neutral fullnode_ namespace, client/network labels, build info

Metric names began with the product name (lotus_...), and nothing in a
series said which daemon or network it came from, so one Prometheus could
not tell an ecashd mainnet node from a regtest one, or from another tier's
daemon, without relabelling each scrape job.

Names now start with one fixed, neutral namespace, fullnode_
(METRICS_NAMESPACE in node/metrics.h, the only place to change it).
process_start_time_seconds keeps the name the Prometheus convention gives
it. Every series carries constant labels, rendered before the metric's
own:

- client: the daemon, from the build (FULLNODE_CLIENT, "ecashd" here);
- network: "<chain>-<network>", the chain part from the build
  (FULLNODE_CHAIN, "ecash") and the network from the chain parameters:
  ecash-mainnet, ecash-testnet, ecash-regtest. Each tier sets both in
  src/config/CMakeLists.txt, or -DFULLNODE_CLIENT=... overrides;
- the operator's, from repeatable -metricslabel=<name>=<value> (at most
  16). Names follow Prometheus rules; client, network, le, quantile, a
  "__" prefix, repeats and names of the metrics' own labels are refused
  at startup, as are empty, over-128-byte or control-character values.

fullnode_build_info{version,commit} 1 (plus client and network, like
every series) gives the build's version and commit.

All 22 metrics are renamed, and the registry's own dropped-samples
counter with them; doc/metrics.md documents the scheme, the catalogue and
a migration table from the old names (with a relabelling rule for the
transition). lotus_peers had a "network" label (the peer's address
network); it is renamed peer_network, since network is now the constant
label. The contrib/ logging collector configs reference no metric names
(only their own lotus_json parser), so they are unchanged; the logging
docs' two metric names are updated.

The registry (metrics/metrics.h) gains SetConstLabels, a name prefix for
its own metric, and IsValidMetricName/IsValidLabelName, checked when a
metric is added. Recording is unchanged: the labels are rendered once
into a string that each series line copies at scrape time.

Cardinality: no new per-metric labels. build_info has 1 series; the
constant labels do not multiply series (they are the same on every series
of a node).

The functional test's exposition parser moves to
test_framework/metrics.py (parse, Scrape lookups that ignore constant
labels unless asked, request, scrape) so later tests share it.

Evidence:
- test_bitcoin metrics_tests pass, with new cases: label/metric name
  rules, constant labels on counters, gauges, histogram buckets/sum/count
  and the dropped-samples counter, refusal cases, every node metric
  namespaced (or process_*) and free of lotus_, ParseMetricsLabels
  accept/refuse cases, network label for each chain type.
- interface_http_metrics.py passes: every series has client="ecashd",
  network="ecash-regtest" and two -metricslabel labels (one needing
  escaping) first; build_info is 1 with the node's version; the eight
  refusal cases each stop startup with their error.
- metrics_tests/rings_prepared_and_reused is flaky before and after this
  change (7/100 and 4/100 failures under the shared machine's load; the
  ring code is unchanged).

Not tested: a build with BUILD_GIT_COMMIT set (this build has no git, so
commit is ""); testnet/mainnet label values other than through the unit
test; full functional suite (run once at the end of the series).
