records.message:
metrics: Avalanche quorum, proof pools, polls, votes and finalization

Whether a node takes part in Avalanche, and how its votes go, was only
visible through getavalancheinfo and debug logs. These series give the
quorum state and the flow of polls, votes and finalizations.

Gauges, set at scrape time by a collector:
- fullnode_avalanche_quorum_established: the latched quorum flag while at
  least 8 nodes are connected (what isQuorumEstablished answers once
  latched), read without its side effects or locks;
- fullnode_avalanche_quorum_nodes and
  fullnode_avalanche_quorum_score{scope=total|connected}: the figures the
  peer manager already publishes for isQuorumEstablished
  (getQuorumMetrics, lock-free);
- fullnode_avalanche_proofs{pool=valid|conflicting|immature|dangling}:
  distinct proofs per pool (takes cs_peerManager once per rendering).

Counters, where the events happen:
- fullnode_avalanche_polls_sent_total and
  fullnode_avalanche_poll_items_sent_total (event loop, at send);
- fullnode_avalanche_polls_received_total{outcome=answered|ignored}
  (AVAPOLL, ignored within the peer's cooldown);
- fullnode_avalanche_votes_received_total{vote=yes|no|neutral}: votes in
  responses to our polls, bucketed as VoteRecord counts them (0 yes,
  positive error no, negative error neutral);
- fullnode_avalanche_items_total{type,outcome=finalized|invalidated|stale}
  for the six vote item types (proof, block, contender, transaction,
  batch, state_anchor: the AnyVoteItem variant's order, checked by a
  static_assert).

fullnode_avalanche_finalization_seconds{type} times an item from its
registration for polling to its finalization. VoteRecord gains an
addedTime, read from the steady clock in addToReconcile only when metrics
are on (8 bytes per record); the two batch paths that replace a record
keep it.

Collectors that read subsystems created after /metrics starts serving
(here the Avalanche processor) live in node/metrics_collectors.cpp:
started at the end of AppInitMain and removed in Shutdown. The registry's
AddCollector is now thread-safe (under the render mutex) and returns an id
for RemoveCollector.

Cardinality: quorum_established 1, quorum_nodes 1, quorum_score 2,
proofs 4, polls_sent 1, poll_items_sent 1, polls_received 2,
votes_received 3, items 18, finalization_seconds 6 label sets (16
buckets each). 39 series plus histogram buckets.

Hot paths: registerVotes (msghand thread) adds one sharded counter add
per vote and per ended item and one ring push per finalization; the
event loop two adds per poll; addToReconcile one clock read per item when
metrics are on. No lock is added to these paths. Overhead benches are run
at the end of the series.

Evidence:
- test_bitcoin metrics_tests pass (new: collectors added/removed while
  rendering; vote bucketing); test-avalanche voterecord_tests and
  processor_tests pass.
- interface_metrics_avalanche.py: before any peer, quorum 0 and all
  label sets present; 16 peers establish the quorum (nodes 16, connected
  score = total, valid proofs = getavalancheinfo's proof_count); polling
  finalizes the proofs (items_total and finalization _count agree, _sum
  > 0); a block is finalized after rounds of neutral and no votes, which
  are counted; a poll within the cooldown is counted as ignored.
- interface_http_metrics.py still passes.

Not tested: invalidated and stale items, and transaction/batch/contender/
state-anchor finalization (counted by the same code); the quorum flag
dropping when nodes fall below 8.

records.message:
metrics: block validation stages, script checks, caches, UTXO, reorgs

Only the total time to connect a block was exported. Where that time
goes, how well the validation caches and the UTXO cache work, how often
the cache is flushed, and how often the chain reorganizes or refuses
blocks, needed -debug=bench logs or nothing.

- fullnode_block_validation_stage_seconds{stage}: the -debug=bench stage
  timers, now also recorded: check, forks, connect, verify (only the
  script wait; the bench log's verify includes connect), index
  (ConnectBlock), and load, flush, chainstate, post_connect (ConnectTip).
  Recorded once a block is connected: failed blocks and template checks
  (fJustCheck) are not counted. Buckets 10 us to 60 s.
- fullnode_script_check_transactions and fullnode_script_check_workers:
  per block, the transactions whose scripts had to be checked and the
  workers used. This tier checks a block's scripts on
  ParallelScriptWorkerPool (one worker per pending transaction, up to the
  hardware threads), not on the CCheckQueue (-par), which ConnectBlock
  no longer feeds; so "queue depth and parallelism" are measured there,
  per block, rather than as an instantaneous queue length that would read
  0 at almost every scrape.
- fullnode_validation_cache_lookups_total{cache=signature|
  script_execution,result=hit|miss}: SignatureCache::Get (both cache
  levels) and the script execution cache lookups of ConnectBlock and
  CheckInputScripts.
- fullnode_utxo_cache_bytes and fullnode_utxo_cache_entries, set in
  FlushStateToDisk from the values it already computes (active

records.message:
bench: cost of the metrics recording on hot paths

The metrics series adds recording to paths that run per coin lookup, per
signature check and per mempool change. These benchmarks run the same
work with the node's metrics off (as without -metrics) and on (a started
registry, as -metrics), so the cost can be measured rather than assumed:

- MetricsOverheadUtxoCacheHit{Off,On}: CCoinsViewCache::HaveCoin hits,
  with and without the lookup counter (FetchCoin).
- MetricsOverheadSigCacheHit{Off,On}: SignatureCache::Get hitting the
  thread's first-level cache, with the cache lookup counter.
- MetricsOverheadMempoolAddEvict{Off,On}: addUnchecked and
  TrimToSize(0) of eight transactions (snapshot publication counted and
  timed, removals counted), as the MempoolEviction bench does.

Measured on this tier's build (macOS arm64, Release, a shared machine at
load average ~50; three runs each):
- UTXO cache hit: 41.9-46.8 ns/lookup off, 49.4-51.3 on (+3 to +8 ns,
  one sharded counter add).
- Signature cache hit: 11.8-12.6 ns off, 14.4-15.7 on (+2.6 to +3.2 ns).
- Mempool add+evict (-min_time=3000): 6.5-7.4 us/tx off, 5.6-8.4 on:
  the difference is below the run-to-run spread.
- With metrics off, against the base build: CCoinsCaching 1347-1643 ns
  (base) vs 1333-1383 (this series), MempoolEviction 52.6-62.1 us vs
  59.4-61.0: within noise.
- Unit costs (existing benches): counter add 2.9-3.0 ns, event ring push
  7.5-9.6 ns, a disabled recording site 0.3-0.4 ns, two clock reads
  29.7-31.3 ns.

Not measured: Avalanche vote registration, block connection (nine ring
pushes per block) and P2P handshakes/pings, whose added work is one or a
few of the unit costs above per event.

records.message:
chronik: add CHRONIK_IMPLEMENTATION={rust,native} and native skeleton

Add a CMake cache option CHRONIK_IMPLEMENTATION, next to BUILD_CHRONIK,
that selects which Chronik is compiled into the node: "rust" (the
default, unchanged) or "native", a pure C++20 implementation that lives in
chronik/native/ under the chronik::native namespace.

With native, chronik/CMakeLists.txt adds chronik/native and returns before
RustHelper is included, so Cargo, Corrosion and a Rust toolchain are never
required, and only one implementation is linked (the native build carries
no chronik_lib symbols). Python plugins are Rust-only, so combining
BUILD_CHRONIK_PLUGINS with native is a configure error.

The skeleton contains:
- types.h: the neutral data model (Tx, TxInput/TxOutput, Coin, Block,
  BlockInfo, capabilities) host adapters convert node types into;
- error.h: ChronikError, with the "NNN: " status-prefix convention of
  abc_rust_error;
- a core library and a Boost.Test unit-test binary, test_chronik_native,
  whose sources each area lists in its own sources.cmake. The directory
  also builds standalone (cmake -S chronik/native) for fast core work;
- a stub ABC host entry providing chronik::Start/Interrupt/Stop with the
  signatures of chronik-cpp/chronik.h, so init.cpp is unchanged. Until the
  host adapter lands, -chronik fails at startup with a clear error.

The build exports ENABLE_CHRONIK_NATIVE to bitcoin-config.h, and
ENABLE_CHRONIK_NATIVE / ENABLE_CHRONIK_ELECTRUM to the functional test
config (the native implementation has no Electrum interface). The C++
bridge unit tests in test_bitcoin exercise the Rust bridge and are only
built with the Rust implementation.

Tier: eCash

records.subject: chronik: native KvStore interface and an MDBX backend matching Rust
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
chronik: native KvStore interface and an MDBX backend matching Rust

Add the storage layer of the native Chronik:

- store.h: KvStore with ordered cursors, duplicate-value cursors, read
  snapshots and read-your-writes write transactions. It is the only path
  from the core to storage; the core library includes no database header
  and links no database. Backends are separate libraries that register
  themselves explicitly (RegisterMdbxStore()), so a host links exactly the
  backends it selects.
- schema.h: the 26 eCash-tier tables in the order the Rust chronik-db
  registers them, with their duplicate-value layout (script_utxo is
  DUPSORT|DUPFIXED with 20-byte tx_num/out_idx/sats entries, token_id_utxo
  DUPSORT with variable entries). Schema::Add lets a tier extension add
  its own tables; the eCash tier carries no V2 table.
- store/mdbx: chronik_native_store_mdbx, built on the vendored libmdbx. It
  reproduces the Rust environment exactly: one env at indexes/chronik,
  256 readers, max(n_tables+16, 64) DBIs, the same geometry (1 MiB lower,
  16 MiB initial, 256 GiB upper, 64 MiB growth, 128 MiB shrink, 16 KiB
  pages), SAFE_NOSYNC|NOMETASYNC|LIFORECLAIM|NOSTICKYTHREADS|NOMEMINIT,
  mode 0600, 16 MiB sync bytes and 65536 sync period, a named DBI per
  table, and keys longer than 7500 bytes stored as
  "MDBX_SHA256_KEY:" || sha256(key) using the host's SHA-256. Rust's merge
  emulation is a physical detail: callers do explicit read-modify-writes,
  which produce the same bytes.

A conformance suite runs against every registered backend: ordering,
SeekGe/SeekLe/SeekLast/Prev, duplicate semantics, read-your-writes,
snapshot isolation under a concurrent writer, Clear, long keys, reopen
persistence, and the environment settings above.

Tier: eCash

records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
chronik: native optional LevelDB storage backend

Adds chronik_native_store_leveldb (CHRONIK_NATIVE_LEVELDB=ON, default
OFF), a second KvStore implementation on the node's vendored LevelDB. The
core is unchanged: it still sees only the KvStore interface, and a
LevelDB-only build (CHRONIK_NATIVE_MDBX=OFF) links no MDBX code.

Layout (documented in leveldb_store.h): one LevelDB at
indexes/chronik-leveldb, never the MDBX/Rust directory. Plain table keys
are varint(id) || key; dup table keys are varint(id) || escaped(key) ||
dup, where the escaping (0x00 -> 0x00 0xff, terminator 0x00 0x00) is
order-preserving, so keys and dups iterate in MDBX order, including plain
cursors over dup tables (used by group UTXO prefix scans and the dump).
Table ids are assigned on first open and persisted with each table's
kind, so tables added later are never renumbered and a changed kind is
refused. A ReadTxn is a snapshot; a WriteTxn is an ordered overlay over a
snapshot (read-your-writes, Clear as a table tombstone), committed as one
WriteBatch with sync=false; Sync() writes an empty synced batch. Opening an
MDBX directory, or a foreign LevelDB, is refused. EstimateEntries counts
exactly (LevelDB has no counts; it is only used for progress logs).

The node selects the backend with the hidden -chronikdbbackend=mdbx|leveldb
(default mdbx, or leveldb in LevelDB-only builds); an unknown or unbuilt
backend is an init error. The legacy-RocksDB refusal applies only to the
MDBX directory, since a LevelDB directory also has CURRENT/MANIFEST files.

Tests: the KvStore conformance suite gains a randomized model test (Get,
both cursor directions, seeks, dup cursors and plain cursors over dup
tables, against an in-memory model, before and after commits) and LevelDB
table-id/refusal tests; every other suite runs on the backend chosen by
CHRONIK_NATIVE_TEST_BACKEND (default MDBX when linked). The standalone
build vendors src/leveldb and src/crc32c without their tests.

records.subject: chronik: native hosts read complete block files through cached descriptors
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
chronik: native hosts read complete block files through cached descriptors

AbcHost::LoadTx and LoadRawTx read one tx (and its undo data) per tx of a
response through BlockManager::ReadTxFromDisk/ReadTxUndoFromDisk, which
open the blk/rev file, fseek, read one buffer through stdio and close it:
seven syscalls per read, two reads per tx.

chronik/native/hosts/common/flat_file_reader.{h,cpp} adds a small LRU
(16 entries) of read-only descriptors keyed by file kind and number,
read with pread through a 4 KiB buffered cursor. It knows only file paths
and a "may the node still append to this file" hook, so other hosts
(BCHN, Bitcoin Core) can reuse it; the header notes what a Bitcoin Core
host must add (un-XOR blocks/xor.dat obfuscation per refill). Windows has
no pread: the cache is disabled there.

- Files the node may still append to (the cursor's current blk file and
  its rev file) are not cached; they keep the BlockManager path.
- rev n is cached once blk n is complete. Undo data can still be appended
  to it (a reorg connecting blocks stored in blk n), which pread handles:
  it reads the file's current contents, and written undo bytes never
  change. A memory mapping could not take that growth safely, which is
  one reason this uses descriptors.
- The host registers an unlink callback: pruned files are dropped before
  the node deletes them, and a concurrent open that started before the
  prune is used for its own read but not cached. (-prune is rejected
  with -chronik today; this keeps the host correct if that changes.)
- Any cached read that fails falls back to the BlockManager path, which
  reports the error as before.

The Rust Chronik (chronik-cpp/chronik_bridge.cpp) is unchanged: it is not
built with the native tree, and sharing the reader would need it compiled
into the Corrosion bridge and owned by ChronikBridge.

Measured with contrib/chronik-parity/bench_tx_reads.py (3,000 blocks,
92% of txs in a complete blk file, 120 history pages of 200 txs, 3,000
/tx lookups, warm page cache, loaded host; medians of 5-7 passes, 3 runs

s, 8 clients 0.22-0.27 s -> 0.24-0.28 s (unchanged, HTTP-bound). Block

Response bytes are identical.

8-thread concurrency) and test_bitcoin chronik_native_blockreader_tests
(AbcHost: cached reads equal BlockManager's, write-file bypass, prune
invalidation and unregistration, concurrent LoadTx).

records.subject: test: show a failed test's logs as one timeline, and write combined.log
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
test: show a failed test's logs as one timeline, and write combined.log

A failure that involves the test and several nodes had to be read from
separate blocks (the framework log's tail, then each node's warnings and
errors), then combine_logs.py run by hand to see what happened in which
order. The runner now merges the logs itself.

test_framework/timeline.py reads test_framework.log and every node's
debug.log (or, where a node also wrote one, its JSON-lines log in the
chain directory, with time from "time"/"@timestamp") as events: time,
source ("test", "node0", ...), level when known, message and raw text.
Continuation lines (tracebacks) stay with their event; a node line's
"(mocktime: ...)" is kept as a field and does not affect the order. Three
ways to read them, by cost:

- read_timeline(): event by event (heapq merge of streamed files), for
  combine_logs.py, and the reference the faster paths are tested against.
- failure_excerpt(): the last lines up to the framework's logged
  exception, reading only the end of each log: the framework log
  backwards to the exception, each node's log up to its time by binary
  search (the logs are in time order). A few milliseconds whatever the
  size of the logs.
- write_combined_log(): the text logs merged in 4 MB binary blocks. The
  timestamps are fixed-width ISO 8601 with microseconds, so they are
  compared as bytes, checked a block at a time with byte operations, with
  no per-line parsing, regular expression or datetime. Only blocks with a
  line that does not start with such a timestamp (a traceback, or a log
  with whole-second timestamps) are parsed as events. Each merge round
  emits the entries below the smallest last key of the sources still
  being read; Python's stable sort keeps equal timestamps in source order,
  then file order.

On failure, the runner writes <tmpdir>/combined.log (each line prefixed
by its source, continuation lines indented) and the failure block shows,
in place of the framework-log tail and the per-node warning blocks, the
last 40 lines of the timeline up to and including the logged exception.
That line is shown without its traceback, which the block already shows
once above. Lines are compact: source column, time of day, level for
warnings and errors, category, message (no source location). The
combine_logs.py hint is replaced by the path of combined.log; the HTML
option stays documented in doc/functional-tests.md.

combine_logs.py now uses the module's parsing and merging. Its options and
output format are unchanged; one behaviour differs: events with equal
timestamps keep their file order. Before, heapq.merge compared whole
(timestamp, source, text) tuples, so same-millisecond framework lines were
printed sorted by their text.

Also fixed: test_runner.py --combinedlogslen raised NameError when the
output was not colored (the combine_logs.py call was indented under
`if BOLD[0]`). Inherited from upstream.

Known limit: the framework's text log has millisecond timestamps, so node
lines in the same millisecond as the exception sort after it and are not
in the excerpt (they are in combined.log).

Unit tests (run by test_runner.py): interleaving of three sources, equal
timestamps, numeric node order, multi-line events, mocktime, JSON sidecar
preferred, records without a time or partly written, missing and empty
logs, lines before the first timestamp, reordering within a source, the
cut-off at the failure, the binary search, and randomized logs (equal
timestamps, tracebacks, blank and whitespace lines, whole-second logs,
nodes logging after the failure) on which the fast combined.log must be
byte-identical to the event-by-event one and the excerpt identical to
the merged timeline's, with small blocks to cross block boundaries.

Measured (macOS arm64, median of 3, load average 63-107, before = the
earlier version of this commit, which merged event by event):
- 954 MB synthetic log: combined.log 23.2 s wall / 12.3 s CPU before,
  2.31 s / 1.82 s after (525 MB/s of CPU time); excerpt 31.7 s before,
  6 ms after.
- Real failed tests (p2p_headers_sync_with_minchainwork, 57 MB;
  abc_p2p_avalanche_cooldown, 50 MB): combined.log 4.1 s and 1.0 s
  before, 0.25 s and 0.17 s after; excerpt 2.8 s and 0.68 s before, 6 ms
  and 3 ms after.
Fast and reference outputs are identical on 51 saved test directories,
the real ones above and the synthetic logs, and on 200 more randomized
cases with block sizes down to 97 bytes.

Validation on the canonical Lotus V2 stack (7e1c60df1c): applied without
conflicts. ruff 0.15.8 format/check pass; mypy with ABC's lint flags
reports the same 5 errors as the base, none in files changed here; all 93
framework unit tests pass. The earlier version of this commit gave the
same full-suite result as the base for every test (335 jobs: 199 passed,
15 skipped, 121 failed in both, the failures being the base's); this
version was checked with unit tests and targeted runner runs only, as it
does not change the runner's flow. Not run: Linux, extended tests.

records.subject: test: write each test's events as one structured timeline.jsonl
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
test: write each test's events as one structured timeline.jsonl

Nodes already write their records as JSON lines (debug-framework.jsonl)
with typed registry fields, but finding what happened across the test and
its nodes still meant reading each file. Each test can now have one
stream, <tmpdir>/timeline.jsonl: every event of every source, sorted by
time, one JSON object per line.

Records: "time" (RFC 3339, UTC, microseconds) and "source" ("test",
"node0", ...) first, then the record's fields in their order, with "level"
and "message" always present. A node record keeps the sidecar's fields as
they are (category, thread, event, peer_id, txid, mocktime, ...); only the
node's source location object "source" becomes "source_location", since
"source" now names the process. Nodes without a sidecar are read from
debug.log, with parsed category, thread, mocktime and source_location.

The framework also writes its log as JSON lines, test_framework.jsonl,
through a formatter next to the text one (test_framework.log is
unchanged): compact, "time" first, then level, category (the logger),
thread, message, source_location, "exception" with the traceback, and any
fields passed as self.log.info(..., extra={"fields": {...}}). The timeline
and the failure excerpt read it in preference to the text log, so the
framework's events have microsecond times.

Building timeline.jsonl without parsing records: the nodes' sidecar lines
and the framework's all start with {"time":"<27-byte timestamp>","level":"
(the node encoder's single sidecar write path forces timestamps with
microseconds and writes time, then level, first; that is its current
behaviour, not a documented guarantee). Blocks of 4 MB are converted with
two byte replacements: the source inserted after the time, and the
node's "source":{ renamed; a JSON string cannot contain an unescaped
quote, so both sequences only occur as keys. The converted lines are
checked column by column with byte operations; a block that does not
pass (a partial record, spaced JSON, another writer) is parsed record by
record instead, with the same result. Lines are merged by comparing the
timestamp bytes, as for combined.log.

When it is written:
- for every failed test: by the runner, once the test's processes have
  stopped, after combined.log; a test run directly writes it at shutdown;
- for a passing test only with --timeline (on the runner, or on the
  test), because of the cost; cleanup then keeps only that file.

Wiring:
- JobResult gains "timeline", the file's path (schema 2); the runner
  writes a failed test's timeline before the JSON-lines "finish" event, so
  --jsonl-file carries the path. README-runner-output.md documents the
  field and the record format.
- The failure block reads the structured records when present and shows a
  few identifying fields compactly, e.g.
  "[netdebug] sending pong (8 bytes) peer=1  {event=peer_message_sent
  peer_id=1 msg_type=pong}", and both file paths.
- timeline.check_timeline(path) checks a file: JSON objects with the
  required keys, in time order.

Not done: scraping each node's /metrics at shutdown (the optional
stretch); it would add an HTTP request to every node stop, and the dropped
line count it would report is already checked by the framework from each
node's logger_shutdown record.

Re-applied on the corrected previous commit: conflicts in
README-runner-output.md (kept the new combined.log description, with "the
text logs" for the HTML note), reporting.py (failure_timeline now takes
the excerpt from the tails, then writes combined.log, then
timeline.jsonl) and timeline.py (kept the new readers and fast paths; the
timeline functions and tests added here).

Measured (macOS arm64, median of 3, load average 70-107; before = the
earlier version of this commit, which converted event by event):
- 1.4 GB synthetic JSON logs: 134 s wall / 53 s CPU before, 21.9 s /
  4.9 s after (291 MB/s of CPU time; ~300 MB/s is the cost of the two
  byte replacements and the 1.52 GB written); excerpt 52.6 s before,
  6 ms after.
- Real failed tests (57 and 50 MB): 5.8 s and 4.0 s before, 1.0 s and
  0.51 s after (about 240 MB/s of CPU time).

Validation on the canonical Lotus V2 stack (7e1c60df1c) plus the previous
commit: ruff 0.15.8 format/check pass; mypy with ABC's lint flags reports
the base's 5 errors, none in files changed here; all 97 framework unit
tests pass, including randomized JSON logs (equal timestamps, spaced and
partial records, blank lines, quotes and ,"source":{ inside messages) on
which the fast timeline.jsonl must equal the event-by-event records, key
order included. The same holds on 40 real failed-test directories from
this stack, on the synthetic logs, and on 120 more randomized cases with
block sizes down to 97 bytes. The earlier version of this commit ran the
full default suite at -j 12: 335 jobs, 195 passed, 15 skipped, 125
failed, the base's 121 plus four load timeouts at load average ~100
(abc_p2p_avalanche_quorum.py, abc_p2p_avalanche_voting.py,
abc_rpc_isfinal.py, feature_reindex.py), which pass alone with and
without it. This version changes how the files are built, not the
runner's flow, so it was checked with targeted runs: a temporary failing
test (failure block, combined.log, timeline.jsonl equal to the
reference, the path in the finish event), and --timeline on 12 passing
jobs (all passed; all 13 files valid, 147,116 records; only timeline.jsonl
left). Not run: Linux, extended tests, a full suite with --timeline.

records.subject: net: add -p2prawlisten and -p2pwslisten to choose the listening transports
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: add -p2prawlisten and -p2pwslisten to choose the listening transports

An eCash node that accepts WebSocket peers also had to run the plain P2P
listener: -listen=1 opened both. Lotus V2 drops plain P2P altogether, but
ecashd must keep it for stock Bitcoin ABC peers, so operators wanting a
WebSocket-only node need explicit switches.

-listen keeps its name, default and interactions (-bind, -whitebind,
-connect, -proxy) and stays the master switch for inbound peers. Two
options select the transports it accepts:

- -p2prawlisten (default 1): raw P2P, i.e. plain P2P, the ordinary
  non-WebSocket protocol.
- -p2pwslisten (default 1, DEFAULT_P2P_WEBSOCKET): P2P over WebSocket.
  It replaces -p2pwebsocket, which is removed without an alias: ecashd
  has not been released, so nobody depends on the old name. The
  pre-existing p2p_websocket_inbound.py use is renamed.

| -listen | -p2prawlisten | -p2pwslisten | accepted inbound          |
|---------|---------------|--------------|---------------------------|
| 0       | any           | any          | nothing (as before)       |
| 1       | 1 (default)   | 1 (default)  | plain P2P and WebSocket   |
| 1       | 0             | 1            | WebSocket only            |
| 1       | 1             | 0            | plain P2P only            |
| 1       | 0             | 0            | nothing, with a warning   |

The defaults keep WebSocket exactly where it was. WebSocket remains
reachable only through -publicbind listeners and, for -rpcallowip
clients, the RPC port. With -listen=0, /p2p/ws upgrades are still
answered 503 and no WebSocket peer is accepted.

With -p2prawlisten=0:

- No plain P2P listening socket is opened at all, not even on loopback.
- No plain P2P address is learned or advertised: AddLocal refuses
  everything but NET_WSS addresses, GetLocal skips them, a peer's view of
  our address is not used (IsPeerAddrLocalGood), -addrmantest's loopback
  address is not sent, and interface discovery is not run. -externaldomain
  advertisement is unchanged.
- -natpmp, -discover, -listenonion and -i2pacceptincoming are soft-set to
  0. Options that only make sense with a plain P2P listener are refused at
  startup rather than ignored: -bind and -whitebind (an operator who names
  a bind address, or grants permissions on one, expects it to listen;
  silently dropping a whitebind's permissions is the worse surprise, and
  -listen=0 already refuses them the same way), -externalip (it
  advertises a plain P2P address), an explicit -listenonion=1 (the Tor
  onion service forwards to the plain P2P onion bind) and an explicit
  -i2pacceptincoming=1 (plain P2P over I2P). Onion binds (-bind=...=onion)
  are -bind and refused likewise.

Outbound connections are not changed by -p2prawlisten. -onlynet=wss is
the way to stop plain outbound P2P, and it now also covers manual
connections (-addnode, -connect, the addnode RPC): when -onlynet includes
wss, a manual plain P2P dial needs its address family's network (IPv4 or
IPv6, so loopback and private addresses included) to be allowed too.
Without wss in -onlynet, manual connections keep ignoring -onlynet, as
before. A WebSocket-only node is then:

  -p2prawlisten=0 -onlynet=wss  (plus -publicbind for public inbound)

Evidence:
- net_tests/plain_p2p_off_advertises_no_plain_address: plain addresses
  refused by AddLocal; inbound and outbound peers' views of us are never
  used; only the NET_WSS address is advertised, and nothing without it.
- net_tests/p2p_listen_args: both switches, the warning, refused
  options, soft-set defaults, -bind still soft-setting -listen=1.
- p2p_listen_options.py (new): defaults accept both; -p2prawlisten=0
  refuses TCP on the P2P port while a WebSocket peer connects and syncs a
  block; addr/addrv2 sent to a peer contain only the -externaldomain (a
  control node with plain P2P advertises the address the peer saw);
  -onlynet=wss makes no plain outbound connection (-addnode and addnode
  onetry to a loopback address); -listen=0 with -p2pwslisten=1 accepts no
  WebSocket peer; -p2pwslisten=0 stops serving /p2p/ws; refused
  options.
- Existing tests touching these paths pass: feature_proxy,
  feature_torcontrol, feature_p2p_privacy_recipes, p2p_i2p_sessions,
  p2p_node_network_limited, p2p_websocket_{inbound,proxy,discovery,tls,
  addr_versions}, rpc_net, abc_feature_avalanche_options.

Not tested: UPnP is not built here (only NAT-PMP, which is soft-set off
and whose mapping would be filtered by AddLocal); real Tor/I2P daemons;
Windows.

records.subject: net: accept P2P over WebSocket on the P2P port, beside raw P2P
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: accept P2P over WebSocket on the P2P port, beside raw P2P

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (defaults): WebSocket and WebSocket/TLS peers are now
also accepted on the public P2P port, the same way raw P2P is. Before,
WebSocket was public only on -publicbind listeners (and on the RPC port
for -rpcallowip clients). Nothing else changes with the defaults: raw
P2P peers are created, checked, timed out and evicted exactly as before,
silent ones included, and no new port is opened.

Why: the user chose to share the P2P port rather than add a default
WebSocket port, so that a node reachable over raw P2P is reachable over
WebSocket too, and a WebSocket-only node needs no extra listener.

One port, three protocols. Each connection on the P2P port is
classified from its first bytes, peeked (never consumed):

- 0x16 0x03 (a TLS ClientHello) -> wss: the HTTP server's TLS stack;
- "GET " (an HTTP request line) -> ws;
- anything else -> raw P2P. Stock peers start with the network magic,
  whose first byte (0xe3, 0xf4, 0xda) can start neither, so they are
  decided at once and never wait for more data
  (ClassifyP2PPortBytes; a magic that could start TLS or GET would wait
  for 4 bytes).

Switches (on the P2P port, under -listen=1):

- -p2prawlisten (default 1) accepts raw P2P ("raw" means plain,
  non-WebSocket P2P). With 0, raw P2P connections are closed after
  classification.
- -p2pwslisten (default 1) accepts WebSocket and WebSocket/TLS, and keeps
  the -publicbind and RPC-port handling. With 0 the P2P port speaks only
  raw P2P, exactly as before this commit (no classification at all).
- The P2P port's listening sockets open when -listen=1 and either is on.
  -bind/-whitebind are therefore accepted with -p2prawlisten=0 (they
  listen for WebSocket), and refused only when both are off. Onion binds,
  -listenonion, -externalip and -i2pacceptincoming stay refused with
  -p2prawlisten=0 (they serve or advertise raw P2P).
- WebSocket needs the HTTP server (-server, which ecashd sets): without
  it the P2P port stays raw-only, and -p2prawlisten=0 warns that nothing
  will be accepted. Lotus V2's HTTP server without RPC listeners is not
  ported.

How a connection travels:

- Raw P2P on (default): the accepted socket becomes a CNode as before,
  marked unclassified. The socket handler peeks at it before its first
  read (ClassifyP2PPortNode). Raw P2P carries on unchanged; HTTP/TLS has
  its socket (nothing read) handed to the HTTP server and the node is
  dropped. Inbound slots, bans and eviction thus apply before any
  HTTP/TLS work, as for any inbound peer. Cost: such a WebSocket peer
  briefly appears as a raw inbound node and uses a second node id.
- Raw P2P off: no node is created before the upgrade. The checks needing
  no data (network active, bans, discouragement when nearly full, a full
  node without an eviction candidate) run first (MayAcceptInbound, which
  does not evict); then the socket goes to the HTTP server, which
  classifies the same way and closes raw P2P without reading it.

What the P2P port serves over HTTP/TLS: only the P2P WebSocket endpoint
(-p2pwebsocketpath, with -p2pwebsockettoken rules). Every other request
gets 404, or the -publicfallback site when set, as on -publicbind. Never
JSON-RPC, REST, wallet, Chronik or health checks. A plain-text request
other than GET is not HTTP to the P2P port at all: raw P2P rejects it as
before. TLS uses the -publicbind configuration (-tlscert/-tlskey,
-tlsephemeral neutral certificates, live reload); the WebSocket session
reuses WebSocketSock and the direct hand-off into CConnman (or the
bridge), the TLS profile, and token and fallback handling unchanged.
-whitebind permissions apply to WebSocket peers on the listener they
reached, matched by the address reached; onion binds still mark peers
as inbound onion.

DoS limits:

- -p2pporthandshaketimeout (debug, default 10 s) bounds how long a P2P
  port connection may take to classify and, for WebSocket, to finish its
  upgrade. On expiry an undecided connection counts as raw P2P (with raw
  on, a silent client is then an ordinary raw peer, as before; with raw
  off it is closed). The HTTP stage keeps the deadline running until the
  upgrade (or the hand-off to -publicfallback) and disarms it before a
  socket can belong to CConnman.
- At most 64 P2P port connections (8 per address) may be in the HTTP
  stage before upgrading; others are closed. Partial first bytes are
  re-peeked each loop instead of polled, so they cannot spin the socket
  thread.

Advertisement is unchanged: NET_WSS still needs -externaldomain, and IP
addresses are advertised when raw P2P is on. A peer knowing only an IP
address could try wss://<ip>:<port>/p2p/ws on the same port; automatic
dialing of that is not implemented (it would need a fallback policy and
SNI-less TLS), only manual -addnode/-connect URLs.

Sock::Release() gives up a socket without closing it, for the hand-off
to the HTTP server.

Evidence:
- net_tests/classify_p2p_port_bytes: every network's magic is raw P2P
  from its first byte; TLS/GET need 2/4 bytes; magics that look like TLS
  or GET wait for 4 bytes.
- net_tests/p2p_listen_args: -bind accepted with -p2prawlisten=0 unless
  both transports are off; onion binds refused; the -server warning.
- p2p_websocket_p2p_port.py (new): a stock-style raw peer proceeds with
  no classification hand-off; raw, ws:// and wss:// node peers share the
  P2P port and sync blocks both ways; Python ws/wss peers handshake;
  REST, health, Chronik, JSON-RPC are 404 (TLS) or not HTTP (plain POST),
  with REST served on the RPC port as control; -publicfallback answers
  plain and TLS requests on the P2P port while wss still works;
  -p2prawlisten=0 closes raw P2P before any version and the first
  WebSocket node gets id 0; -p2pwslisten=0 refuses ws/wss and accepts
  raw; silent, partial-HTTP, partial-TLS and partial-"GE" clients are
  closed at the deadline while a WebSocket peer connects; the per-address
  pending limit; with raw on a silent client is a raw peer past the
  deadline.
- p2p_listen_options.py adapted: with -p2prawlisten=0 the port is bound
  but raw P2P is closed; both off opens no socket.
- Passing, run after this change: all p2p_websocket_*, interface_http*,
  p2p_timeouts, p2p_leak, p2p_eviction, p2p_permissions,
  p2p_add_connections, p2p_disconnect_ban, p2p_invalid_messages,
  feature_p2p_privacy_recipes, feature_proxy, rpc_net.

Not tested: PROXY protocol headers on the P2P port (supported on
-publicbind and the RPC port only; a PROXY header on the P2P port is raw
P2P garbage); Windows; real browsers; load beyond the functional tests;
the test framework's TEST_P2P_TRANSPORT=websocket mode with raw P2P on,
where tests asserting peer ids see the extra id noted above.

records.subject: net: add -p2prequiretls, and keep -onlynet=wss off unencrypted ws://
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: add -p2prequiretls, and keep -onlynet=wss off unencrypted ws://

An operator who exposes P2P over WebSocket may want every P2P connection
encrypted. Raw P2P is already a separate switch (-p2prawlisten=0); this
adds the WebSocket half.

-p2prequiretls (default 0) refuses WebSocket P2P peers that did not
arrive over TLS, wherever WebSocket P2P is accepted: the shared P2P
port, -publicbind listeners and the RPC port. A ws:// upgrade then gets
exactly the answer of any unserved request: 404, or the -publicfallback
site. A probe cannot tell the endpoint exists (IsP2PWebSocketRequest is
false for it, so every caller, including the fallback decision, treats
it as an unknown path).

Trusted proxies (-trustedproxy, as resolved by the existing PROXY and
X-Forwarded-For handling) keep TLS termination working. A connection
counts as TLS when:

- TLS ended at this node; or
- a trusted proxy's PROXY v2 header carries the PP2_TYPE_SSL TLV with
  PP2_CLIENT_SSL (new: proxy_protocol::Header::client_tls; v1 headers
  cannot say, and truncated TLVs are not believed); or
- the HTTP request comes from a trusted proxy (after any PROXY header)
  and the last X-Forwarded-Proto value, the one the nearest proxy set,
  is "https".

Nothing from an untrusted address is believed: its X-Forwarded-Proto is
ignored, and a PROXY header from it is not read at all (as before).
Behind an L4 proxy sending PROXY, the HTTP comes from the client itself,
so only the TLV counts. PROXY headers are not supported on the shared
P2P port (see the previous commit).

Outbound: -onlynet=wss means WebSocket over TLS. A ws:// dial (not to
an .onion host) now needs ipv4 or ipv6 in -onlynet, by the host's
address family (names: either), so -onlynet=wss alone never dials
unencrypted ws://, nor raw P2P (the earlier commit). Without -onlynet
nothing changes; -onlynet without wss already refused all WebSocket
dials. -onlynet's help says so.

Evidence:
- proxy_protocol_tests/v2_ssl_tlv: the TLV alone, after other TLVs, with
  sub-TLVs, IPv4 and IPv6; no PP2_CLIENT_SSL, truncated TLVs and v1 give
  no TLS.
- p2p_websocket_require_tls.py (new): defaults accept ws:// and wss:// on
  the P2P port, -publicbind and the RPC port; with -p2prequiretls=1
  ws:// gets 404 on all three while wss:// upgrades and Python wss peers
  handshake on the P2P port and -publicbind; from a trusted proxy,
  "X-Forwarded-Proto: https" (and "http, https") is accepted on the P2P
  port and -publicbind, "http" and "https, http" refused; a PROXY v2 SSL
  TLV is accepted, PROXY v2 without it refused, also with an
  X-Forwarded-Proto from the client behind it; from an untrusted address
  the same headers and PROXY header are refused; with -publicfallback a
  ws:// upgrade gets the fallback site; -onlynet=wss refuses ws:// and raw
  dials to loopback and connects wss://, while ws:// works without
  -onlynet.
- Passing after this change: all p2p_websocket_*, interface_http*,
  p2p_listen_options, feature_p2p_privacy_recipes, feature_proxy.

Not tested: real CDNs or load balancers (HAProxy/NLB TLVs are built by
hand from the PROXY v2 specification); Forwarded (RFC 7239) headers,
which are not read; outbound -p2prequiretls (it is inbound only;
-onlynet=wss covers outbound).

records.message:
doc: describe the P2P transport switches, the shared P2P port and TLS-only nodes

Operators need one place that says what -listen, -p2prawlisten and
-p2pwslisten accept together, how the P2P port tells raw P2P from
WebSocket, and how to run a WebSocket-only or TLS-only node.

doc/p2p-websocket.md:
- the -listen/-p2prawlisten/-p2pwslisten matrix, with whether the P2P
  port is bound;
- the shared P2P port: classification by first bytes, what is served
  there over HTTP/TLS (only the P2P WebSocket path; 404 or
  -publicfallback otherwise), limits and timeouts, PROXY headers read
  there only with raw P2P disabled, the one default behaviour change, and that a peer knowing
  only an IP address is not made to try wss:// on the same port;
- -p2prawlisten=0: no raw P2P inbound or advertisement, refused
  Tor/I2P/-externalip options and why, outbound unchanged;
- -p2prequiretls and how trusted proxies vouch for TLS;
- -onlynet=wss: no manual raw P2P, no unencrypted ws://;
- recipes: WebSocket-only node (-p2prawlisten=0 -onlynet=wss) and
  TLS-only node (-p2prawlisten=0 -p2prequiretls=1 -onlynet=wss), with the
  caveat that a TLS-terminating proxy's hop to the node is unencrypted
  and that only proxies setting or overwriting X-Forwarded-Proto may be
  trusted;
- table rows for the new options; "raw P2P" replaces "plain TCP".

doc/release-notes.md: the new options and the shared P2P port, described
as new features (ecashd is unreleased: no migration notes).

Evidence: test/lint/check-doc.py reports every option documented; the
recipes' option combinations are those exercised by p2p_listen_options,
p2p_websocket_p2p_port and p2p_websocket_require_tls.

peers.

records.subject: contrib: HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 benchmark driver and load generator
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
contrib: HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 benchmark driver and load generator

To compare HTTP/1.1 with HTTP/2 on the node's TLS port, and a base build
with an HTTP/2 build, with the same tools, before HTTP/2 exists:

- contrib/bench/http2/httpload.c: a closed-loop load generator in C over
  OpenSSL, HTTP/1.1 (N keep-alive connections, one request in flight each)
  or, when built with nghttp2, HTTP/2 (N connections x S streams). One
  thread per connection, latency per request, only 200s count; prints one
  JSON object. Python clients are too slow to load the server at these
  rates (tens of thousands of requests per second).
- contrib/bench/http2/run.py: builds httpload (HTTP/1.1 only if pkg-config
  does not find libnghttp2), starts a regtest node per --bitcoind in a
  fresh datadir, builds a large block with the wallet, then runs small RPCs
  (getblockcount: 64 HTTP/1.1 connections; 4 x 16 and 1 x 64 HTTP/2 streams)
  and large replies (getblock <hash> 2: 4 HTTP/1.1 connections; 1 x 4
  HTTP/2 streams) in interleaved rounds, and reports medians with the load
  average around each run. HTTP/2 workloads are skipped for nodes that do
  not select ALPN h2, so the base is measured by the same command.
- README.md documents the workloads, requirements and output.

Binaries, ports and the work directory are arguments; nothing is
hard-coded.

How to reproduce:
  # build the node(s) as usual (wallet enabled), e.g. in build/
  contrib/bench/http2/run.py --bitcoind build/src/bitcoind \
      --rounds 3 --seconds 10 --port-base 36500
  # optionally a second build to compare: add --bitcoind other/src/bitcoind
Expected output: a line per run, e.g.
  round 1 node0 small-h1: 56118 req/s, p50 1.11 ms, p99 1.59 ms, errors 0, load 22.2->22.8
then a Markdown table "| node | workload | median req/s | median p50 ms |
median p99 ms | MB/s | errors | load avg (1 min) |".

Evidence: on the base tree (no HTTP/2) a 1-round smoke run printed the
HTTP/1.1 rows and skipped the HTTP/2 ones (node reported "h2: no"). Not
tested: Linux, and clients on a different machine than the node.

records.message:
build: add nghttp2 for HTTP/2 (depends package, ENABLE_HTTP2)

Boost.Beast has no HTTP/2. nghttp2 provides the HTTP/2 framing, HPACK and
flow control as a C library with no I/O and no TLS, so the node can drive
it from its own Asio connections and TLS sessions (the deprecated
libnghttp2_asio is not used). This commit only adds the dependency.

- depends/packages/nghttp2.mk: nghttp2 1.70.0, the latest release
  (2026-07-29), library only (--enable-lib-only: no applications, examples,
  HPACK tools, HTTP/3 or Python) and static, with every optional dependency
  disabled so nothing is picked up from the build host. Selected by default;
  NO_HTTP2=1 skips it, like NO_ZMQ.
- CMake: ENABLE_HTTP2 (default OFF) requires nghttp2 >= 1.68.1 through a
  new FindNGHTTP2 module (pkg-config, Homebrew prefix, version read from
  nghttp2ver.h). Native builds use the system library. ENABLE_HTTP2 is
  exported to bitcoin-config.h and to the functional tests' config.ini.
- doc/http2.md starts with the build options and the CVE list.

Security: 1.68.1 is the oldest release with every library fix in the
nghttp2 advisories and the NVD; 1.70.0 covers CVE-2026-27135 (1.68.1),
CVE-2024-28182 CONTINUATION flood (1.61.0), CVE-2023-44487 Rapid Reset
(1.57.0), CVE-2023-35945 (1.55.1), CVE-2020-11080 (1.41.0),
CVE-2019-9511/9513 (1.39.2), CVE-2018-1000168 (1.31.1), CVE-2016-1544
(1.7.1) and CVE-2015-8659 (1.6.0). CVE-2026-58055 is in the nghttpx proxy,
which is not built.

Evidence:
- The tarball's SHA-256 (aa317e2c...b9b3ded5) was computed locally from the
  official GitHub release download and matches the digest GitHub publishes
  for that asset.
- `make nghttp2 HOST=aarch64-linux-gnu` in a Debian 12 arm64 container
  fetched, verified, configured and built the package; the cached package
  contains only include/nghttp2/{nghttp2.h,nghttp2ver.h},
  lib/libnghttp2.a (410 exported nghttp2_* functions) and libnghttp2.pc
  (Version 1.70.0).
- `make print-packages` lists nghttp2, and does not with NO_HTTP2=1.
- macOS configure with -DENABLE_HTTP2=ON finds Homebrew's libnghttp2 1.70.0
  and defines ENABLE_HTTP2; a test project pointing FindNGHTTP2 at headers

x86_64 Linux hosts, and a full node build against the depends library.

records.subject: http: serve HTTP/2 on TLS listeners with nghttp2
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
http: serve HTTP/2 on TLS listeners with nghttp2

Browsers, HTTP clients and load balancers prefer HTTP/2 over TLS, and it
lets one connection carry many concurrent requests. With HTTP/2 built
(ENABLE_HTTP2) and -http2 on (default 1 in such builds), the TLS listeners
(the RPC port's TLS side and -publicbind) select ALPN h2 before http/1.1
when the client offers it. Plain-text listeners stay HTTP/1.1 only: no
h2c upgrade and no prior-knowledge cleartext HTTP/2, which no browser
speaks and which would put a second protocol on unauthenticated
connections for no client we need. Public listeners with -publicfallback
do not offer h2, since that relay passes HTTP/1.1 bytes through unchanged.

Design:
- http2::ServerSession (src/http2_server.{h,cpp}) wraps an nghttp2 server
  session without any I/O: bytes in through Receive(), frames out through
  Collect(). Requests and responses stay Boost.Beast messages: a stream
  becomes an http::request presented as HTTP/1.1 (version 11, :authority as
  Host, cookie fields joined per RFC 9113 8.2.3), and an http::response is
  sent with hop-by-hop fields (Connection, Keep-Alive, Transfer-Encoding,
  Upgrade, Proxy-Connection) dropped. Bodies of 4 KiB or more are framed
  with NGHTTP2_DATA_FLAG_NO_COPY: DATA frame headers are written in front of
  slices of the response body itself, which is kept alive until the write
  completes; smaller bodies are copied. Large replies use DATA frames as big
  as the peer allows.
- H2Connection (httpserver.cpp) drives it on the connection's strand over
  our existing OpenSSL stream (OsslStream): a reader feeds bytes in, a
  writer sends batches of up to 256 KiB (directly while the socket takes
  them, then asynchronously), and each request runs as its own coroutine
  through the code HTTP/1.1 uses, now factored out as ForwardedClient(),
  EndpointAllowed() and RouteRequest(): -trustedproxy X-Forwarded-For,
  health endpoints, -rpcallowip, public listener rules (only /p2p/ws and
  /chronik), Chronik in process, the registered handlers with their
  authentication, zstd, HEAD, metrics. HTTP/2 requests are queued without
  a per-connection strand so streams of one connection run concurrently
  (HTTP/1.1 requests of a connection are sequential anyway); the
  -rpcworkqueue limit applies as before (503 when full). A reply with
  Connection: close (shutdown) sends GOAWAY.
- Limits with built-in defaults (configurable in a later commit): 100
  concurrent streams, 16 KiB header lists (431 beyond), the RPC body limit
  (413, then RST_STREAM NO_ERROR once the reply is sent: an earlier reset
  would make nghttp2 drop the reply), RST_STREAM rate limit 200 burst /
  33 per second (Rapid Reset), 8 CONTINUATION frames, 16 KiB frames,
  1 MiB stream / 8 MiB connection receive windows, no server push.
  -rpcservertimeout: idle connections (no handler running, no progress)
  get GOAWAY and are closed one timeout later; a stream whose request is
  still arriving after that long is reset.
- tls::AllowServerAlpnH2() marks per connection whether h2 may be
  selected; the selection callback prefers h2, then http/1.1 (server
  preference via SSL_select_next_proto, the same API on OpenSSL 1.1.1 and
  3.x). Classic CONNECT gets 405, as on HTTP/1.1.

Evidence (macOS arm64, Homebrew nghttp2 1.70.0 and OpenSSL 3, Release):
- http2_tests (14 cases, a real nghttp2 client in memory): request mapping,
  bodies over many DATA frames, NO_COPY and copied replies, HEAD,
  out-of-order replies on 10 streams, late replies after RST_STREAM, 431,
  413, 405, advertised SETTINGS, bounded output batches, and abuse: a
  client exceeding the acknowledged stream limit gets GOAWAY
  PROTOCOL_ERROR, 20 CONTINUATION frames get GOAWAY, rapid open+reset is
  cut off with GOAWAY after the burst, a bad preface closes.
- interface_http2.py (Python h2 as an independent client): ALPN h2; RPC
  with valid, wrong and missing credentials (200/401/401); 32 RPCs
  multiplexed on one connection; REST, HEAD, 404, 405; /livez; zstd replies
  decode to the plain reply; X-Forwarded-For from the trusted proxy gives
  403 for an address outside -rpcallowip; Chronik over h2 byte-identical
  to Chronik over HTTP/1.1; the public listener answers 404 to RPC, wallet,
  REST and GET /p2p/ws over h2 and serves Chronik; HTTP/1.1-only clients
  still get http/1.1; the plain port answers the HTTP/2 preface with 400
  and ignores an h2c upgrade; with -http2=0 h2 is never selected.
- p2p_websocket_tls_profile.py now expects h2 to be selected in HTTP/2
  builds (http/1.1 otherwise). interface_http, interface_http_publicbind,
  interface_http_trusted_proxy, interface_http_public_fallback,
  interface_http_tls_certs, interface_http_metrics, interface_rpc,
  chronik_rpc_port_proxy, p2p_websocket_tls and the httpserver and
  net_websocket unit tests pass unchanged.

Not tested: OpenSSL 1.1.1 (same ALPN calls; only built against 3.x),
Linux, Windows, h2 through real load balancers, browsers. 100-continue is
not sent over HTTP/2 (clients send the body anyway). Expect the machine's
load average (about 90 on 18 cores) to have hidden timing issues.

records.subject: http: configurable HTTP/2 limits, abuse tests and a fuzz target
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
http: configurable HTTP/2 limits, abuse tests and a fuzz target

The HTTP/2 connection limits had fixed values. Operators need to tune
them (a node serving many browser tabs needs more streams; a node behind a
hostile network wants less), so each becomes an option, checked at startup
(an out-of-range value refuses to start, like other HTTP options):

  -http2maxstreams (100), -http2maxheaderlistsize (16384),
  -http2maxcontinuations (8), -http2maxframesize (16384),
  -http2streamwindow (1 MiB), -http2connwindow (8 MiB),
  -http2resetburst (200), -http2resetrate (33/s)

doc/http2.md documents each limit, what is fixed (body limit, no push,
nghttp2's own SETTINGS/PING/glitch flood limits, 256 KiB write batches),
and that the server has no per-IP connection limit for either protocol.

A deadline reset now counts as connection activity: an idle GOAWAY in the
same deadline tick replaced the queued RST_STREAM, so the client saw the
connection end instead of the stream reset.

Fuzz target http2_server: arbitrary client bytes (usually after the
connection preface) into http2::ServerSession with a real nghttp2 session
and fuzzed limits; between chunks the input decides whether to answer
requests (empty to 20 KB bodies, HEAD, Connection: close), accept or
refuse extended CONNECTs, consume, echo or end tunnel bytes, reset streams
and shut down, so the adapter's stream bookkeeping is exercised together
with nghttp2's parser.

Evidence:
- interface_http2_limits.py against a running node with tight limits:
  SETTINGS advertise them; a 3000-byte header gets 431 and the connection
  keeps serving; opening and resetting streams ends the connection with
  GOAWAY after 21 resets (burst 20); 50 CONTINUATION frames end it without
  any response; exceeding the acknowledged stream limit gives GOAWAY
  PROTOCOL_ERROR; a request without END_STREAM is reset with CANCEL after
  -rpcservertimeout (3 s); an idle connection then gets GOAWAY NO_ERROR;
  after each abuse a new connection still serves RPC; out-of-range values
  of four options refuse to start.
- http2_tests still pass; interface_http2.py passes.
- Fuzzing: see the series README (run with an ASan/UBSan/libFuzzer build
  and a sanitizer-instrumented nghttp2).

Not tested: limits under real concurrent load from many clients; the
glitch limiter's interaction with legitimate busy clients.

records.subject: http: WebSockets over HTTP/2 (RFC 8441 extended CONNECT)
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
http: WebSockets over HTTP/2 (RFC 8441 extended CONNECT)

A client that negotiated h2 cannot send an HTTP/1.1 Upgrade on that
connection, so without extended CONNECT it could not open the P2P
WebSocket (or Chronik's) at all. HTTP/2 connections now advertise
SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL = 1 and accept
:method CONNECT / :protocol websocket for /p2p/ws and /chronik/ws, under
the rules of the HTTP/1.1 upgrade: -rpcallowip on RPC listeners, public
prefixes on -publicbind, upgrade tokens (Authorization: Bearer or the t=
cookie), -trustedproxy addresses, and the P2P sub-protocol negotiation
(p2p-zstd-v1, p2p-zstd, none). permessage-deflate is not offered over
HTTP/2.

- H2Tunnel turns an accepted stream into an Asio AsyncStream. Reads hand
  out the client's DATA and reopen its window only by what they hand out
  (http2::ServerSession consumes tunnel bytes on delivery, unlike request
  bodies); writes become DATA frames and wait while 256 KiB are queued for
  the client's window. Bytes already received with the CONNECT are kept.
- P2P: CConnman polls sockets, so it gets one end of a socketpair holding
  an ordinary WebSocketSock (server role, plain byte layer): WebSocket
  framing, zstd and back-pressure are the existing code (patch 087). The
  HTTP/2 connection pumps the WebSocket bytes between the other end and the
  stream. Ending the stream disconnects the peer; disconnecting the peer
  ends the stream. getpeerinfo shows websocket.alpn "h2". Unlike the
  HTTP/1.1 handoff, these peers share the HTTP/2 connection, so they cross
  the HTTP I/O threads and end when the HTTP server stops. Platforms
  without AF_UNIX socketpairs (Windows) answer 501.
- Chronik: Beast's WebSocket stream runs on the tunnel unchanged
  (InProcessWsSession). Its server handshake needs an HTTP/1.1 upgrade, so
  the CONNECT is presented as one (GET, Upgrade, our own random key); the
  101 it writes is captured and becomes the HTTP/2 200 response with the
  handshake's other fields (e.g. CORS), anything else is sent as that
  status. Beast's teardown and close_socket customization points end the
  stream.
- Refusals: 501 for another :protocol, 400 without
  Sec-WebSocket-Version 13 or when Chronik refuses the upgrade, 503 while
  P2P or Chronik is not ready or the server is stopping, 403/404 for
  paths not served as over HTTP/1.1 (no tunnel is opened). A connection
  with open tunnels is not idle.

Evidence:
- http2_connect_tests (5 cases): SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL only when
  enabled, and a :protocol request is rejected otherwise; a tunnel carries
  bytes both ways repeatedly and both half-closes close the stream; a
  client is held at the stream window until bytes are consumed, then
  200 KB arrive intact; a reset tunnel with unconsumed bytes returns its
  connection window, so a 30 KB request on a 64 KiB connection window
  still arrives; a refused CONNECT gets its status.
- interface_http2_websocket.py (Python h2 with its own WebSocket framing

records.subject: net: offer h2 when dialing wss:// peers and open the WebSocket over HTTP/2
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: offer h2 when dialing wss:// peers and open the WebSocket over HTTP/2

Browsers offer ALPN "h2, http/1.1"; our dialer offered http/1.1 only, which
sets its TLS handshakes apart (patch 098's browser-like profile documented
this gap). Now, when HTTP/2 is built (ENABLE_HTTP2) and -http2 is on (the
default), the dialer offers h2 first, exactly like Chrome. Without HTTP/2
built, or with -http2=0, it keeps offering only http/1.1: h2 is never
offered without the ability to speak it.

If the server selects http/1.1, nothing changes. If it selects h2, the
dialer:
- starts an HTTP/2 connection (Http2ClientLayer, src/http2_client.*, on
  nghttp2) and waits for the server's SETTINGS;
- requires SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL = 1 (RFC 8441 3), else gives up
  on this dial (logged);
- sends :method CONNECT, :protocol websocket, :path from the URL,
  Sec-WebSocket-Version 13, the offered Sec-WebSocket-Protocol list, the
  upgrade token as Authorization: Bearer, and its User-Agent;
- requires 200, no extensions and an offered (or no) sub-protocol, as for
  HTTP/1.1.
The connection is then an ordinary WebSocketSock (client role) whose byte
layer is Http2ClientLayer over the TLS layer: P2P framing, zstd and
WebSocketSock's back-pressure are unchanged, and the WebSocket bytes travel
in DATA frames. The layer accepts up to 1 MiB ahead of the server's flow
control window; new WebSocketByteLayer hooks (HasPendingWrite,
FlushBuffered) let WebSocketSock report those bytes to CConnman, which
polls for the event they wait on (readable, for a WINDOW_UPDATE) and
flushes them. Reads fetch more only after what was decoded was returned.
Our receive windows are 4 MiB (stream) and 16 MiB (connection); push is
refused. Shutdown sends GOAWAY and close_notify. Log lines keep the
"WebSocket upgrade to <host>" wording, with "(HTTP/2)".

tls::NewContext() and ReloadingClientContext take the h2 offer as a
parameter (default off, so other users are unchanged).

Evidence:
- http2_client_tests: the client layer against http2::ServerSession over a
  socketpair (no TLS) with 32 KiB socket buffers and 64 KiB HTTP/2
  windows: SETTINGS, extended CONNECT and 200, 3 MB up while the server
  consumes and 3 MB down, byte for byte, then END_STREAM reads as EOF; a
  server without RFC 8441 is recognized before any CONNECT.
- p2p_websocket_http2.py, node to node over wss:// on -publicbind: ALPN h2
  on both sides (getpeerinfo), IBD of 250 blocks over HTTP/2, 15 x 85 kB
  transactions each way through the server's 64 KiB windows without
  compression (about 1.2 MB of WebSocket bytes each way) and their blocks;
  disconnecting ends the tunnel on both sides; a dialer with -http2=0 and a
  server with -http2=0 both fall back to HTTP/1.1.
- p2p_websocket_tls_profile.py: the dialer's ClientHello selects h2 from a
  server offering h2 and http/1.1 (HTTP/2 builds; http/1.1 otherwise), and
  node to node agrees on h2.
- All other p2p_websocket_* tests, interface_http_publicbind and the
  net_websocket unit tests pass.

Not tested: dialing third-party HTTP/2 servers or proxies (Cloudflare,
nginx) that implement RFC 8441, OpenSSL 1.1.1, Windows, and the TLS
fingerprint of the new offer against JA3/JA4 databases.

records.subject: bench: measure serving one block to many P2P WebSocket peers
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
bench: measure serving one block to many P2P WebSocket peers

Serving a block to many WebSocket peers costs per peer: the block's
serialization (when it is the most recent block) or disk read, its P2P
checksum, and the p2p-zstd-v1 stream compression. Add tools to measure
this, so that a change to block serving can be compared with its base on
the same fixture with the same tool:

- src/bench/ws_block_serve.cpp (bitcoin-bench -filter='WsServe.*'):
  per-peer block serialization, P2P checksum, stream compression and
  decompression, for ~1, 8 and 31.9 MB blocks of P2PKH-shaped
  transactions with random keys, signatures and hashes.
- contrib/bench/ws-block-frames/serve_ab.py: interleaved A/B runner.
  It builds a regtest fixture once (one fresh block per cell, submitted
  with submitblock), then for each round and cell (block size x peer
  count) starts each build on an APFS clone of it, alternating which
  goes first. All peers connect, handshake, then request the same block
  at the same moment. Per serve it records the node process's CPU time
  (proc_pid_rusage, or /proc on Linux), wall time until every peer has
  the whole block (checked by SHA256), and the bytes the node put on the
  wire (getnettotals), plus metric deltas with -metrics. It writes
  results.jsonl and SUMMARY.md (median, min-max, B/A ratio of medians).
- contrib/bench/ws-block-frames/peers.py: the peers, asyncio
  connections in several client processes. WebSocket peers decode the
  zstd stream with the P2P dictionary as a real peer would; raw TCP is
  supported too (--transport=tcp).

The scripts take the two builds as arguments; nothing is hard-coded.
Nodes use ports 41604/41605 unless --rpcport/--port say otherwise.

How to reproduce:

    cmake -GNinja -S <tree> -B <build> -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -DBUILD_BITCOIN_QT=OFF
    ninja -C <build> bitcoind bitcoin-bench          # for both trees
    python3 contrib/bench/ws-block-frames/serve_ab.py \
        --base <base-build> --patched <patched-build> --output <dir> \
        --sizes 1,8,32 --peers 8,32,64 --rounds 5
    <build>/src/bench/bitcoin-bench -filter='WsServe.*'

serve_ab.py prints one line per serve ("round 0 A 8MB-32: cpu 0.912s
wall 0.981s wire 220519104 ok=True ['p2p-zstd-v1']") and ends with a
Markdown table per cell: "| Block | Peers | Metric | A median (min-max)
| B median (min-max) | B/A | n |".

On a loaded Apple M5 Max (18 CPUs, load average ~30-60 from other
work), per MB of block: serialization 0.21 ms, checksum 0.37 ms, stream
compression 2.6 ms, decompression 0.27 ms. Stream compression dominates
what a node spends per WebSocket peer.

Not done: no Linux run (the /proc CPU reader is untested), no TLS (ws://
only), no WAN conditions; the fixture is not a mainnet sample.

records.subject: net: compress blocks once for zstd P2P WebSocket peers
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: compress blocks once for zstd P2P WebSocket peers

A p2p-zstd-v1 WebSocket connection compresses one zstd stream per
direction. Its output depends on the connection's history, so a block
sent to N WebSocket peers is compressed N times. Compression is most of
what a node spends per WebSocket peer when it serves a block (2.2-2.7
ns/byte against 0.2 for serialization and 0.4 for the checksum), so a new
tip served to many peers costs N times that.

Port the V2 tier's independent block frames (V2 patch 095, "[v2 only]
net: cache dictionary-versioned independent compressed block frames") to
the eCash tier as part of its existing compressed WebSocket protocol.
Both p2p-zstd-v1 and p2p-zstd support independent frames without another
subprotocol or feature negotiation.

- Format (as V2): an unfragmented binary message with RSV2 only, payload
  [format 1][dictionary version LE32][one zstd frame with its content
  size], compressed with only the dictionary. Version 1 is the existing
  p2p-zstd-v1 dictionary. It decompresses to whole P2P messages and
  neither uses nor changes the stream state.
- Decoder: V2's strict validation: unknown format or dictionary
  version, skippable, concatenated, trailing or truncated data, missing
  or over-limit content size, and a declared window above 1 MiB (checked
  before allocating) are fatal, and nothing is appended on error.
- Sender: WebSocketSock follows the outgoing P2P message framing (CConnman
  sends a header with MSG_MORE, then the payload) and sends `block`
  messages of at least -p2pcompressoncethreshold bytes (default 65536,
  header included; 0 never sends frames but still accepts them) as one
  independent frame, after framing whatever precedes them. A header split
  by a flush, or any other unusual send pattern, falls back to the stream;
  the P2P bytes delivered are the same either way.
- Cache: one LRU shared by all peers (net_zstd_independent.*), bounded by
  the allocated bytes of its frames (-p2pcompressoncecache, MiB, default
  128) and 64 blocks. Keys include the block hash, full double-SHA256
  payload digest, exact P2P header and dictionary version. Encode accepts
  arbitrary payloads, so the header's 32-bit checksum cannot substitute for
  a payload digest. A mismatch regression holds the entire header fixed
  while changing body bytes and verifies distinct decoded frames.
  Peers asking for a block while
  it is being compressed wait for that compression (a shared future, not
  V2's cache-wide lock), so unrelated blocks and hits are not blocked.
- Metrics (lotus_, this tier's prefix): frames sent/received, cache hits,
  misses, evictions, bytes, entries and compress-once encodes.
  getpeerinfo shows frames sent/received per WebSocket peer.
- doc/p2p-websocket.md documents the eCash rule in place of V2's "not
  suitable for the eCash tier" note.

Evidence:

- Focused unit coverage: stream history across frames, fresh-peer decoding,
  invalid RSV combinations, strict validation, message limits, cache
  bounds, identity, eviction and concurrent requests; mixed zstd/plain
  peers; split headers, multi-call payloads, thresholds and client frames.
- p2p_websocket_compress_once.py: three zstd peers, one uncompressed
  WebSocket peer and raw TCP receive identical block bytes; one encode,
  one miss, two hits and three independent frames; repeat requests hit;
  both dictionary and dictionary-free zstd peers can send independent frames.
- Original session reported focused unit and related functional tests pass
  after removing negotiation. Final resumed validation is in the delivery
  packet; no broad sweep is performed during recovery.

A/B (contrib/bench/ws-block-frames, previous commit): A = base, B = this
commit. These historical measurements used the earlier handshake token
on B and the existing token on A; removing the extra token leaves the
compression algorithm unchanged. The corrected full-payload cache key
adds per-request hashing; these historical A/B numbers do not measure
that correction. ws://, regtest blocks of ~225-byte
P2PKH-shaped transactions with random keys/signatures/hashes. Medians of
5 interleaved rounds (order alternating), Apple M5 Max, 18 CPUs, shared
with other agents' builds (1-minute load average 45-65 throughout):

    block peers | node CPU ms A -> B (B/A) | wall ms A -> B (B/A) | wire MB A / B
     1 MB    8 |    22.4 ->     8.5 (0.38) |    25.6 ->     9.4 (0.37) | 5.1 / 5.1
     1 MB   32 |    98.1 ->    27.4 (0.28) |    98.2 ->    28.3 (0.29) | 20.3 / 20.3
     1 MB   64 |   191.1 ->    59.0 (0.31) |   220.8 ->    57.1 (0.26) | 40.6 / 40.6
     8 MB    8 |   170.8 ->    62.4 (0.37) |   198.9 ->    66.8 (0.34) | 40.8 / 40.8
     8 MB   32 |   722.4 ->   204.7 (0.28) |  1429.2 ->   213.6 (0.15) | 163.4 / 163.3
     8 MB   64 |  1471.2 ->   395.4 (0.27) |  2751.1 ->   521.7 (0.19) | 326.8 / 326.7
    32 MB    8 |   703.1 ->   256.0 (0.36) |  1176.5 ->   269.0 (0.23) | 164.3 / 164.3
    32 MB   32 |  2980.0 ->   827.5 (0.28) |  5463.2 ->  1139.1 (0.21) | 657.2 / 657.0
    32 MB   64 |  6072.0 ->  1693.9 (0.28) | 11669.6 ->  2175.4 (0.19) | 1314.3 / 1314.0

Min-max ranges (in the bench output) do not overlap for node CPU in any
cell; wall-time ranges are wide under this load (e.g. 32 MB/64 peers: A
7.5-16.6 s, B 1.3-4.7 s). Wire bytes are the same: one block compressed
alone with the dictionary is as small as in a fresh stream. Metrics show
exactly one encode and N-1 hits per serve. Per-peer encoding
(bitcoin-bench WsServe*PerPeer): 2.5-3.3 ns/byte for the stream against
0.02 ns/byte to copy the cached frame. What remains per frames peer is
mostly the block's disk read and checksum (next commit).

How to reproduce: build the previous commit and this one (Release), then
from this tree

    python3 contrib/bench/ws-block-frames/serve_ab.py \
        --base <previous-build> --patched <this-build> --output <dir> \
        --sizes 1,8,32 --peers 8,32,64 --rounds 5
    <this-build>/src/bench/bitcoin-bench -filter='WsServe.*'

A median (min-max) | B median (min-max) | B/A | n |".

Not tested: TLS (wss://) serving under load, Linux and other platforms,
sanitizers, the full functional suite, real WAN peers or mainnet blocks. Frames
are not yet used for other large messages (blocktxn, headers), which
stay in the stream. Server-role peers still copy the cached frame into

The V2 tier can later rebase its patch 095 onto this shared code

net_processing: serialize and checksum a served block once for all peers

When many peers ask for the same block (a new tip), each request reads
the block from disk (or serializes the most recent block) and computes
its double-SHA256 checksum again in V1TransportSerializer. On this host
that is 0.2 ms/MB to serialize (or a page-cache read) plus 0.4 ms/MB to
hash, per peer. After compress-once (previous commit) it is most of what
a node spends per WebSocket frames peer, and it is most of what it
spends per raw TCP peer.

Keep the serialized payloads of recently served blocks with their
checksums (BlockMessageCache, net_block_message_cache.h), for blocks of
at least 64 KiB, bounded by -blockmessagecache (MiB, default 64, 0
disables) and 4 entries. Further peers get a copy of the bytes and the
known checksum (new CSerializedNetMsg::m_checksum, used by
prepareForTransport when set). The bytes are those on disk and on the
wire for that block hash, from validated storage or the validated most
recent block; requests are still checked (BlockRequestAllowed, pruning,
hasData) before the cache is consulted. Filtered and compact block
requests are unchanged. Metrics: lotus_p2p_block_message_cache_hits_total
and _misses_total.

Each peer still copies the payload into its send queue (vSendMsg owns
vectors); sharing one buffer would need changes to CConnman's send
queue and was not attempted.
