contrib: add transaction relay measurement tools

Changing transaction relay needs numbers from real nodes, measured the same
way before and after: how long a transaction takes to reach every node,
and how many bytes each node spends on it. The tools take the binary as an
argument, so the relay before Nucleation relay and after it are measured
with one tool; this commit comes first in the series for that reason.

contrib/bench/tx-relay:

- relay_onehop.py: one node, a P2P sender and a P2P observer; the delay
  from handing the node a transaction to its announcement (inv or
  invshort), end to end as the Python peers see it and inside the node
  (from its debug log: accepting the transaction to queueing the
  announcement; the end-to-end figure includes 10-20 ms of the test
  framework's own delay on this machine);
- relay_cluster.py: a regtest cluster of N nodes in a random graph (each
  makes --outbound connections), optionally through a TCP proxy that
  delays each direction of each link by a one-way latency drawn per link
  (--latency MIN-MAX ms; there is no tc on macOS); transactions submitted
  at a fixed rate to random nodes over RPC. Reports time to 50/90/99/100%
  of the nodes (from the nodes' AcceptToMemoryPool log lines, one machine
  so one clock), bytes sent per node per transaction by kind
  (announcement, request, body, reconciliation, other) and by message
  type, duplicate bodies (from the fullnode_txrelay_ metrics when the
  build has them), node CPU per transaction and the load average;
  --silent/--silent-args give a fraction of the nodes extra options, to
  stand for peers that do not relay;
- run_interleaved.py: several variants (binary and options), one round at
  a time, so drift in the machine's load hits all of them; JSON lines out
  and a table of medians with the range over rounds.

All three use the functional test framework of the build directory given
(use the newest tree's, which knows every message either relay sends) and
have a __main__ guard; none uses multiprocessing.

How to reproduce:

  cmake -GNinja .. && ninja           # in build/
  contrib/bench/tx-relay/relay_onehop.py --build-dir build --txs 150
    -> {"load_average": [...], "max_ms": ..., "mean_ms": ...,
        "median_ms": ..., "node_max_ms": ..., "node_median_ms": ...,
        "node_p90_ms": ..., "p90_ms": ..., "txs": 150}
  contrib/bench/tx-relay/relay_cluster.py --build-dir build --nodes 24 \
      --outbound 8 --txs 300 --rate 20 --latency 10-80 --json run.json
    -> one JSON object: propagation_seconds.t50/t90/t99/t100.{median,
       p90,worst}, bytes_per_node_per_tx.{announce,request,body,recon,
       other}, bytes_per_node_per_tx_by_msg, floor_bytes,
       duplicate_bodies_metric, cpu_seconds_per_tx, complete, ...
  contrib/bench/tx-relay/run_interleaved.py --build-dir build --rounds 3 \
      --variant old=/path/to/old/bitcoind --variant new=build/src/bitcoind \
      --out runs.jsonl -- --nodes 24 --outbound 8 --txs 300 --rate 20 \
      --latency 10-80
    -> a markdown table, one row per variant: median [min-max] over rounds

Checked: smoke runs of relay_cluster.py (6 nodes, 20 transactions, 10-30
ms) and relay_onehop.py on the old and the new relay; ruff check and
format. Not checked: Linux (the proxy and ps parsing are POSIX; ps output
formats differ by platform).

records.subject: net: announce transactions on a fixed relay tick
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: announce transactions on a fixed relay tick

Transaction announcements waited for a Poisson timer: inbound peers shared
one timer with a 5 s mean, outbound peers had their own with a 2 s mean, and
high-bandwidth peers had a second 25/50 ms "fast" timer for relayed (not
locally originated) transactions. In the relay simulation (2,000 nodes,
10-80 ms links) these delays account for almost all of the time a
transaction takes to reach every node: 4.7 s median against 0.6 s for the
same flood with a 25 ms tick. Nucleation relay drops the random delays;
origin privacy is to come from wallets submitting through several nodes,
not from relay timing.

Every peer now announces transactions on the same tick, the multiples of
-txrelaytick (default 10 ms, 1-1000 ms) on the monotonic clock. A peer that
sends at a boundary next sends at the following one, so peers that became
ready at different times within a tick still share its boundary, and under
load the tick is what batches many transactions into one message. The tick
clock is MockableSteadyClock: -mocktime does not affect it, and unit tests
set it directly.

- TxRelay::m_next_inv_send_time (0 = handshake incomplete), the fast timer
  and m_local_inventory_to_send are replaced by m_relay_ready, set by the
  first SendMessages after the handshake (the same point the timer was
  first initialised, so transactions received during the handshake are
  still not queued for the peer), and m_next_tx_tick.
- A scheduler task runs just after each tick boundary and wakes the message
  handler when transaction inventory is waiting. Without it a queued
  announcement could wait up to the handler's 100 ms poll timeout.
- Proof announcements keep their Poisson timers (out of scope); the
  inbound/outbound interval constants remain for them, FAST_* go.
- The high-bandwidth shorttx push of 16 or more transactions is unchanged,
  except that it now waits for the tick like everything else.

Tests: new txrelay_tests (tick alignment, two peers sharing one boundary,
nothing before the boundary, nothing twice). Three v2_protocol_handler
tests that advanced mocktime to fire the Poisson timers now advance the
tick clock instead; two of them asserted that local or low-bandwidth
bursts wait for the slow timer and now assert that every burst goes at the
tick, pushed only to high-bandwidth peers.

Measured (regtest, one node, a P2P sender and a P2P observer, interleaved
two rounds each, macOS arm64, machine load average 46-80): one-hop delay
from sending a transaction to receiving its INV, median 1.7 / 2.1 ms, p90
9.8 / 10.2 ms, 150 transactions per run (acceptance: median <= tick + 1 ms).
The base binary: median 3.3 / 3.5 s, p90 10.3 / 12.6 s, 30 transactions
per run (inbound peer, 5 s mean timer).

Not tested here: the full functional suite (run once on the finished
series, compared with the base), multi-hop propagation (R10).

records.subject: net: relay transactions to a fan-out of peers through one queue
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: relay transactions to a fan-out of peers through one queue

RelayTransaction and RelayTransactionBatch inserted each transaction into
every peer's m_tx_inventory_to_send (unless the peer's known filter had it),
taking m_peer_mutex and each peer's inventory lock per transaction. Every
node therefore receives every transaction's announcement from about every
neighbour: in the relay simulation announcements, not bodies, are where the
bytes go (~870 bytes per node per transaction at 16 peers, growing with
peers), while a bounded fan-out with the same 10 ms tick reaches every node
almost as fast.

Relaying a transaction now appends {txid, local} to one queue (O(1) per
transaction, its own mutex). At each relay tick the first SendMessages call
drains the queue:

- relay peers are those past the handshake that accept transactions; one
  lock per peer per tick records which queued transactions each lacks (not
  in its known filter, or Avalanche-stalled for it);
- a transaction this node originated (unbroadcast: wallet, RPC) goes to
  every candidate, otherwise to `fanout` candidates picked uniformly, with
  fanout = clamp(max(min, ceil(pct x relay peers)), min, max)
  (-txrelayfanoutmin 8, -txrelayfanoutpct 0.25, -txrelayfanoutmax 32);
- a child also goes to the peers its nearest recently relayed in-mempool
  parent went to (a 50,000-entry route memory), so fan-out does not hand
  a child to a peer that never heard of the parent;
- the chosen transactions are inserted into the peers' inventory; the send
  loop keeps its known-filter check, mempool (topological) order and fee
  filter as before.

The per-send cap of INVENTORY_BROADCAST_MAX_PER_MB x max block MB (and
INVENTORY_BROADCAST_PER_SECOND) becomes a per-peer budget per tick,
ceil(-txrelayratemax x tick), default 250,000 per second (1M TPS x 2 /
fan-out minimum), i.e. 2,500 per 10 ms tick. The excess stays queued for
the next tick; nothing is dropped. The static_assert tying
INVENTORY_MAX_RECENT_RELAY to the old rate goes: at sustained per-peer rates
above 350,000 / 2 min a late getdata may get NOTFOUND; peers that negotiate
short-id announcements (next commit) fetch through getshorttx instead.

Tests: txrelay_tests checks the fan-out formula at its boundaries (n < min,
ceil between min and max, at and above max, floating-point rounding, pct 0
and 1), that 40 peers get each relayed transaction exactly 10 times with
random coverage, originated transactions to all 40, known peers excluded,
children to every peer their parent went to, and the per-tick budget
(25 transactions at 10 per tick: 10, 10, 5). New p2p_tx_relay_fanout.py: a
node with a fan-out of 3 and 12 P2P observers announces each of 20 relayed
transactions to exactly 3 of them and an RPC transaction to all 12; 12
nodes in a ring plus 8 chords all receive 30 transactions entered over
P2P and RPC. p2p_tx_privacy.py passes.

Not tested here: the full functional suite (run once on the finished
series), the orphan rate and bytes per transaction on multi-node clusters
(R10).

records.subject: net: announce transactions by 8-byte short ids to peers that support it
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: announce transactions by 8-byte short ids to peers that support it

An INV entry is 36 bytes (type and txid). Since every node fetches each
body once but hears about it from about fan-out neighbours, announcements
dominate relay bytes; in the relay simulation 8-byte ids take a fan-out-8
network from 678 to 349 bytes per node per transaction.

New messages (stock peers never see them used):

- sendinvshort {uint32 version, uint64 flags}, sent after verack to
  transaction relay peers. Flag 1 = short-id announcements (flag 2 is
  reserved for continuous reconciliation, next commits). A peer that sends
  it back with a flag we support may use that feature towards us. Stock ABC
  peers ignore the unknown post-verack message and keep receiving INVs.
- invshort {uint256 epoch_id, vector<uint64> short_ids}, used instead of
  MSG_TX INV entries towards such peers. Blocks and proofs keep INV.

Short ids use the per-epoch key of set reconciliation:
DeriveEpochSipHashKey(tip hash, tip height), applied with the same SipHash
as the Merklix handler's ComputeMerklixShortId, so one index serves
announcements and (next) reconciliation. The epoch is the chain tip; a new
block starts a new epoch. Every id is derived through
PeerManagerImpl::ShortIdFor(peer, txid), which records the accepted grinding
risk and the per-connection salt option (option b) in its NOTE/TODO
comment, as decided.

txrelay::TxRelayIndex (net/txrelay_index.{h,cpp}) maps short ids to txids
for the current and the previous epoch, so peers on either side of a block
are understood. It is updated when a transaction is queued for relay (so a
transaction is "known" before its first tick), from
TransactionAddedToMempool/RemovedFromMempool, and re-keyed from the mempool
on UpdatedBlockTip (one SipHash per mempool transaction). Colliding ids
keep every transaction under the id and are counted; a short-id request is
answered with all of them.

Receiving invshort: a known id marks the peer as knowing the transaction;
an unknown id becomes an announcement in m_txrequest under a request key
(the short id plus 24 bytes of the epoch id), with its own parameters
(5,000 in flight, 100,000 announcements per peer, the usual 200 ms delay
for non-preferred peers, 2 s expiry so another announcer is tried soon).
Requestable keys are batched into one getshorttx per epoch per peer
(LIVE_MEMPOOL, context = epoch id, the epoch key), recorded as pending in
the Merklix handler so the shorttx answer counts as solicited. Any arrival
of the transaction forgets its short-id announcements.

Merklix handler changes for relay epochs (a LIVE_MEMPOOL context that is a
relay epoch and keyed with its key, via a TxRelayEpochProvider the peer
manager implements):

- getshorttx is answered from the relay index, not by hashing the whole
  mempool per request, and serving clears the unbroadcast flag as a
  getdata does (mempool_unbroadcast.py failed without this);
- getshorttx/shorttx get their own per-peer limit, 1,000 per second: the
  reconciliation limit (32 per second for all sync messages) would drop
  relay traffic that comes every tick;
- solicited bodies take the ordinary tx-message path (ProcessSingleTx), so
  orphan handling, 1p1c packages and reject caches apply; through
  ProcessRawTxBatch, p2p_1p1c_network.py lost its low-fee parents;
- they are not merged into a scoped transaction set.

-txrelayshortids (default 1) turns the feature off; the regtest-only
-txrelaytestshortidbits truncates ids to force collisions in tests.

Tests: txrelay_tests covers the index (epoch rotation, previous epoch kept,
an older one dropped, removal only from the current epoch, the admission
window, forced 4-bit collisions keeping all 50 transactions and counting
them), request keys, and a peer manager that sends invshort only to the
peer that negotiated it (with the tip's epoch key), marks known ids,
requests an unknown one once by getshorttx, serves our ids from the index,
and ignores invshort from a peer that did not negotiate. New
p2p_tx_relay_invshort.py: negotiation with P2P peers, a getshorttx for an
unknown id, four nodes relaying over invshort only (no INV entries for
transactions), and 6-bit ids where relay skips colliding transactions but
a block still brings both nodes to the same tip. Test framework:
msg_sendinvshort, msg_invshort, msg_getshorttx. Also passing:
p2p_tx_relay_fanout, p2p_tx_privacy, rpc_atomic_tx_batch, p2p_feefilter,
p2p_leak_tx, mempool_unbroadcast, p2p_invalid_messages, p2p_1p1c_network,
p2p_opportunistic_1p1c, p2p_orphan_handling, mempool_packages, and the
txrelay, v2_protocol_handler, net, denialofservice and metrics unit suites.

Two existing tests assumed things the new message changes:
p2p_message_capture.py split the 12-byte message-type field at a NUL that
a 12-character type ("sendinvshort") does not have; it now partitions.
p2p_websocket_inbound.py asserted that zstd without a dictionary makes a
bare handshake smaller on the wire; with sendinvshort added after verack,
the base's 461 payload bytes (456 on the wire) became 497 (502). It now
exchanges ten pings first, so the stream has something to compress (the
base binary passes the changed test too).

Not handled: invshort for an epoch we do not know (the sender is a block
ahead, or behind by two) is dropped and left to reconciliation; per-link
salts (decision 5, option b); the index rebuild cost at a 1M-transaction
mempool is not measured here. Not tested here: the full functional suite
(run once on the finished series), bytes per transaction on clusters (R10).

records.subject: net: reconcile recently admitted transactions with peers continuously
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: reconcile recently admitted transactions with peers continuously

With a bounded fan-out, a transaction can stop where every node that
picked a next hop picked a peer that does not relay it on. The eCash tier
already has the complete Merklix set reconciliation (merklixsync, bucket
drill-down with GF(2^64) syndromes, getshorttx/shorttx), but nothing ever
starts it. In the relay simulation, reconciling with one peer every 0.25 s
cuts the worst case with 30% silent nodes from 8.3 s to 1.6 s for almost
no bytes.

Every -txreconinterval (default 250 ms; 0 turns it off) a node sends the
next peer that negotiated reconciliation (sendinvshort flag 2), round robin
by peer id, a LIVE_MEMPOOL Merklix summary whose context is the current
short-id epoch and whose key is that epoch's key. The summarised set is
the transactions admitted in the last -txreconwindow (default 30 s) that
are still in the mempool, not the whole mempool, which keeps the
differences small. The peer runs the existing drill-down and fetches what
it lacks with getshorttx; the bodies take the ordinary transaction path
and are relayed on as non-local. Reconciliation is one way per round: the
receiver pulls what the sender has.

Merklix handler changes, for relay epochs only:

- summaries and bucket requests keyed with a relay epoch's key are valid
  (IsValidReconSipHashKey accepts only the keys DeriveReconSipHashKey
  derives);
- the scoped set of a relay epoch is the reconciliation window (from the
  relay index), so the existing summary/diff code needs no change;
- short ids found "missing" are first checked against the whole relay
  index: a transaction can be in our mempool but outside our window
  (admitted earlier, or at the other edge of the peer's window); those
  are not fetched;
- short ids in summaries are masked like relay ids (all 64 bits outside
  tests).

The existing per-peer limit of 32 sync messages per second applies to the
summaries and drill-down messages on both sides; one summary per peer per
interval x relay peers is far below it.

Tests: txrelay_tests checks round robin (two of three peers negotiated
reconciliation: summaries alternate between exactly those two, one per
250 ms, none within an interval, and the window summary counts the relayed
transaction). The window expiry is covered by the index test of the
previous commit. New p2p_tx_reconciliation.py: six nodes in a ring with a
fan-out of 1, each with three silent P2P peers, 20 transactions entered at
three nodes: all six nodes have all 20 after 0.84 s (one run, load average
about 40); summaries go only to negotiating peers. The same test with
-txreconinterval=0 did not deliver everything within 15 s (one control
run; not kept as a test because the failure is random).
p2p_tx_relay_fanout, p2p_tx_relay_invshort, p2p_1p1c_network and
mempool_unbroadcast pass.

Not tested here: the full functional suite (run once on the finished
series), reconciliation cost at high transaction rates, where window-edge
differences grow with the rate and the drill-down goes deeper (R10).

Follow-up measurement correction (original commit 7cc5db46b4, folded here):

net: cut reconciliation's duplicate bodies and drill-down bytes

The first cluster measurements (relay_cluster.py, 6 nodes, 20
transactions at 10/s, 10-30 ms links, two runs) showed reconciliation
costing far more than it should: 1,109-1,394 bytes per node per
transaction, almost all of it merklixbuck bucket summaries, and 10 of 110
bodies (9%) were duplicates (target: below 1%). Three causes:

- Reconciliation pushed its own getshorttx, outside the transaction
  request tracker, so a transaction found missing by reconciliation and
  announced by a peer was fetched twice. Missing short ids now become
  announcements from the reconciling peer (AddRelayShortIdAnnouncements),
  so one request per transaction is in flight whatever found it.
- The windows are cut by each node's own admission times, so the newest
  transactions, still on their way by announcement, showed up as
  differences every round. The summarised set now leaves out the last two
  reconciliation intervals (500 ms by default).
- A mismatched bucket was drilled into even when we had more than the
  peer there (our own extras at the window edges), and a root mismatch
  with matching buckets drilled into all 16 (the D1 rule, meant for scoped
  sets that must converge exactly). For relay epochs only, a bucket or
  undecodable sub-bucket is drilled into only where the peer has more than
  we do, and the D1 fallback is skipped. A miss hidden by our own extra in
  the same bucket is found in a later round, by this peer or another.

Measured with the same cluster, two runs: reconciliation 163 bytes per
node per transaction (all merklixsync summaries: 4 per second per node,
so the cost per transaction falls as the rate rises), no merklixbuck,
duplicate bodies 0 of 100 in both runs; time to every node 0.54 / 0.72 s
worst (0.34-0.55 s before). p2p_tx_reconciliation.py (fan-out 1, half the
peers silent) delivers everything in 2.38 s, against 0.84 s before: the
grace period and drilling less make recovery slower in that extreme case.

Tests: txrelay_tests' round-robin test now admits its transaction a
second before the rounds (the newest 500 ms are left out). txrelay_tests,
v2_protocol_handler_tests, p2p_tx_reconciliation, p2p_tx_relay_invshort,
p2p_tx_relay_fanout, p2p_1p1c_network and mempool_unbroadcast pass.

Not tested here: the full functional suite (run on the finished series);
higher rates, where the window edges hold more transactions.

net: push transaction bodies to high-bandwidth peers only with -txrelaypushhb

Bursts of 16 or more transactions were pushed as unsolicited shorttx
bodies to every high-bandwidth peer (BIP152 high-bandwidth in either
direction, noban, or -highbandwidthtx). Every such peer then receives the
body whether or not it already has it from someone else. In the relay
simulation pushing to two peers instead of announcing saves about 0.1 s
end to end and costs 1.8 duplicate bodies per node per transaction (+360
bytes); announcing costs no duplicate bodies.

The push now happens only with -txrelaypushhb=1 (default 0); otherwise
those peers get announcements like everyone else (short ids if they
negotiated them). Receiving pushed bodies is unchanged. The measurement
commit decides whether the default should flip back for Avalanche
finalization latency.

bodies by default and 20 pushed bodies with the option. The
v2_protocol_handler tests that check the push path, and
rpc_atomic_tx_batch.py (which asserts "sending shorttx"), now set the
option. lotus_v2_loopback_tps_stress.py still passes -highbandwidthtx=1
only, so it now runs without pushes; it starts bitcoind directly and is
also meant for older binaries, which do not know the new option.
p2p_tx_relay_fanout and p2p_tx_relay_invshort pass.

records.message:
rpc,doc: say that a node's own transactions reveal their origin

Nucleation relay removed the random announcement delays, and a node sends
the transactions it originated (wallet, RPC: the unbroadcast set) to every
relay peer at the next tick (since the fan-out commit), so a fraction of
transactions does not die at a source whose few chosen peers do not relay
it on. Both make the entry node of a transaction easy to see: in the relay
simulation a 10% spy set finds the origin of 75-90% of node-originated
transactions. As decided, privacy is to come from the client instead:
submitting each transaction through several independent nodes.

The sendrawtransaction and submitrawtxbatch help now say so, and the
release notes describe the new relay and its settings. Sending through
several nodes from the wallet PWA is a separate task in that project (not
a daemon change).

Tests: rpc_help.py and rpc_rawtransaction.py pass; test/lint/check-doc.py
passes. That originated transactions go to every peer is tested in
p2p_tx_relay_fanout.py and txrelay_tests (fan-out commit).

records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: transaction relay metrics and structured txrelay logs

Tuning the fan-out, tick and reconciliation, and seeing whether short-id
collisions ever happen (the trigger for per-link salts), needs numbers
from running nodes. The node already has a lock-free Prometheus registry
(-metrics) and typed structured log events; this uses both.

Metrics, all named from one prefix (TXRELAY_METRIC_PREFIX,
"fullnode_txrelay_"; the node's metrics are moving to a neutral fullnode_
namespace, so the plan's lotus_txrelay_ names are superseded and the
prefix is the one line to rebase), labels from fixed small sets only:

- announce_sent_total, announce_recv_total, announce_dup_total, by
  kind="short|full" (invshort ids, inv entries); dup = received for a
  transaction we already had;
- body_recv_total, body_dup_total: bodies through the tx-message path
  (tx messages and short-id responses);
- fanout_peers (histogram): peers each relayed transaction was queued for;
- queue_depth (gauge): transactions drained at the last non-empty tick;
- tick_overrun_total: a tick drained more than a tick late with
  transactions waiting (they still go; nothing is dropped);
- recon_rounds_total, recon_diff (histogram of missing ids per received
  summary or bucket summary), recon_overflow_total (undecodable
  sub-buckets), recon_fetched_total (ids requested because of
  reconciliation);
- shortid_collision_total;
- first_seen_to_announce_seconds (histogram): from queueing a transaction
  for relay to the tick that queues its announcements.

Bytes per message type, and so per kind (announcements, requests, bodies,
reconciliation), were already exported as lotus_p2p_{sent,received}_bytes
by type; invshort and sendinvshort are now message types there.

Logs: a new txrelay debug category with typed events, at most one per tick
or message: txrelay_tick (transactions drained, announcements queued; only
for ticks that had any), peer_invshort_received (peer, ids, new ids),
peer_recon_summary_sent (peer, window size) and
mempool_tx_shortid_collision (txid, short id, transactions already under
it). New log fields: short_id, peers, missing.

Also: a reconciliation round whose window is empty no longer sends a
summary (a peer cannot be missing anything from us then); found while
adding the summary log, which logged "0 transactions" four times a second.

Tests: p2p_tx_reconciliation.py now reads the metrics: recon rounds,
recon-fetched ids, short announcements and bodies are non-zero (one run:
101 rounds, 63 ids fetched by reconciliation, 60 short announcements, 106
bodies of which 6 duplicates, the duplicates coming from a body requested
both by reconciliation and by announcement), and checks the summary log
line. The structured event and field-key lints pass (110 production call
sites). interface_http_metrics, feature_logging, rpc_misc,
p2p_tx_relay_invshort and the metrics, logging, txrelay and
v2_protocol_handler unit suites pass.

Not tested here: the full functional suite (run once on the finished
series); the metrics on clusters under load (R10).

records.message:
contrib: add the transaction relay simulator behind Nucleation relay

The fan-out rule, the 10 ms tick, 8-byte ids and 250 ms reconciliation
were chosen with a relay simulator run outside the tree. Keeping it here
lets the numbers in the commits be rerun, and the defaults retuned against
the same model.

contrib/devtools/relay-sim has the simulator (relay_sim.py), the design
study's experiment tables (relay_experiments.py), the final candidates
(relay_final.py) and a runner for the node's defaults
(relay_node_defaults.py), with a README holding the plan's table and a
rerun with the defaults. Changes from the out-of-tree copy: the node's
fan-out rule as k=(min, pct, max) (same formula as TxRelayFanout,
including its rounding epsilon), NODE_DEFAULTS, a process-count argument
for table(), docstrings, and ruff fixes (no behavioural change). Every
runner using multiprocessing has a __main__ guard: macOS starts workers by
re-importing the script.

Rerun (4 processes, about 7 s): with the node's defaults, 100% of 2,000
nodes reached in 0.71 s median (0.76 s worst) at 349 bytes per node per
transaction; with 30% silent nodes 0.88 s / 1.63 s, never without
reconciliation; the same numbers as the plan's table. A flood on the same
tick with 36-byte ids reaches 100% in 0.48 s at 685 bytes.

Not modelled: queueing, batching, message headers, invshort's epoch field;
the plan's Poisson-timer baseline row comes from the earlier study and is
quoted, not rerun.

records.message:
bench: measure the relay short-id index

Nucleation relay re-keys its short-id index at every block: one SipHash
and two hash-map inserts per mempool transaction. The plan asked for the
cost at a 1M-transaction mempool, and lookups of announced short ids happen
for every announcement received.

New benchmarks (src/bench/txrelay_index.cpp): RelayIndexRekey10k and
RelayIndexRekey1M (one new epoch over a 10,000 / 1,000,000 transaction
mempool, per transaction), RelayIndexAddRemove (index and drop one
transaction at 100,000) and RelayIndexFind (look up a short id, half
present).

Measured (macOS arm64, Release, load average 50-100, three runs; nanobench
flags the small ones as unstable at this load): re-key 133-246 ns per
transaction at 10k and 427-1,357 ns at 1M, i.e. 0.4-1.4 s per block at a
1M-transaction mempool; add+remove 437-539 ns; find 67-202 ns. The
re-keying ran with the index lock held, so a block stalled every lookup
for that long; the next commit builds the new epoch outside the lock.

How to reproduce:

  ninja -C build bitcoin-bench
  build/src/bench/bitcoin-bench -filter='RelayIndex.*'
    -> nanobench table: ns/tx (or ns/op), tx/s, err%, total, benchmark

records.subject: net: build a new relay epoch outside the index lock
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: build a new relay epoch outside the index lock

At a block the short-id index is re-keyed from the whole mempool. That
took the index lock for the whole rebuild: 0.4-1.4 s at a 1M-transaction
mempool (RelayIndexRekey1M, previous commit), during which every invshort
lookup, every transaction queued for relay and every short-id request
waited.

The new epoch is now built in a private structure and swapped in under
the lock; until then the current and previous epochs keep answering.
Insert no longer needs the lock (it is only called on a private epoch or
with the lock held), so it is renamed InsertUnlocked and documented as
such; the collision counter it bumps is a mutable atomic.

Tests: txrelay_tests (index epochs and collisions) pass;
RelayIndexRekey1M still costs 0.4-1.4 s of CPU per block (unchanged: the
same work, outside the lock). Not done: incremental double indexing that
would spread the work over the epoch.

Session recovery correctness repair:

Fixup provenance: a0ba5c282f corrects epoch rebuild races introduced by a4345c1c49.

Mutation tracking now starts before obtaining the mempool snapshot. The
index builds outside its mutex and applies concurrent Add/Remove events
before publication. A separate builder mutex serializes rebuilds; only
builders take it. Snapshot callbacks run without the index mutex, so the
index never nests its mutex across mempool.cs acquisition. No background
thread, condition variable, shutdown waiter, or retry loop is introduced.

The mutation journal stops at 65,536 events. Overflow discards the candidate
and retains the current epoch for retry during the next normal update.
Sustained churn can defer rekeying; this performance case was not measured.
An exception clears active tracking. Initial snapshot admissions are merged
with mutations when seeding the reconciliation window. Benchmark snapshot
providers now copy the supplied data; pre-repair rekey timings therefore do
not measure this new implementation.

Validation: ninja -C build -j2 bitcoind test_bitcoin bitcoin-bench rc0;
10 txrelay_tests pass in 0.83s, covering a deterministic stale snapshot with
Add/Remove, 65,537-event overflow then successful retry, first-epoch window
admissions, and failed-snapshot cleanup. No benchmark or suite rerun.

records.subject: bench: block validation scaling benchmarks and A/B drivers
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
bench: block validation scaling benchmarks and A/B drivers

Two changes planned for this tier (starting a block's coin prefetch early,
off-thread, and hashing large blocks' Merkle trees on several threads)
need base-versus-patched numbers measured the same way on both trees. This
adds the measuring tools first, so the base can be measured with exactly
the tool the patches are measured with.

src/bench/block_validation_scaling.cpp (bench_bitcoin):
- BlockMerkleRoot_{1000,5000,10000,50000,100000}: the single-threaded
  consensus BlockMerkleRoot, with mutation detection, over a synthetic
  block of n transactions.
- CheckBlockMerkleRoot_<same sizes>: the Merkle check of block validation
  (IsBlockMutated, i.e. CheckMerkleRoot, which net_processing runs on
  arrival), recomputed each iteration by clearing the block's cached
  m_checked_merkle_root. A patch changing how validation computes the root
  shows up here under the same name on both trees.
- DeserializeBlock_{1000,10000,100000}: deserializing such a block, which
  lays out every transaction and hashes it for its id.
- HashBlockTxIds_{1000,10000,100000}: the id hashing part alone, so the
  share of deserialization spent hashing can be read off.
- CoinsPrefetchWalk_{100,1000,5000}: CCoinsViewDB::PrefetchOutpointsAsync
  (the sorted MDBX cursor walk plus readahead hints) over random coins of a
  500k-coin in-memory database: the walk's CPU cost on a warm cache.

contrib/bench/block-validation/ (README.md documents all of it):
- ab_microbench.py: interleaved A B A B runs of bench_bitcoin with a
  filter; per benchmark and arm the median over rounds of nanobench's
  median time per unit, the range, and the ratio to the first arm.
- ab_block_connect.py: `fixture` builds a regtest datadir with 2,000,000
  anyone-can-spend coins and 6 test blocks of 10,000 two-input
  transactions spending random coins (any bitcoind of the tier can build
  it, in about 15 s). `run` clones the datadir per round and arm (APFS
  copy-on-write), starts that arm's bitcoind with -dbcache=4
  -debug=bench, evicts chainstate/mdbx.dat from the page cache before each
  block, submits the blocks with submitblock and records submitblock wall
  time and the node's ConnectBlock ("Connect total") and ConnectTip
  ("Connect block") times. --warm reads the database into the cache
  instead, to measure the warm case.
- Eviction without root: `purge` needs root on macOS ("Unable to purge
  disk buffers: Operation not permitted" here), so the driver maps the
  file and calls msync(MS_SYNC | MS_INVALIDATE), which writes back and then
  drops that file's cached pages (vmtouch -e's method), and checks with
  mincore() that nothing stayed resident. Linux uses fdatasync plus
  posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED).
- abstats.py: shared arm parsing, medians/ranges and Markdown tables.
- Arms are NAME=BUILD_DIR_OR_BINARY [extra args]; nothing hard-codes a
  path, and arms of one binary with different options are allowed.

How to reproduce:
  Build both trees (Release; e.g. -GNinja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
  -DBUILD_BITCOIN_QT=OFF), targets bitcoind and bitcoin-bench, in
  $BASE/build and $PATCHED/build. Then from either tree:

  contrib/bench/block-validation/ab_microbench.py \
      --arm base=$BASE/build --arm patched=$PATCHED/build \
      --filter '(CheckBlockMerkleRoot|DeserializeBlock|HashBlockTxIds)_.*' \
      --rounds 7 --min-time 300 --out micro.json
  contrib/bench/block-validation/ab_block_connect.py fixture \
      --bitcoind $BASE/build --dir /tmp/block-connect-fixture
  contrib/bench/block-validation/ab_block_connect.py run \
      --fixture /tmp/block-connect-fixture --rounds 7 \
      --arm base=$BASE/build --arm patched=$PATCHED/build --out connect.json

  Each prints one Markdown table row per benchmark or metric:
  "| name | base median [min-max] n=7 | patched median [min-max] n=7 |
  patched/base |" (ns per transaction/outpoint for the microbenchmarks,
  ms for block connection); --out keeps every raw sample, and run's
  stderr shows each round and the page-cache residency before the blocks.

Evidence (shared machine: 18 cores, load average 40-90 from other agents'
builds throughout; one base build):
- The microbenchmarks run; base numbers for scale: BlockMerkleRoot 66-79
  ns/tx; DeserializeBlock 223-258 ns/tx, of which HashBlockTxIds 136-144
  ns/tx; CoinsPrefetchWalk 0.49-0.63 us/outpoint (warm).
- ab_block_connect.py fixture: 2,000,000 coins, 159 MB chainstate, built
  in 15 s. Base, cold: 6 blocks connect in 2.4-5.9 s (400-1000 ms per
  20,000-input block, i.e. 20-50 us per input, varying with the machine's
  disk load); mincore shows 0% of mdbx.dat resident before every block.
  Warm (--warm): 552-653 ms for the 6 blocks, 100% resident.
- Two A/B arms of the same binary differ by up to ~8% in medians on this
  machine (e.g. DeserializeBlock base vs a build that does not change
  it: 0.99-1.09), which is the noise floor for these tables.

Not tested: the Linux eviction path (written, not run); P2P block and
compact block arrival (the driver submits by RPC); any quiet-machine run.

records.subject: validation: prefetch an arriving block's coins in the background
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
validation: prefetch an arriving block's coins in the background

ConnectBlock prefetches the coins a block spends (patch 039's
PrefetchOutpointsAsync), but despite its name the prefetch runs on the
validating thread, inside ConnectBlock, as a sorted cursor walk: each seek
faults in its B-tree pages one at a time. On a cold page cache that walk is
most of ConnectBlock (here 20-50 us per input, ~400-1000 ms for a
20,000-input block), and it only starts after the Merkle check, CheckBlock
and writing the block to disk are done.

Now, when a full block arrives, its coins are read on background threads:

- node::BlockPrefetcher (node/blockprefetch.{h,cpp}): collects the block's
  spent outpoints, leaving out spends of transactions in the same block,
  turns them into sorted, unique coin keys, and walks them in up to
  -blockprefetch stripes (default 4 threads, stripes of at least 256 keys)
  so that several reads are outstanding at once. Bounded: at most 2 blocks
  in flight; a further block is dropped, not queued; each block is started
  once (the last 8 hashes are remembered); blocks with fewer than 9
  transactions are skipped, as in ConnectBlock. Threads start at the first
  large block. -blockprefetch=0 disables it (debug option, 0-16).
- Started from net_processing as soon as a block is deserialized (BLOCK,
  before IsBlockMutated, for blocks we requested or whose header claims
  the anti-DoS work), after a BLOCKTXN reconstruction, and after an
  optimistic compact-block reconstruction; and from ProcessNewBlock's entry
  (RPC submitblock, -loadblock/reindex), deduplicated. ChainstateManager::
  PrefetchBlockCoins also requires the header's proof of work to be valid,
  so a peer cannot make the node read the disk for free.
- The workers never take cs_main. The caller, which holds cs_main briefly
  anyway at each of these points, passes a DBBackgroundHandle of the
  active coins database. The handle (dbwrapper.h) runs a function only
  while the database is open; ~CDBWrapper first detaches it, then waits for
  running uses, so a cache resize (which reopens the database), snapshot
  activation or shutdown can never close the environment under a walk.
  CDBWrapper::PrefetchSortedRawKeys is the existing walk, split out of
  PrefetchRawKeys; it takes its own read transaction and cursor from the
  mutex-guarded pools, and the environment is opened with
  MDBX_NOSTICKYTHREADS, so a read transaction may run on a thread other
  than the one that created it, concurrently with the writer (MDBX readers
  see a snapshot). The workers only read, and only to warm the OS page
  cache: validation reads every coin itself, so results cannot change.
  Errors are caught and counted.
- ConnectBlock's own prefetch is unchanged and remains the fallback; it is
  cheap once the pages are resident.
- Metrics (in the fullnode_ namespace the metrics are moving to):
  fullnode_block_prefetch_started_total, _dropped_total, _outpoints_total,
  _errors_total and the fullnode_block_prefetch_duration_seconds histogram
  (arrival to end of prefetch). -debug=bench logs each prefetch.

Mempool admission path: not changed, decided by the A/B below. The
patched-1thread arm (background prefetch with one thread, i.e. moving the
same single walk off-thread and starting it early) is no faster than base
(1.00x ConnectBlock total); the gain comes from several walks outstanding
at once. Admission needs each input right away, its prefetch batches are
small (>= 8 cold inputs), and the warm walk costs 0.5-0.6 us per outpoint
(CoinsPrefetchWalk), so moving that walk to another thread has nothing to
overlap with; striping a large cold admission batch is possible future
work.

A/B (contrib/bench/block-validation/ab_block_connect.py; base = the tier
plus the benchmark commit; same fixture: 2,000,000 coins, 6 blocks of
10,000 two-input transactions spending random coins; -dbcache=4;
mdbx.dat evicted before each block, 0% resident by mincore; 7 interleaved
rounds; ms; median [min-max]):

| metric | base | patched | patched -blockprefetch=0 | patched -blockprefetch=1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ConnectBlock, 6 blocks | 4483 [3883-5880] | 1665 [935-2426] (0.37x) | 4823 [2540-10710] (1.08x) | 4493 [2272-6012] (1.00x) |
| ConnectBlock, median block | 798 [657-1004] | 282 [159-434] (0.35x) | 820 [395-1771] (1.03x) | 681 [369-897] (0.85x) |
| submitblock, 6 blocks | 4858 [4251-6409] | 1998 [1168-2817] (0.41x) | 5203 [2820-11221] (1.07x) | 4919 [2508-6265] (1.01x) |

Warm page cache (--warm, same rounds and arms but the 1-thread one):

| metric | base | patched | patched -blockprefetch=0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ConnectBlock, 6 blocks | 630 [553-653] | 636 [592-813] (1.01x) | 622 [553-915] (0.99x) |
| submitblock, 6 blocks | 957 [851-999] | 1011 [939-1209] (1.06x) | 955 [876-1255] (1.00x) |

So: cold, ConnectBlock takes ~0.37x the time; warm, the background walk
(about 12 ms of CPU for 20,000 keys, on 4 threads) costs up to ~5% of

records.subject: validation: compute large blocks' Merkle roots on several threads
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
validation: compute large blocks' Merkle roots on several threads

A received block's Merkle root (CheckMerkleRoot, run by IsBlockMutated on
arrival and by CheckBlock) is one thread hashing n - 1 nodes with
SHA256D64: 66-79 ns per transaction here, ~8 ms for a 100,000-transaction
block, on the path between receiving a block and relaying/connecting it.

- consensus/merkle: ComputeMerkleRootChunked computes the tree as
  independent subtrees of a power-of-two number of leaves, handed to a
  caller-supplied task runner (consensus code owns no threads), then
  combines their roots with ComputeMerkleRoot. The result is bit-identical,
  mutation flag included: full subtrees are exactly the corresponding part
  of the tree, and pairs (2i, 2i+1) never straddle subtrees, so the
  CVE-2012-2459 check sees the same pairs. The last, partial subtree stops
  where ComputeMerkleRoot's level reaches one node; in the whole tree that
  node is the odd last node of each remaining level up to the subtree's
  height, so it is hashed with itself once per missing level (no pair, so
  no mutation check, as in the original). BlockMerkleRootParallel reads
  the leaves (transaction ids) inside the tasks. BlockMerkleRoot and
  ComputeMerkleRoot are unchanged.
- validation: CheckMerkleRoot uses ValidationBlockMerkleRoot: BlockMerkleRoot
  below PARALLEL_MERKLE_MIN_TXS (2,500) transactions; above, 4 threads, and
  8 from 10,000 transactions, two subtrees per thread handed out by an
  atomic counter. The threads are the existing ParallelScriptWorkerPool
  (ConnectBlock's and mempool batches' script workers), no new pool. It
  gains TryRun: if another caller is using the pool (e.g. ConnectBlock's
  scripts), the Merkle work runs on the calling thread as before rather
  than waiting. RunOnValidationWorkers exposes this for other users.

Cutoff, measured (bench_bitcoin MerkleRootThreads_<n>_t<threads>, which
forces the threaded path; t1 is the sequential BlockMerkleRoot; 5-7
rounds; ns per transaction, median [min-max]):

| txs | t1 (sequential) | t2 | t4 | t8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 73.4 [69.9-84.2] | 89.4 [73.1-107.6] | 89.8 [79.0-98.4] | 85.8 [52.3-150.1] |
| 2,500 | 102.3 [75.7-143.7] | - | 39.9 [35.2-55.8] | 64.4 [44.2-86.2] |
| 5,000 | 69.1 [67.3-72.7]* | 54.8 [45.5-67.7] | 33.5 [32.4-52.7] | 34.0 [22.0-67.6] |
| 10,000 | 72.3 [67.5-80.1]* | 47.5 [41.5-56.4] | 34.1 [29.1-34.6] | 22.3 [19.0-23.3] |
| 50,000 | 79.4 [72.2-82.7]* | 47.9 [46.5-50.6] | 25.4 [23.1-27.4] | 16.8 [15.4-19.9] |
| 100,000 | 79.3 [75.9-82.7]* | 49.7 [48.0-50.7] | 27.4 [24.4-28.4] | 14.7 [14.5-16.0] |
(* BlockMerkleRoot_<n> in the same run.) Threading loses at 1,000
transactions (waking workers costs more than ~70 us of hashing) and wins
at 2,500 even worst case against best case; 8 threads only pay off from
about 10,000.

A/B of validation's Merkle check (CheckBlockMerkleRoot_<n>; base = the tier
plus the benchmark commit only, patched = this commit; 7
interleaved rounds; ns per transaction):

| txs | base | patched | patched/base |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 69.0 [65.5-78.9] | 73.9 [65.7-79.8] | 1.07 (same code; noise) |
| 5,000 | 70.8 [65.2-72.5] | 43.4 [35.0-54.7] | 0.61 |
| 10,000 | 76.4 [68.8-79.9] | 23.7 [17.8-28.9] | 0.31 |
| 50,000 | 79.2 [69.8-85.6] | 18.7 [16.8-22.0] | 0.24 |
| 100,000 | 77.7 [74.3-84.3] | 17.5 [16.6-20.5] | 0.23 |

i.e. 7.8 ms -> 1.8 ms for a 100,000-transaction block. With the previous
commit, cold block connection (ab_block_connect.py, 5 rounds, base vs
both commits): ConnectBlock total 3174 [2402-3442] -> 1193 [1072-1419] ms
(0.38x), submitblock total 3512 -> 1456 ms (0.41x); the Merkle part of a
10,000-transaction block is ~0.5 ms of that, inside the noise.

Transaction ids during deserialization (not changed): each transaction is
hashed for its id as it is laid out (CTransaction::Place ->
HashSerialization), one at a time, while the block is read off the wire.
Hashing is ~60% of deserialization (HashBlockTxIds 136-144 vs
DeserializeBlock 223-258 ns/tx), i.e. ~14 ms of ~26 ms for a
100,000-transaction block; four threads could save ~10 ms there. Deferring
does not help: the ids are needed immediately for the Merkle check.
Parallelizing needs a block-level deserializer that first scans every
transaction's wire bounds (ScanTransactionWire is already separate) and
then builds the transactions on worker threads (the storage allocator is
a concurrent slab allocator, so that part is safe), plus a way for the
primitives library to reach a thread pool it cannot depend on. That is a
restructuring of the serialization path rather than a small change, so it
is reported here and left for a separate patch.

How to reproduce:
  Build base (the benchmark commit) and patched (this commit), target
  bitcoin-bench, then:
  contrib/bench/block-validation/ab_microbench.py \
      --arm base=$BASE/build --arm patched=$PATCHED/build \
      --filter 'CheckBlockMerkleRoot_.*' --rounds 7 --min-time 300
  contrib/bench/block-validation/ab_microbench.py \
      --arm patched=$PATCHED/build \
      --filter '(BlockMerkleRoot|MerkleRootThreads)_.*' --rounds 5 \
      --min-time 300
  Output: one Markdown row per benchmark, "median [min-max] n=<rounds>"
  in ns per transaction, plus the patched/base ratio.

Tests (merkle_tests): ComputeMerkleRootChunked equals ComputeMerkleRoot,
root and mutation flag, for every leaf count 0-300 with every chunk size
1-64 (tasks run in reverse order), and for 1023-12345 leaves with chunks
of 128-2048 on real threads; mutation: the last 1/2/4/8 leaves repeated
(CVE-2012-2459 shape) and identical adjacent pairs at many positions, for
2-160 leaves and chunk sizes 1-32, plus the explicit [1..6] vs
[1..6,5,6] example at every chunk size (same root, only the second
flagged); BlockMerkleRootParallel and ValidationBlockMerkleRoot (forced
onto the worker pool at 1-8 threads) equal BlockMerkleRoot for 1-3333
transactions, including a duplicated last transaction. Pass:
merkle_tests, validation_block_tests, blockcheck_tests, validation_tests,
p2p_invalid_block.py, p2p_compactblocks.py, interface_http_metrics.py.

Not tested: the full unit and functional suites (one sweep at the end of
the series); contention with a concurrent ConnectBlock in a live node
(TryRun's fallback is exercised only by construction); Linux or x86
SHA256D64 implementations' relative costs, which may move the cutoff; a
quiet machine (load average 40-90 throughout).

records.message:
bench: signed-transaction flood and A/B driver for mempool admission

Why: mempool admission is a candidate throughput ceiling for a high-TPS
node, and changing it (parallel script checks, an admission thread) needs
numbers from realistic load before and after. MiniWallet's anyone-can-spend

  regtest fixture: confirmed P2PKH outputs and a flood of signed P2PKH
  spends (35% ECDSA, 35% Schnorr, 15% 2-5 input mixed, 15% dependent
  chains of 2-8), signed in worker processes.
- flood.py runs one flood against a fresh clone of the fixture from N raw
  P2P peers (one process each) or N RPC sendrawtransaction clients, with a
  ZMQ `sequence` subscriber (libzmq through ctypes) timestamping every
  mempool add. It reports accepted tx/s, sender-to-mempool latency
  percentiles, node CPU, load average and the node's mempool metrics, and
  can run macOS `sample` on the node at a chosen mempool size.
- ab.py runs configurations interleaved over rounds (rotating the first
  configuration each round), resumes, and prints medians with min-max.
- sample_summary.py reduces a `sample` call tree to inclusive/self shares
  and direct callers for one thread.
- src/bench/mempool_admission.cpp: MempoolAdmissionSignedSerial admits
  2000 never-seen signed transactions per iteration (cold signature
  cache), in process, without networking.
- src/test/util/admission.{h,cpp}: helpers that fund a P2PKH wallet from a
  TestChain100Setup coinbase and build ECDSA/Schnorr-signed spends and
  children, shared by the benchmark and the admission tests that follow.

arm64 with 18 logical CPUs at load average 55-75 from other builds):

  thread profile while the mempool grew from 150k: 75% in
  MempoolOverlayLayer::AddTransactionBatch (26% memmove in
  TxOverlayArena::InsertBatchParallel), 9% script verification,
  7% SendMessages. Early in the flood (mempool below 30k): 30% script
  verification, 22% overlay publication, 25% SendMessages.
- Accepted rate falls from about 4k tx/s at the start to about 1k tx/s
  at 190k mempool entries; 2.0-2.6k tx/s over the whole run.
- MempoolAdmissionSignedSerial: about 41 us per transaction.

records.subject: mempool: grow Merklix overlay arenas geometrically, not per batch
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
mempool: grow Merklix overlay arenas geometrically, not per batch

Why: the admission profile in the previous commit put 75% of the message
handler thread in MempoolOverlayLayer::AddTransactionBatch once the mempool
held 150k transactions, and script verification at 9%. Admission
publishes the overlay after every coalesced burst of peer transactions, so
this, not signature checking, was the throughput ceiling for large
mempools: the accepted rate fell from about 4k tx/s to about 1k tx/s as
the pool grew.

The cause is two reserve calls that ask for exactly the next batch:
- TxOverlayArena::InsertBatchParallel and UtxoOverlayArena::
  BatchUpdateParallel splice with
  nodes_.reserve(nodes_.size() + new_nodes). An exact reserve beyond
  capacity reallocates to exactly that size, so every batch copies the
  whole persistent arena (memmove was 26% of the thread).
- AddTransactionBatch calls created_coins_.reserve(size + 2k) and
  spent_outpoints_.reserve(size + 2k), which rehashes both maps (bucket
  arrays zeroed and refilled) on every batch.
Each is O(overlay size) per batch, so a stream of small batches is
quadratic.

What: reserve only when the container would actually grow, and then to at
least double its capacity (vectors) or size (unordered maps). Contents,
ordering of every exported list (they are sorted) and all roots are
unchanged; only allocation timing differs.

Evidence:
- New unit test batched_inserts_match_serial_inserts_while_growing: 3000
  transactions (half spending outputs of earlier ones, inside and across
  batches) added one by one and in random batches of 17-80 give equal
  Subtree A roots, UTXO roots, counts, fees, sigchecks, costs and net
  erased/inserted sets, with and without the state root in the header.
  mempool_overlay_tests pass.
- bitcoin-bench (shared host, load average about 70):
    MempoolOverlayAddBatch64To100k  4,175,146 ns/tx before, 5,275 after
    MempoolOverlayAddBatch64To10k     162,015 ns/tx before, 5,358 after
- 200k signed-transaction flood, 8 peers: node CPU for the whole flood
  64.5 s before, 26.9 s after; overlay share of the message handler at
  150k mempool entries 75% before, 4.9% after; script verification is
  now the largest item (33%). Interleaved A/B rounds are in the README of
  the admission series.

How to reproduce:
    ninja -C build bitcoind bitcoin-bench test_bitcoin
    build/src/bench/bitcoin-bench -filter='MempoolOverlayAddBatch.*'
    build/src/test/test_bitcoin --run_test=mempool_overlay_tests
    contrib/bench/mempool-admission/flood.py --bitcoind build/src/bitcoind \
        --fixture FX --workdir RUN --peers 8 \
        --sample-seconds 8 --sample-at-size 150000
bitcoin-bench prints nanobench rows in ns/tx; flood.py prints JSON with
node_cpu_s and tps_10_90.

Not addressed: the persistent arena still never compacts, so its memory
grows with every path copy until the next reset; that is unchanged.

records.subject: validation, net: split admission into reusable phases (no behavior change)
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
validation, net: split admission into reusable phases (no behavior change)

Why: to verify scripts for many transactions outside cs_main and then
admit them, admission needs (a) a way to hand it script results computed
elsewhere without trusting them blindly, and (b) the peer-side handling
of a received transaction split at the admission call, so the verdict can
be handled later on the message thread. This commit adds both and uses
neither yet; every existing caller passes nothing and runs exactly the
previous code.

What:
- PrecomputedAdmissionChecks / ScriptCheckOutcome (validation.h): the
  context-free CheckRegularTransaction result and, per flag set (standard,
  consensus), whether the input scripts passed, the reported failure
  (result, reason, debug message) and the sigcheck count, together with
  the spent outputs they were computed against and the txid.
- ComputeAdmissionChecks: fills that without any lock. It runs the same
  CScriptCheck sequence as CheckInputScripts (factored into
  VerifyTxScriptsAgainst, which VerifyTxScriptsFromResolvedCoins now
  wraps), including the mandatory-flags recheck that tells
  TX_NOT_STANDARD from TX_CONSENSUS, and stores signatures in the
  signature cache as admission does. Consensus flags run only after the
  standard flags pass, as in admission.
- AcceptToMemoryPool(..., precomputed): PreChecks and
  ConsensusScriptChecks call CheckInputScriptsReusing, which reuses an
  outcome only if the txid matches, the flags are equal and every spent
  output (amount and script) equals what admission resolved itself under
  the locks; otherwise it calls CheckInputScripts. It consults and
  updates the script execution cache exactly as CheckInputScripts does
  (erase on the policy lookup, insert after consensus success), so the
  cache, verdict and sigcheck count do not depend on which path ran.
  Script validity is a function of (transaction, spent outputs, flags)
  only, so a matching outcome cannot change a verdict.
- GetMempoolScriptFlags exposes the next-block flags admission uses.
- PeerManagerImpl::ProcessSingleTx is now PrepareTxAdmission (request
  bookkeeping and the already-have branch) + ProcessTransaction +
  FinishTxAdmission (relay, orphans, reject filters, conflicting pool,
  1p1c reconsideration, misbehavior). Same statements, same order, same
  locks.

Evidence: new mempool_admission_tests (precomputed and ordinary verdicts
identical for valid ECDSA and Schnorr spends and for a bad signature; a
matching outcome is what admission reports; outcomes with a different
amount, script, flags or txid are ignored; a missing input still fails as
an orphan). mempool_tests, txvalidation_tests, txvalidationcache_tests,
txpackage_tests, orphanage_tests, denialofservice_tests,
mempool_overlay_tests pass. Functional p2p_invalid_tx, p2p_orphan_handling,
p2p_opportunistic_1p1c, p2p_1p1c_network, mempool_accept pass.

How to reproduce:
    ninja -C build test_bitcoin
    build/src/test/test_bitcoin --run_test=mempool_admission_tests

records.subject: validation: staged mempool admission with scripts verified outside cs_main
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
validation: staged mempool admission with scripts verified outside cs_main

Why: admission verifies input scripts while holding cs_main and the
mempool lock, so it uses one core and blocks everything else that needs
cs_main for the whole signature check. Script validity depends only on the
transaction, the outputs it spends and the verification flags, so it can
be computed without the locks for many transactions at once, provided the
locked commit checks that what it relied on still holds.

What: AcceptToMemoryPoolStaged(chainman, txs, options, stats):
  A. cs_main + mempool lock: look up the outputs each transaction spends
     (an earlier transaction of this call, the mempool, or the UTXO set),
     recording coins this pulled into the coins cache. Coinbases,
     transactions already in the mempool, non-standard ones, and
     transactions that cannot be resolved or that double-spend the
     mempool or an earlier transaction of the call skip phase B (their
     verdict comes from phase C without script work spent on them).
  B. No locks: ComputeAdmissionChecks for the rest on
     options.script_threads threads of the existing script worker pool
     (the one parallel rawtxbatch validation uses; the caller is one of
     the threads).
  C. cs_main: for each transaction in order, the ordinary
     ChainstateManager::ProcessTransaction with its precomputed checks,
     inside one deferred mempool-snapshot publication; then evict the
     coins phase A cached for transactions that were not admitted.
Because phase C is the serial admission code under the locks and reuses
a script outcome only for identical flags and spent outputs (previous
commit), its verdicts, reject reasons, mempool changes, overlay updates
and notifications are those of serial admission in this order at commit
time. A block connected, a reorg, or any mempool change between A and C,
including our own earlier commits, is handled by phase C itself: spent
inputs fail as missing, changed flags or outputs re-run the scripts.
options.skip_at_commit lets a caller re-apply its own pre-checks (e.g.
"already have") under cs_main at the commit point; StagedAdmissionStats
reports the locked and unlocked phase times.

Evidence:
- mempool_admission_tests:
  * staged_admission_matches_serial_admission (differential): shuffled
    scenarios of 120 inputs' worth of valid ECDSA/Schnorr/multi-input
    spends, dependent chains (some child-first), double spends, bad
    signatures and their children, orphans, duplicates, zero-fee, dust and
    non-final transactions; serial vs staged with random batch splits
    (1-16 and 1-120) at 1, 4 and 8 threads: identical result type,
    TxValidationResult, reject reason, debug message, vsize, fees and
    effective feerate for every transaction, and identical final mempool.
  * staged_double_spend_race_first_in_order_wins: in one batch the first
    spend wins and the second gets txn-mempool-conflict
    (TX_AVALANCHE_RECONSIDERABLE) without being verified; two racing
    callers: exactly one wins, 20 rounds.
  * staged_chain_in_one_batch_is_not_an_orphan: parent, child, grandchild
    and sibling in one batch are all admitted; child-before-parent is an
    orphan exactly as serially; a child of a parent failing its scripts in
    the same batch is an orphan.
  * staged_block_between_phases: a block connected while phase B runs
    spends one input (missing inputs), confirms one transaction
    (txn-already-known) and its in-batch child (admitted against the
    confirmed output); an unrelated transaction is admitted.
  * staged_skip_at_commit; staged_concurrent_callers_and_blocks (three
    threads admitting overlapping batches with double spends while blocks
    connect; mempool check() passes, never both sides of a double spend).
  All pass, and pass under ThreadSanitizer (Debug, -DENABLE_SANITIZERS=
  thread, 0 reports). mempool_tests, txvalidation_tests,
  txvalidationcache_tests, txpackage_tests, orphanage_tests pass.
- bitcoin-bench, 2000 never-seen signed transactions per iteration,
  -checkmempool=0, shared host (load average 30-60, 18 logical CPUs):
    MempoolAdmissionSignedSerial     30.3 us/tx
    MempoolAdmissionSignedStaged1    28.9 us/tx
    MempoolAdmissionSignedStaged4    17.3 us/tx
    MempoolAdmissionSignedStaged8    15.2 us/tx
    MempoolAdmissionSignedStagedAll  16.4 us/tx
  The locked remainder (phase A plus serial admission without scripts:
  mempool insertion, notifications, coins-view construction, snapshot
  publication) is about 13 us/tx and bounds the speedup at about 2x
  in process; profiled in the README of this series.

How to reproduce:
    ninja -C build test_bitcoin bitcoin-bench
    build/src/test/test_bitcoin --run_test=mempool_admission_tests
    build/src/bench/bitcoin-bench -filter='MempoolAdmissionSigned.*'
    # ThreadSanitizer
    cmake -GNinja -B build-tsan -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
        -DENABLE_SANITIZERS=thread -DBUILD_CHRONIK=OFF
    ninja -C build-tsan test_bitcoin
    build-tsan/src/test/test_bitcoin --run_test=mempool_admission_tests
bitcoin-bench prints one nanobench row per benchmark (ns/tx, tx/s).

Not done here: nothing calls the staged path yet (next commit).

records.subject: net: admit peer transactions on an admission thread (-parallelmempool)
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
net: admit peer transactions on an admission thread (-parallelmempool)

Why: the message handler thread admitted every received transaction itself
while holding cs_main, so script verification for all peers ran on one
core and stalled every other message while it did. The previous commit
lets admission verify scripts outside the locks for a batch; this one
feeds it from the network without changing what a peer observes.

What:
- node::TxAdmissionQueue: per-peer FIFO queues drained round-robin (one
  transaction per peer per turn), bounded per peer (256, the size of the
  existing coalesced TX burst), in total (16384) and in bytes (64 MiB).
  Counts pushes, takes, drops and "full" events.
- PeerManagerImpl, with -parallelmempool (default 1):
  * The message thread handles a TX message as before up to the mempool
    call (PrepareTxAdmission: request bookkeeping, already-have, force
    relay, reconsiderable 1p1c), then queues the transaction with an
    AddRef'd CNode and its PeerRef. Directly following TX messages are
    read and queued in the same turn.
  * A "txadmit" thread takes batches of up to 256 and calls
    AcceptToMemoryPoolStaged with -parallelmempoolthreads script threads
    (0 = one per core, the default). "Already have" is re-checked under
    cs_main at each transaction's commit point, as serial handling checks
    it right before admitting. Transactions of a peer that is
    disconnecting are not admitted (like its unread messages).
  * Verdicts go back in commit order; the message thread handles them
    with the unchanged FinishTxAdmission (relay, orphans, reject filters,
    conflicting pool, 1p1c, misbehavior), so relay, orphan and DoS
    outcomes are those of serial handling in that order. A transaction
    already had at commit time is handled as a fresh TX message then.
  * Ordering: while a peer has transactions without verdicts, its next
    non-TX message is held (so e.g. a pong is sent after the verdicts of
    the transactions sent before the ping); a transaction whose earlier
    copy (from any peer) is still in admission is held until that copy's
    verdict, then handled like a serial node would handle the duplicate.
  * Backpressure: a transaction that does not fit is held and the peer is
    not read from until it fits; its messages stay in the receive buffer
    and TCP applies backpressure. Held work is bounded by one coalesced
    burst per peer.
  * StopTxAdmission() stops the thread and drops what it holds (releasing
    the CNode references) before CConnman::Stop(); it also runs from the
    destructor. After it, TX messages are handled serially.
- -parallelmempool=0 keeps the previous code path (serial admission on the
  message handler thread, unchanged) for A/B and as a safety valve.

Evidence:
- txadmission_queue_tests: round-robin with per-peer order, per-peer /
  total / byte bounds and full counting, drop, take-all, interrupt, and a
  four-producer one-consumer run (exactly-once, per-peer order).
- New functional test mempool_parallel_admission.py (node0 parallel with 4
  threads, node1 -parallelmempool=0): the same signed sequence (40
  independent, a 5-chain, child-before-parent, a double spend, zero fee,
  a duplicate) yields identical mempools; 20 parent+child pairs each
  followed by a ping are in the mempool when the pong arrives; 4 peers
  with 120 transactions, the same transaction from all of them and a
  two-peer double-spend race: every valid one admitted once, exactly one
  side of the race, no disconnects; an invalid signature disconnects its
  sender on both nodes; a block mined mid-flight leaves every transaction
  confirmed or in a mempool that regtest checks on every admission. The
  debug log shows node0 admitting on [txadmit] and node1 never.
- ThreadSanitizer + DEBUG_LOCKORDER (Debug, -DENABLE_SANITIZERS=thread):
  mempool_parallel_admission, p2p_invalid_tx, p2p_orphan_handling,
  p2p_opportunistic_1p1c and mempool_reorg against the TSan bitcoind:
  pass, no reports, no lock-order failures. txadmission_queue_tests and
  mempool_admission_tests under TSan: no reports.
- With parallel admission on (now the default in functional tests):
  p2p_invalid_tx, p2p_orphan_handling, p2p_opportunistic_1p1c,
  p2p_1p1c_network, p2p_leak_tx, p2p_feefilter, p2p_tx_privacy,
  p2p_compactblocks, mempool_accept, mempool_packages, mempool_limit,
  mempool_reorg, mempool_resurrect, mempool_spend_coinbase,
  mempool_unbroadcast, mempool_expiry, abc_mempool_chainedtx,
  rpc_packages, abc_p2p_avalanche_transaction_voting, chronik_ws,
  chronik_ws_ordering, chronik_mempool_conflicts, chronik_tx,
  chronik_tx_removal_order pass.
  abc_p2p_avalanche_transaction_finalization fails with "mempool full"
  in test_mempool_full; it fails identically on the unmodified base
  binary (RPC path, not affected here).
- 200k-transaction signed flood, 8 P2P peers, single runs (A/B tables in
  the series README): relaying peers 15.1k tx/s parallel vs 10.2k serial;
  non-relaying peers 24.1k vs 13.0k.

How to reproduce:
    ninja -C build bitcoind test_bitcoin
    build/src/test/test_bitcoin --run_test=txadmission_queue_tests
    test/functional/mempool_parallel_admission.py \
        --configfile=build/test/config.ini
    contrib/bench/mempool-admission/ab.py --bitcoind new=build/src/bitcoind \
        --config serial=new:-parallelmempool=0 \
        --config parallel=new:-parallelmempool=1 \
        --fixture FX --workdir AB --rounds 5 --peers 8

Not tested: interface_zmq.py (no python zmq module here; ZMQ "sequence"
notifications are exercised by every flood run instead), Linux, the full
functional suite. Known gap: during the few milliseconds a transaction
is in admission, an INV for it from another peer can still trigger a
GETDATA (AlreadyHaveTx does not know about in-flight transactions); the
duplicate is then held and handled as already-have.

util: seed each salted hasher from one random context

The admission profile attributed 6-17% of its serial commit phase to

not stand in for end-to-end admission measurements. Release benchmark
admission checks remain enabled, so rejected work cannot inflate a result.

records.subject: rpc: verify synchronous broadcast scripts outside the chain lock
records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
rpc: verify synchronous broadcast scripts outside the chain lock

Concurrent sendrawtransaction clients previously serialized script checks
under cs_main even when peer admission used unlocked verification.

For synchronous broadcasts with -parallelmempool enabled, resolve inputs
with the same deferred PreChecks used by staged peer admission, copy the
spent outputs, release the locks and verify scripts on the calling RPC
thread. Advisory cache entries are uncached before unlocking. The original
locked BroadcastTransaction critical section still checks chain/mempool

metrics: measure admission lock scopes and queue backpressure

independently against exact sends, mempool membership and ZMQ notifications.

records.message:
build: add nghttp3 and ngtcp2 to depends and an ENABLE_WEBTRANSPORT option

Why: P2P over WebTransport (HTTP/3 over QUIC; doc/p2p-webtransport.md,
added later in this series) needs a QUIC stack and an HTTP/3 layer. ngtcp2
1.25.0 with its OpenSSL backend (libngtcp2_crypto_ossl, built on OpenSSL's
QUIC TLS callbacks SSL_set_quic_tls_cbs, so OpenSSL >= 3.5) and nghttp3
1.18.0 are sans-I/O C libraries that fit the node's own event loops and
the OpenSSL already linked for TLS. This commit only makes them buildable
and findable; nothing uses them yet and the option is OFF by default.

What:
- depends/packages/nghttp3.mk (1.18.0, .tar.xz sha256 aad782c2...fef19)
  and ngtcp2.mk (1.25.0, sha256 2a34d248...b6fb), static, library-only.
  ngtcp2 depends on depends' openssl and fails its build step when
  libngtcp2_crypto_ossl was not produced (configure only warns when
  SSL_set_quic_tls_cbs is missing), so an OpenSSL 1.1.1 package cannot
  silently yield a library without the backend.
- depends/patches/nghttp3/0001-extra-settings.patch (132 lines, -p1):
  nghttp3_conn_set_extra_settings() to send up to 8 additional SETTINGS
  and a callback for unknown received SETTINGS. nghttp3 has no API for
  either and will not take WebTransport before it is an RFC; the
  WebTransport support codepoints are SETTINGS entries. Drop the patch
  once nghttp3 ships WebTransport.
- depends: webtransport_packages = nghttp3 ngtcp2, NO_WEBTRANSPORT=1 to
  skip them.
- cmake/modules/FindNghttp3.cmake, FindNgtcp2.cmake (components ngtcp2,
  crypto_ossl; versions from version.h). FindNghttp3 rejects an nghttp3
  without the patch (e.g. Homebrew's), so a stock library on the include
  path cannot be picked up by accident.
- ENABLE_WEBTRANSPORT (default OFF; config header define). When ON:
  OpenSSL >= 3.5 (the general minimum is 3.0), nghttp3 >= 1.18.0 and
  ngtcp2 >= 1.25.0 are required, their headers are searched first
  (include_directories BEFORE SYSTEM, as for OpenSSL: Homebrew links
  unpatched nghttp3/ngtcp2 headers into /opt/homebrew/include), and
  src/net_quic/version_check.cpp static_asserts the versions and the
  patched nghttp3 API.

Series position: after the OpenSSL 3.5 patches (OpenSSL lane,
additions-20261019h 0001-0003: depends OpenSSL 3.5.9, minimum 3.0 with
the found OpenSSL's headers searched first). That recipe configures
OpenSSL with no-quic; no-quic removes only OpenSSL's own QUIC stack, not
the third-party QUIC TLS API (SSL_set_quic_tls_cbs) that crypto_ossl
uses, so the recipe needs no change here (verified below). With an
OpenSSL 1.1.1 package ngtcp2's build step stops with
"libngtcp2_crypto_ossl was not built".

Measured / run:
- make -C depends nghttp3 (aarch64-apple-darwin25.6.0, native): builds,
  patch applies; the patched lib/ is identical to the prototype's.
- make -C depends ngtcp2 with the OpenSSL lane's openssl.mk (3.5.9,
  no-quic; byte-identical to the exported 0001 recipe): OpenSSL builds,
  ngtcp2's configure reports "libngtcp2_crypto_ossl: yes", libngtcp2.a
  and libngtcp2_crypto_ossl.a are staged.
- cmake -DENABLE_WEBTRANSPORT=ON against Homebrew OpenSSL 3.6.5 and
  ngtcp2/nghttp3 built with the recipes' options: configures (versions
  found) and bitcoind builds. OFF: configures, the config define is
  undefined, no ngtcp2/nghttp3 lookup.
- FindNghttp3 pointed at Homebrew's stock libnghttp3 1.18.0: rejected.
