records.message:
chronik: native V2 HAS_STATE outputs and state roots

The stack's "v2: expose HAS_STATE state roots in Chronik" (v2/087), with
the later !3 -> !7 coin guards, taught the Rust Chronik the HAS_STATE
output flag. The native Chronik was written before HAS_STATE and still
rejected flag bit 2, so it could not index the outputs stateful contracts
create, and it did not report their state roots. Port the Rust changes:

- ext/lotus_v2 types: Output::state_root and HasState(); flags other than
  token/burn/state are rejected (0xf8); the 32-byte root follows the token
  field on the wire; Validate rejects "burn state", "zero state root" and
  "stateless root field" in the Rust order; MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES 812 -> 844.
- Legacy-index script of a V2 output (AbcHost OutputScript): forward
  nFlags & 0x07 and append the node's stateRoot after the token id, byte
  for byte as BridgeTxOutputScript.
- Coin records and spent coins accept the state flag (flags & ~7), as
  decode_coin and SpentCoin::valid.
- Explorer output JSON: has_state and state_root.
- Protobuf TxOutput.state_root (field 7): the host fills the new
  TxOutput::state_root of a transaction's own outputs by decoding the
  indexed script like Rust v2_state_root / decode_v2_output_script (frame
  or 0x6a || frame); MakeTxProto forwards it. Empty on eCash nodes.

The read-budget estimates that use 812 bytes per output are unchanged, as
in Rust. Tests: the Rust codec cases (state_root_outputs, flags 8,
zero state root, 845-byte bound) in types_tests, and explorer records of
stateless and stateful outputs in v2_explorer_http_tests.

records.message:
mining(v2): select the coinbase version, legacy coinbases on regtest only

A coinbase is either a V2 coinbase (version 7), which commits to the
parent block and height in its input, or a legacy coinbase (version 1
or 2) with a null prevout and the BIP34 height in its scriptSig. The
inherited test suite mines coinbases and spends them with legacy
transactions, so it needs legacy coinbases; the legacy bridge then
needs a source of legacy coins.

Consensus: the coinbase version selects the rule. Version 7 uses
CheckCoinbaseContext; version 1 or 2 uses the BIP34 rule and is valid
only where the new Consensus::Params::allowLegacyCoinbase is set
(regtest). Any other coinbase version is bad-cb-version. Previously the
rule was chosen by the input's nFlags, so a version 7 coinbase without
the V2 coinbase input could use the BIP34 branch.

Selection:
- BlockAssembler::Options::coinbase_version (1, 2 or 7, default 7);
  CreateNewBlock refuses a legacy version where it is not allowed.
- CreateCoinbaseShell/PadCoinbaseToMinSize build the coinbase input for
  BlockAssembler, the getblocktemplate fast path and the test utility,
  so each form writes only its own fields.
- -coinbaseversion=<1|2|7> sets the node's default; init fails for other
  values, and for 1 or 2 off regtest.
- generatetoaddress, generatetodescriptor and generateblock take a
  coinbase_version argument, and getblocktemplate a "coinbase_version"
  request key (RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER for other values or for a legacy
  version off regtest). The cached template is rebuilt when its
  coinbase version differs from the request.
- The share-pool coordinator keeps building V2 coinbases.
- TestChain100Setup mines legacy (version 2) coinbases by default,
  m_coinbase_version selects another; createCoinbaseAndMerkleRoot keeps
  the version of the coinbase it is given.
- The functional framework writes coinbaseversion=2 into the [regtest]
  section of each node's config file, so that a test starting a node on
  another chain is unaffected and -coinbaseversion=7 on the command line
  takes precedence.

Tests:
- miner_tests: coinbase_outputs_survive_wire_round_trip runs for
  versions 2 and 7; coinbase_version_selects_coinbase_form checks the
  form of versions 1, 2 and 7 and that the blocks connect;
  legacy_coinbase_rejected_off_regtest checks bad-cb-version on testnet
  for versions 1 and 2, and that the assembler refuses to build one;
  version 3 is rejected by the transaction version rule.

records.message:
primitives(v2): version-tagged transactions without hybrid fields

A transaction is either legacy (version 1 or 2: legacy inputs and outputs
in the eCash grammar, named by SHA256d) or V2 (version 7: V2 inputs and V2
outputs in the v7 grammar). Any other version has no serialization and does
not decode (bad-txns-version). The wrapped 0x80000007/0xC0000007 forms, the
version XOR of legacy identities, the flat fallback identity and
HasStructuralV2Identity are deleted; a version 7 transaction without a
structural identity does not construct (bad-txns-v2-identity).

The CTxIn/CTxOut fields are kept (Chronik reads them); the invariant is
enforced where a transaction gets its bytes, so a mixed transaction cannot
exist. A version 7 output with branches and a scriptPubKey other than its V2
encoding is refused. CMutableTransaction defaults to version 2.

- ToV2Output is lossless: a legacy output maps to legacy_script, so the V2
  state records legacy coins with the 0x80 EncodeCoin record. The implicit
  V0-leaf mapping of legacy scripts is gone; primitives/v2_outputs.h builds
  explicit V2 outputs (V0LeafOutput, OpTrueOutput) and matches coinbase
  payees (CoinbaseOutputPaysScript), used by the miner fund, staking
  rewards and treasury rules.
- TxOutCompression stores a V2 output by its fields (V2 tag) and reads it
  back with its V2 encoding as scriptPubKey; a legacy output by its script.
- The 256-input/256-output caps apply to every version;
  bad-txns-legacy-state-output is deleted (unrepresentable).
- Token extraction and the 45-byte OP_TRUE script path no longer parse
  legacy scriptPubKeys as V2 outputs.
- Coinbase script data: node::GetCoinbaseScript/SetCoinbaseScript use
  vCoinbaseData for version 7 and scriptSig for legacy coinbases.

Genesis (T1-08 folded in): the easter-egg transaction becomes version 1
with its legacy input and output (TxId == TxHash == SHA256d), and the
coinbase pays an explicit V0-leaf output. TxIds and merkle roots are
unchanged, but the serialized size committed in the header changes, so:
- mainnet re-mined: nonce 223676906, hash 00000000dab29e7c...523d0d;
- testnet re-mined: nonce 259010196, hash 00000000847b5740...563873;
- regtest: nonce 4 still meets the target, hash 5297d8c9...3feb7605
  (was 720da0e6...50723e4); checkpoint, checkpoints_tests, blocktools.py
  and p2p_headers_sync_with_minchainwork.py follow.
The nonces were found by a 16-thread search from 0 over
CBlockHeader::GetHash() under each network's chain id against nBits
0x1d00ffff, in a temporary unit test that is not committed.

Tests:
- transaction_tests: raw versions 0/3/wrapped do not decode; v1/v2 round
  trip with SHA256d ids; mixed transactions do not serialize.
- Fixtures that spent V2 outputs now take them from a V2 coinbase
  (TestChain100Setup::MineV2Coinbase); inherited vectors with random
  versions draw version 1 or 2 (sighash_tests reads sighash.json field by
  field so upstream expected hashes are kept); txpackage_tests and
  rpc_decodescript return to upstream SHA256d txids.
- t1_baseline_tests: the regtest genesis golden moves as described above.
- Python: legacy grammar for versions 1/2, SHA256d legacy ids;
  pad_tx stays within 256 outputs by using large OP_RETURN outputs when
  standard ones cannot reach the size; feature_tx_version expects decode
  failures for bad versions; feature_v2_fallback_identity expects

records.message:
coins(v2): record whether a coin was created by a legacy transaction

Coin::IsLegacy() says whether a legacy (version 1 or 2) transaction created
the coin. The bit is the coin's output representation: a legacy transaction
creates legacy CTxOuts, a version 7 transaction V2 outputs, and every store

records.validation_status: Final native filetree exact actual81; focused fail/fix union71cases+3helpers+5standardfunctionals PASS with explicit per-attempt provenance. No all-prefix/fullsuite claim. Shared boundary unchanged.
records.message:
consensus(v2): let v7 spend legacy P2PKH coins with a V2 signature

A version 7 input (nFlags 1) may spend a coin created by a legacy
transaction when the coin is exactly P2PKH (rules A5/A6, design §2.3):

- Shape (CheckTxInputs): path index 0, one witness without siblings, an
  empty script and arguments [sig, 33-byte compressed pubkey]; else
  bad-txns-v2-legacy-coin-witness. Uncompressed keys are refused (Q3).
  Another legacy script gives bad-txns-v2-legacy-coin-template.
- Key hash (CheckTxInputs): HASH160(pubkey) must be the coin's key hash,
  else bad-txns-v2-legacy-p2pkh.
- Signature (CScriptCheck::CheckLegacyBridgeInput): a V2 BIP340 signature
  (64 bytes, or 65 with mode byte 1 or 2) by the pubkey's x-only key over
  the V2 signing message of invocation (input, witness 0), verified through
  the block's batch collector like any V2 signature.

Signing message for legacy coins (§2.5):
- A coin's wire is EncodeCoinOutput: EncodeOutput for a V2 coin, and
  LegacyCoinWire = 0x80 || value || CompactSize(|script|) || script for a
  legacy coin, the bytes EncodeCoin already records in the state (which
  now uses the same function). The coins root, the own-input hash, the
  coin field sizes and coin introspection (0xdc) use it. EncodeOutput
  still refuses legacy outputs as transaction outputs.
- The selector leaf is LegacyBridgeLeaf = TaggedHash(Branch, 0x03 ||
  CS(coin script) || CS(witness script)), with branch index 0, so a bridge
  signature never verifies for a native V2 spend or another coin.
- The all-OP_TRUE and pure-mode-0 preparation shortcuts are not taken for
  legacy coins.

Tests (v2_legacy_bridge_tests): modes 0/1/2 valid in a block and in the
mempool, the spent coin removed and the new coin V2; the coin stays
spendable by a legacy transaction; wrong key hash; another key's
signature, mislabelled modes, mode bytes 0/3 and a signature for another
transaction fail; every bad witness shape; an uncompressed key; P2PK, OP_TRUE,
bare multisig and P2PKH-plus-opcode coins are not templates; bridge and
native signatures by one key do not swap; three bridge inputs batch in one
block and any one bad signature invalidates it.

records.message:
consensus(v2): let v7 spend legacy P2SH coins on the legacy interpreter

A version 7 input may spend a legacy P2SH coin (rule A7, design §2.4). The
witness is one witness without siblings on path 0 whose script is the
redeem script and whose arguments are the pushes that precede it in a
legacy scriptSig.

- CheckTxInputs: the coin's script is P2SH (a9 14 <20> 87) or P2PKH, else
  bad-txns-v2-legacy-coin-template; HASH160(redeem script) must be the
  coin's script hash, else bad-txns-v2-legacy-p2sh-hash.
- CScriptCheck: the unchanged legacy VerifyScript runs the coin's script
  with scriptSig' = minimal pushes of the arguments and of the redeem
  script, under the flags a v1/v2 spend gets at the same height (Q4), and
  its sigchecks count toward the same limits. Legacy inputs and P2SH bridge
  inputs share one interpreter routine (RunLegacyScript); only the checker
  and the scriptSig differ. The coin comes from the resolved coins (block
  validation passes no spent output to v7 inputs).
- LegacyBridgeSignatureChecker (script/bridge_checker): CheckSig takes a
  legacy signature (ECDSA DER or 64-byte Schnorr, plus hashtype) over the
  V2 signing message of (input, witness 0) in the mode its hashtype
  selects: 0x41 mode 0, 0xC1 mode 1, 0xC3 mode 2 (Q5); scriptCode does
  not enter the message (the selector leaf commits to the redeem script).
  Verification goes through the input's caching checker, so the
  signature cache and the batch collector apply. CHECKDATASIG is
  unchanged. CheckLockTime compares against the V2 lock (value lock >> 8,
  height or time by its kind byte) and needs a non-final sequence;
  CheckSequence is BIP68 without the version gate.

Tests (v2_legacy_bridge_tests): 2-of-3 multisig with ECDSA and Schnorr in
each mapped hashtype, in a block and in the mempool; hashtypes 0x01, 0x42,
0x43, 0x81 and 0x40, another key, a legacy-sighash signature and a
relabelled mode fail; wrong redeem hash; a P2SH-plus-opcode coin is not a
template; for thirteen signature-free redeem scripts (OP_TRUE, OP_FALSE,
OP_RETURN, hash puzzles, CLEANSTACK, CHECKDATASIG valid/invalid/null,
sigchecks density, opcount, push size) the v2 legacy spend and the v7
bridge spend of the same coin give identical block and mempool verdicts;
CLTV and CSV against the V2 lock and the input sequence.

state(v2): decode the legacy coin wire in every coin codec

EncodeCoin writes a legacy coin as its LegacyCoinWire (T1-06), but only
the sparse-state decoder read it, with its own parser; the fast-sync

use it in all three decoders, bounding the coin frame by
MAX_COIN_OUTPUT_BYTES.
